assets.title: Grok return · verified intake and next steps
assets.text:
GROK RETURN — OCTOBER 9, 2026

RECEIPT
Five nested ZIP packages from two outer folders: 129 file occurrences including
two matching master indexes, reduced to 115 unique files (86 images, 23 documents,
6 Python helpers preserved as inert text). 40,944,166 bytes of unique content.
CRC, file size, SHA-256 and all image decodes passed. Provider scripts were not run.
See received/intake_receipt.json for every archive/member-to-file relationship.

BROWSE
Outfits now have one entry per existing outfit. The 17 gun variants live inside
those outfits beside the original angles. The source IDs and hashes determine
the parent outfit; no separate “yellow suit with gun” outfit was created.
Nine failed earlier gun attempts remain in Needs review. Exact byte duplicates,
including the saloon rollout/REV-HD-004 and carried-forward v001 media, share files.

Supporting cast includes Boss discovery / Round 1 and Caleb returned candidates.
Round 1 has ten boss proofs, three four-option tattoo sheets, six artwork
derivatives and two contact sheets. Select a boss before asking for four views,
a meeting scene or motion. This is not completion of all fifty discovery options.

Tattoo recovery includes the actual blaster source sheet and verified derivatives.
A clean source drawing and a body-placement crop have different roles. Eye/know/
chest originals remain missing; the large provider image index is an inventory,
not thousands of supplied images. Unconfirmed candidates stay in Needs review.

KNOWN LIMITS
These are technically verified candidates, not newly approved masters.
REV-HD-001 changes the vest/scene. CAL-P01 has tattoo-placement defects. Velvet’s
hip side fails the provider check. Several gun variants drift in mouth/jewelry/ink.
Boss 006 places its tattoo on the chest and has an additional unsourced neck mark;
Boss 009 matches artwork option B and its proposed missing arm is unclear.
Provider statements about earlier user approval remain attributed claims.
Hip stills measure 1280 x 720; the README's 1024 x 576 description is stale.
No video generation, lip-sync, timing alignment or Cloud run occurred in intake.

NEXT
Review from the existing outfit/cast/detail pages. Storyboard > Shot progress now
links received cash and boss candidates instead of requesting them from scratch.
Current review exports go to docs/notes/downloads; direct docs/notes/cfa-review.json
is also supported. Read-only review intake chooses the newest valid snapshot.

PROVENANCE
asset_ledger.json preserves canonical media IDs, source aliases, source IDs and
provider records; hd_audit.json and boss_audit.json preserve measured checks.
Incoming packs are moved to From Grok/Processed after verification. ZIP deletion
is recorded separately in cleanup_receipt.json; extracted canonical files remain.

COMPARE_TEMPLATE - one page, four columns: REF (upload image 1) | GROK BOT baseline | NANO BANANA | CHATGPT

# NOVA-IMG-BENCH-20261009 - Image benchmark plan (stills only)

Prepared 2026-10-09 by Grok Bot for Nova (teammate of Ziggy). **Every result in this kit is `needs_user_review`. Nothing is approved.** No outside-tool results are included; columns for tools A and B are empty until Nova runs them.

## 1. Goal
Ziggy is building music-video characters and animating them later (Google Flow / Veo, Gemini). Before committing to an image tool, he wants to know:

1. **Fidelity:** which tool best holds his locked characters - face identity, small text tattoos ("eye", "know", "AL", "G-A-I-B"), piercings, grills/teeth, and props on the correct side (character-left vs character-right).
2. **Refusals:** which tool refuses which characters. Background: Gemini refused to *animate* the jeweled slug-lord crime boss (image_25.png, probably because it read as a copy of a famous film crime lord), then also refused the gecko-frog redesign V09; a toned-down hippo music-label boss replaced it. Whether the *image* generators refuse these is unknown - that is what the PROBE tests measure.

## 2. Contenders (verified 2026-10-09 via official pages)
| Lane | Product | Where to use it | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | **Google Nano Banana** family (Gemini image models). Current names: **Nano Banana 2** (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image), **Nano Banana Pro** (Gemini 3 Pro Image), Nano Banana 2 Lite (Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite Image). | **Gemini app** (gemini.google.com -> Images / Create images; Nano Banana 2 is used when the Gemini model is Flash or Pro; Nano Banana Pro via "Redo with Pro" on paid Google AI plans). **Google AI Studio** (aistudio.google.com, pick Gemini 3 Pro Image / Nano Banana Pro). **Flow** (Nano Banana Pro for image creation on paid plans). | Lite is not designed for multiple reference images - do not use it. Record which model produced each image in `tool_version_or_mode`. Recommended: Nano Banana Pro (AI Studio or Gemini app Redo with Pro); if only Nano Banana 2 is available, use it consistently and log it. |
| **B** | **OpenAI ChatGPT Images 2.5** (released 2026-09-08). API models: gpt-image-2.5-flare, gpt-image-2.5-sunburst. | **ChatGPT** (chatgpt.com / desktop / mobile, all tiers) - upload refs and paste the prompt in a new chat. API is optional and not needed for this kit. | Log "ChatGPT Images 2.5 (ChatGPT app)" or the API model id in `tool_version_or_mode`. |
| **C** | **Grok Bot** in-house renders (baseline) | Already exist - copied into `BASELINES/`. No new generation. | Ziggy scores these; scores left blank. |
| (D, optional) | Midjourney | midjourney.com | Optional 4th lane only. Not built into this kit (no folders/rows). If Nova adds it, copy the A rows, use tool `D_MIDJOURNEY`, and note that its reference-image features work differently, so the same-refs rule may not apply exactly. |

Sources: support.google.com/gemini/answer/14286560 (Gemini Apps Help: Nano Banana models), blog.google "Where to use Nano Banana Pro", aistudio.google.com/models/nano-banana, openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-images-2-5. Product menus change often - if a menu name differs on the day, log what you actually used. No capability claims or scores are made here.

## 3. Rules (apply to every test, every tool)
1. **Same refs + same prompt to every tool.** Upload exactly the files listed on the prompt card, in the listed order, from `refs/<TEST-ID>/`. Paste the PROMPT block verbatim. Do not edit the prompt for one tool only. Files starting `CTX_` are context for scoring - never upload them.
2. **Fresh chat per test** (new conversation in Gemini/ChatGPT, new session in AI Studio/Flow). Don't carry characters between tests.
3. **Max 2 rerolls** (3 attempts total) per test per tool. A reroll = regenerate / resend the same prompt in a fresh chat. Save and log every attempt, not just the best one.
4. **Log every refusal verbatim.** Copy the exact refusal text into `refusal_text`, set `refused=Y`, and save a screenshot as `<TEST-ID>_<TOOL>_a<N>_REFUSAL.png`. A refusal counts as an attempt. Do not soften or rephrase the prompt to get past a refusal - that changes the test. (If you want to explore a softened version, log it as a separate row with `notes=SOFTENED` and the changed text.) Also log partial refusals, e.g. "made the image but removed the tattoos", in `notes`.
5. **No celebrity likeness.** All characters are original. Prompts say "NOT a celebrity". Don't add real names, film names or franchise names. Filenames were renamed to drop franchise words. (The old "Nelly-style" eyebrow wording was replaced with a plain description for the same reason.)
6. **Nothing is approved.** Every ledger row stays `status=needs_user_review`. Nova records; Ziggy decides.
7. **Don't fabricate.** If a tool wasn't run, leave the row empty. Don't fill scores for images you didn't see.
8. Keep download quality: use the tool's "download full size" option. Save as PNG if offered, otherwise keep the original format but use the same base name.

## 4. Test list (18 tests)
| # | Test ID | Subject | Uploads | Flag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | HD-01 | Hon Dolo (main) - pinstripe look | 5 | calibration |
| 2 | HD-02 | Hon Dolo (main) - saloon look | 5 | calibration |
| 3 | HD-03 | Hon Dolo (main) - yellow look | 6 | calibration |

## 5. Run order
1. **Calibration - HD-01, HD-02, HD-03** (Hon Dolo pinstripe, saloon, yellow) in both tools. Stop and look: are the uploads accepted, does the tool read "image 1/2/3" correctly, are sides being mirrored? Write any process issues in `notes`. Do not change the prompts - if something is broken in the kit, tell Ziggy before continuing.
2. **HD-04** (Hon Dolo cream).
3. **LAG-01** (Lisan Al Gaib signature look; natural white teeth, no grill).
4. **BOSS-001 ... BOSS-010** in order (round-1 boss candidates).
5. **Refusal probes last: PROBE-03 (hippo), PROBE-02 (gecko-frog V09), PROBE-01 (original slug-lord).** Run them last so a possible account warning can't block the fidelity tests. Expect refusals; that is data.

For each test, do tool A then tool B (or alternate the order per test to avoid bias - note it).

## 6. Naming and saving returned files
- Nano Banana: `RETURNS/A_NANOBANANA/<TEST-ID>_NANOBANANA_a<N>.png`
- ChatGPT: `RETURNS/B_CHATGPT/<TEST-ID>_CHATGPT_a<N>.png`
- `<N>` = attempt 1, 2 or 3. Example: `HD-01_CHATGPT_a2.png`.
- Refusal screenshots: `<TEST-ID>_<TOOL>_a<N>_REFUSAL.png` in the same folder.
- One row per attempt in `LEDGER.xlsx` (or `LEDGER.csv`). Attempt 1 rows are pre-filled; insert rows for attempts 2-3.
- Grok Bot baselines are already in `BASELINES/<TEST-ID>_GROKBOT.jpg` (some tests have a second `_GROKBOT_B.jpg`).

## 7. How to score
- Fill the score columns in `LEDGER.xlsx` using `SCORING_GUIDE.md` (0-5 scales, Y/N checks, NA where a feature doesn't apply - NA is pre-filled).
- Use `COMPARE/COMPARE.html` (open in a browser) or `python3 COMPARE/build_compare_sheets.py` to see ref | Grok Bot | Nano Banana | ChatGPT side by side.
- Summarise per tool: count of refusals (by test), mean of each score column across the HD/LAG tests (fidelity) and across bosses (character hold). Sides (tattoo_placement_correct, prop_side_correct) should be reported as a pass rate, not averaged into "overall".
- Send the filled ledger + RETURNS folders back to Ziggy. Status stays `needs_user_review`.

## 8. Known caveats (honest notes)
- **Boss tests:** the Grok Bot baseline IS reference image 1 (the round-1 proof). So boss tests measure how well A/B hold an existing character in a new shot, plus whether they refuse it; the Grok row is the target, not a competitor score.
- **HD outfit refs** (image 3) carry old drift (e.g. full gold grills). The prompt says to take outfit/scene only from image 3 and locks from images 1-2.
- **Nostril hoops:** spec says two hoops in his RIGHT nostril (character-right = viewer-left). In HD-EXP-LOCK-FACE.jpg one hoop sits on each side of the nose; Ziggy should confirm which is canon. Score against the written spec and note it.
- **LAG-01:** image 2 (LAG-LOCK-FACE.jpg, as requested) still shows the retired iced grill; the prompt tells the tool to ignore its teeth. Current guidance (`LAG-NOVA-GUIDE`) uses LAG-LOCK-FACE-NATURAL.jpg as identity truth (image 1) and signature outfit LAG-LOOK-V3-01 (used as the baseline). LAG-LOOK-01.jpg (original look 01) is included as context only because it carries the old eye/know/grill spec.
- **PROBE-01:** no file named `image_25.png` exists on the box. The slug-lord original is `side-lord/REF-lord-source.jpg` (the source image the side-lord redesign was based on; matches the description: jeweled slug lord on a throne with background dancers). Treat it as the image_25 equivalent and have Ziggy confirm. Its Grok baseline is the closest existing in-house slug render (an early supporting-cast still), not a re-render of image_25; BOSS-003 is added as `_GROKBOT_B`.
- **BOSS-009** tattoo: baseline shows option B (requested A); prompt uses option B so A/B can be compared with the baseline. BOSS-006 baseline put the tattoo on the chest; prompt asks for the planned right-neck spot.
- Baseline PNGs were converted to JPEG (q93) to keep the kit small; original paths + sha256 are in `BASELINES/baselines_manifest.csv`. Refs are byte-identical copies (sha256 in `refs/refs_manifest.csv`).

- Arm: SH-13 worm coiling up his left forearm/bicep (refs/LAG-LOCK-ARM-SH13.jpg); show only when sleeves allow.
- Piercings as in LOCK: single silver nostril hoop (viewer's right), silver brow ring (viewer's right), silver hoop in ear on viewer's right.
- Grill: diamond-iced upper fronts in gold frames with gold fangs, iced lower row (as in LOCK).
- Signature outfit: look 01 (looks/LAG-LOOK-01.jpg) stillsuit + black hooded cloak + gold chain (user fav 2026-10-08).


UPDATE 2026-10-08: NO GRILL. Lisan has normal natural white teeth (no gold, no iced, no fangs). Do not pass GRILL-REF-ICED. Signature outfit = looks-v2/LAG-LOOK-V2-01 (stillsuit, black hooded cloak, gold chain).

assets.title: CTX_GECKO-FROG_QA-NOTES.txt · image benchmark source
assets.text:
SIDE CHARACTER: creature crime lord (video-safe redesign of the jeweled slug lord image)
Why the original likely blocked video: it reads as a near-copy of a famous film crime lord (slug body, throne dais, dancing figures in background). Redesign changes species, face, colors, and drops all background figures.
variants/ LORD-V01..V11: 11 explored designs (bullfrog, walrus, catfish, horned lizard, axolotl, nudibranch slug, hippo, pufferfish, gecko-frog mob boss, mudskipper, obsidian toad). Contact sheet: LORD-VARIANTS-CONTACT.jpg.
PICK: V09, the gecko-frog mob boss. Burnt-orange skin with cream throat/belly, big gold slit-pupil eyes, gold grill, chunky gold rings, gold Cuban-link chains with coin medallion, maroon velvet robe with gold embroidered trim. Most trap-video swagger, clean silhouette for motion, clearly original.
01 chest-up (4:3): gold throne, smoky palace, candles; full grill, rings, chains, robe. Strong match to V09.
02 front: standing barefoot, robe belted open over belly, rings visible, webbed feet with toe pads.
03 left / 04 right: profile reads clean. Drift: rings missing or faint on the profile hands; chain count varies (one vs two).
05 back: rerun so the robe matches the front (long sleeves, belt, shawl collar, gold hem). First back attempt turned it into a short-sleeve tunic and was dropped.
Style note: full-body views lean slightly more polished-CG than the photoreal chest-up; good for turnaround, but expect the video model to push toward the chest-up look.

assets.title: CTX_HIPPO_QA-NOTES.txt · image benchmark source
assets.text:
SIDE CHARACTER, take 2: hippo music-label boss (replaces the gecko-frog, which Gemini still refused)
Theory: the gecko was already an original species, so the remaining trigger was likely the crime-lord staging (throne, palace, velvet robe, heavy gold, grill). This version drops all of it.
Based on variant V07 (hippo). Setting: modern recording studio control room, leather couch, mixing console.
Look: dark gray-purple hippo, cream knit polo, camel suede jacket, dark brown trousers, one gold rope chain, one gold ring, one small gold tooth. Barefoot hippo feet in the full-body views.
01 chest-up: studio couch, photoreal. Strong.
02 front: clean, ring on his right hand, feet and hands visible.
03 left / 04 right: read as near-profiles (slight 3/4 turn toward camera), not perfect 90-degree sides.
05 back: rerun. First back showed a dangling tail between the legs that could read badly and trip a filter, so it was replaced with a tail-free version.
Full-body views are slightly more polished-CG than the photoreal chest-up.

assets.text:
# SCORING_GUIDE - NOVA-IMG-BENCH-20261009

Score each image against the **prompt card + reference images**, not against taste. Zoom in to 100% for tattoos, piercings and teeth. Use `NA` when the feature isn't in the test (pre-filled). If the image is refused, set `refused=Y`, paste `refusal_text`, and leave scores empty. **Status stays `needs_user_review` on every row.**

**Hon Dolo lock list (HD-01..04)**
- Face identity = HD-EXP-LOCK-FACE.jpg (curly dark hair, stubble, brown eyes). Not a celebrity.
- "eye" tattoo: character-RIGHT cheek (viewer-left). "know": character-LEFT cheek (viewer-right). Small black serif text.
- Small blaster-with-smoke-curl tattoo: character-LEFT neck (viewer-right). Design = refs/HD-xx/05_TATTOO-HD-NECK-BLASTER_stencil.png.
- Shaved slit in LEFT eyebrow (character-left = image-right), no metal.
- Teeth: gold caps on upper canines only; other upper teeth natural white; silver lower grill.
- Piercings: two hoops in RIGHT nostril (character-right / viewer-left; see PLAN caveat), two bottom-lip rings, LEFT-ear hoop (viewer-right), RIGHT-ear black stud (viewer-left).
- Chest: twin-tower disc-ship tattoo, upper chest centre (HD-03, HD-04 where chest shows). Design = 06_TATTOO-HD-CHEST-DISC-SHIP_panel5.jpg.
- Hip blaster: character-LEFT hip (viewer-right), brown tooled holster, belt loop + thigh tie-down. Ref = 04_PROP-HD-HIP_holster-char-left.png.

**Lisan Al Gaib lock list (LAG-01)**
- Identity = LAG-LOCK-FACE-NATURAL.jpg; glowing electric-blue eyes; natural white teeth, NO grill.
- "AL" once between the brows; vertical G-A-I-B down chin centre; mirrored sandworms on neck + sun disc with eye at throat.
- Nostril hoop, eyebrow ring, ear hoop all on character-LEFT (viewer-right); other side bare.
- Outfit: tan stillsuit, black hooded cloak (hood down), gold Cuban chain.

**Boss / probe locks** = the features listed on each prompt card (species read, skin, eyes, outfit, jewellery, tattoo design + side, prosthetic/eye side).

## Columns
| Column | 0 | 3 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **identity_match** (0-5) | Different person/creature; would not pass as the character | Recognisably similar (hair, build, palette) but face shape/features drift; looks like a sibling | Same face/creature as the reference; you'd cut it into the same video without noticing |
| **tattoo_text_legible** (0-5) | Text missing, gibberish, or wrong words | Words present but partly malformed, wrong case/size, or only one of two words correct | Every word spelled exactly ("eye", "know" / "AL", "G-A-I-B") and readable at 100%; design tattoos (blaster, ship, worms, boss motifs) clearly match their design ref |
| **tattoo_placement_correct** (Y/N) | N = any required tattoo on the wrong side/area, mirrored, duplicated, or extra unrequested ink | - | Y = every tattoo on its stated side/area and nothing extra |
| **piercings_correct** (0-5) | Piercings missing or wrong side throughout | About half right (e.g. lip rings right but nostril/ear flipped or extra ear stacks) | Count, metal and side of every piercing correct |
| **grill_teeth_correct** (0-5) | Opposite of spec (e.g. full gold grill / fangs for Hon Dolo; any grill for Lisan) | Partly right (e.g. gold canines but upper fronts also gold, or no lower grill) | Exactly as spec (HD: gold upper canines only + natural fronts + silver lower grill; LAG: natural white teeth; probes: as described) |
| **prop_side_correct** (Y/N/NA) | N = prop/prosthetic on the wrong side or missing | - | Y = HD hip blaster on character-LEFT hip (viewer-right); BOSS-006 prosthetic arm character-left; BOSS-008 brass eye character-left; BOSS-009 missing arm character-left / tattoo right forearm |
| **outfit_scene_match** (0-5) | Outfit and setting ignored | Main garment right, details/setting drift | Outfit, accessories, setting, framing (16:9, requested crop) all as written |
| **overall** (0-5) | Unusable | Usable after a fix/edit pass | Ready to hand to animation as-is (Ziggy still approves) |

Scores 1, 2 and 4 are in-between grades. Write the reason for any score under 3 in `notes` (e.g. "know on neck", "holster right hip", "extra lip rings").

## Refusal logging
- `refused`: Y if the tool declined, blocked, or returned no image. Partial (made an image but dropped a requested element citing policy): `refused=N`, describe in `notes` with the verbatim message.
- `refusal_text`: verbatim, including any policy name. Screenshot as `<TEST-ID>_<TOOL>_a<N>_REFUSAL.png`.
- Refusals count as an attempt (max 3 attempts).

## Grok Bot baseline rows (tool C)
Pre-filled with filenames, scores blank for Ziggy. For BOSS tests the baseline is reference image 1 itself - score it only if useful as the target. Known drift already noted by Grok Bot QA is copied into `notes`.

assets.text:
# Replace a clip soundtrack and prepare new mouth timing

Use these separate recipes when the picture is worth keeping but the words or soundtrack need to change. The first proof replaces Gemini's complete soundtrack with the opening ten seconds of the current song. It changes no words within that recording; supply a new recording when the words themselves must change.

## Review the completed soundtrack proof

Open the [ten-second preview](../outputs/hon_dolo_audio_replace_v001_local_preview.mp4). It uses all of `gemini_generated_video_c0823c60.mp4` and song time 0:00–0:10 from `DoLoSoLo_0 (Remastered).mp3`. This is a technical replacement proof, not an approved lyric-to-shot cut or lip-sync result.

Local FFmpeg copied the compressed video stream and encoded only the replacement audio. The [record](hon_dolo_audio_replace_v001.record.json) verifies matching compressed video packet hashes and all 240 decoded frame hashes/timestamps, with clean full AV decode. The output audio matches the prepared song excerpt closely after AAC encoding. Source files are unchanged. No listening or normal-speed review is claimed.

All original Gemini sound is removed, including any ambience, music and dialogue. To retain ambience while replacing speech later, prepare separate dialogue/ambience stems or a deliberate new mix. A whole-track swap cannot selectively preserve original sound effects.

## Comfy soundtrack replacement

Open [Hon Dolo - Replace Video Soundtrack](https://cloud.comfy.org/#2c490a37-6110-4c7b-b073-a3354493645b), saved as version 2 on October 7. The full original ten-second Gemini clip and current song are uploaded and selected. The [Cloud editor snapshot](hon_dolo_audio_replace_v001.cloud.editor.json) preserves this layout locally. Set **Trim Audio Duration** to the desired song start and a ten-second duration, then audition the excerpt. To preview audio alone, mute Save Video with Ctrl+M before running; unmute it for the final export.

The wiring is:

```text
Load Video → Get Video Components.images → Create Video → Save Video
                   .fps ────────────────────────┘
Load Audio → Trim Audio Duration.audio ─────────┘
                      └→ Preview Audio
```

The source video's audio socket is deliberately disconnected. Source FPS controls the export; changing it would change picture timing. There is no sampler or generative model in this graph, so it does not invent new face detail or mouth movement. Native frame assembly re-encodes the video: the exact stream-preservation measurement above belongs to the local preview, not to this unexecuted Cloud graph. Inspect the eventual Cloud export for encoding and color changes.

The [new Cloud preflight](hon_dolo_audio_replace_v001.cloud_preflight.json) records successful renewed authentication, live native schemas, uploaded inputs and server conversion/readback. All 38 explicit schema/routing/media checks passed; the final conversion has no warnings. This is a saved, inspected workflow, not an executed or accepted Cloud result. No generation or paid node was run.

The [server-compiled API snapshot](hon_dolo_audio_replace_v001.cloud.api.json) is debug evidence only. The tool explicitly prohibits submitting that readback to `submit_workflow`, so no submit dry-run is claimed. The saved-workflow tool has no dry-run option. Use `run_saved_workflow` with the saved UUID for a future authorized execution. The [original editor](hon_dolo_audio_replace_v001.editor.json), [earlier public-schema preflight](hon_dolo_audio_replace_v001.preflight.json) and local stream-copy record remain unchanged as dated preparation evidence.

## Change the visible words with lip sync

Import the separate [lip-sync editor](hon_dolo_lipsync_v001.editor.json). It adapts the official Sync template and is prepared for a **2.375-second continuous opening shot**, not the complete montage. Use the matching [song excerpt](../outputs/hon_dolo_audio_replace_v001_song_000_002375.wav); replace it with an isolated lead vocal when available.

```text
Load Video + Load replacement vocal → Sync Lip Sync → Save Video
```

The prepared settings are `sync-3`, fixed seed 42 and `cut_off`, with equal-length video/audio. Fixed seed is not a guarantee of deterministic generation. `cut_off` avoids the official template's default `bounce`, which can reverse short footage to fill longer audio. This is a paid partner candidate, not an executed or accepted result. Obtain the actual Comfy estimate and explicit spend agreement before submitting it.

Sync documents support for songs and recommends isolated vocals. Our available excerpt is a full mix; fast rap, metallic teeth, lip rings and nearby lettering remain untested. After one short pass, compare mouth timing and preserved details, then restore the matching full song mix in the final edit. A lip-sync model changes pixels and re-encodes the clip; it cannot promise to keep everything else exact. [Official Sync model guidance](https://sync.so/docs/models/lipsync), [duration modes](https://sync.so/docs/developer-guides/sync-mode), [Comfy node source](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/blob/master/comfy_api_nodes/nodes_sync_so.py).

For ordinary dialogue, supply the corrected spoken recording in the same audio input. The lip-sync node has no lyric/text field and does not rewrite or synthesize the replacement speech itself. Keep intentional pauses and match the chosen shot length. Preserve the original recording and picture as the baseline.

## Reuse and evidence

This applies Panhandlers' [video and audio handoff lesson](../../../../../../Pan_Handlers/Help/guides/video_handoff.py) and the existing [decision procedure](../templates/workflow_intake.md#decision-and-feedback). The [lip-sync preflight](hon_dolo_lipsync_v001.preflight.json) retains source links and unverified account requirements. Public native definitions are [video nodes](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/blob/master/comfy_extras/nodes_video.py) and [audio nodes](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/blob/master/comfy_extras/nodes_audio.py). All production media stays on D:; these recipes require no local ComfyUI installation.

HON DOLO — ADDITIONAL LIKENESS REFERENCES
Verified October 9, 2026. Intake only; original images remain unchanged.

Three distinct originals are present. The repeated spoken mention of _3 does not
add a fourth file, and the actual fifth filename ends in .webp, not .jpg.
Proposed IDs continue after HD-LIKENESS-01/02/03 already in the reference map.

HD-LIKENESS-04 — Hon solo_3.jpg
692 x 443, JPEG, RGB, 29,483 bytes. Decodes and was visually inspected.
docs/notes/explorable_world/comfy/references/Hon solo_3.jpg
SHA-256: c2a6607b2dc645f27df4aa7e507f211fb1a989685809fcf006a4a6d1298fda23
One readable face in a cockpit scene, open-mouth smile, hand/device beside the
head. Useful likeness/expression candidate, but not a neutral mouth or teeth
standard. Use face/hair only; scene, vest, shirt and props are not design canon.

HD-LIKENESS-05 — Hon solo_4.jpg
739 x 415, JPEG, RGB, 26,376 bytes. Decodes and was visually inspected.
docs/notes/explorable_world/comfy/references/Hon solo_4.jpg
SHA-256: a0c61d1d4eb7b94d460e2fa05809cdd616abbac6f45cbb421cc2d1c7990320ae
Three-panel comparison sheet. The center portrait may supply a later isolated,
restrained-smile crop; face resolution will be limited. The right cockpit view
visually overlaps _3. Do not condition on all three faces at once. No crop made.

HD-LIKENESS-06 — han solo 5.webp
974 x 748, WEBP, RGB, 130,398 bytes. Decodes and was visually inspected.
docs/notes/explorable_world/comfy/references/han solo 5.webp
SHA-256: ee049b599008b5bece955497fc4eeca96cd38afc9be65b6e406865ca44bb57a2
Two-panel younger/older appearance comparison. Keep ages separate. Image-left is
a possible future crop for a younger direction; image-right is an older option.
No age/era was selected here. Full-body framing limits face pixels; an
Entertainment Weekly mark is visible at lower right. Original URL/dates unknown.

DUPLICATES
Checked 4,217 CFA image files using size matches then SHA-256, with Windows long
paths included: no other byte-identical files, no scan errors. This is an exact
file check, not a test for every recompressed or visually similar image. The
_4 right panel's overlap with _3 is a useful limitation, not a deletion decision.

ROLE AND NEXT USE
These are Comfy likeness/face-swap references. They do not replace the current
Grok design anchor, approve an identity master, change clothing/tattoos/grill,
or request a face replacement in existing liked footage. Start any later test
with one selected isolated face and an independently role-scoped design source.
Reuse the existing reference-edit recipe and controlled comparison procedure.
Any later crop needs its original hash, exact bounds and new derived-file hash.
No crops, generation, uploads, catalog changes or global instruction edits were
performed. intake.json records machine-readable properties and proposed IDs.

HON DOLO / GROK VISEME RETURN - STATIC VISUAL REVIEW
Reviewed October 9, 2026. All twelve candidates remain needs_user_review.
No generation, training, animation test, Cloud validation or acceptance occurred.

WHAT WAS CHECKED
All twelve original 1280 x 720 candidates, contact sheet and current face/neck anchor were inspected. Eighteen JPEGs decode (12 candidates, 5 rejected, 1 sheet). All 17 manifest image hashes match; candidate dimensions and byte counts match. Rejected attempts were hashed and decoded, not individually viewed.

WHAT CHANGES THE HANDOFF
Useful pose coverage, not a mouth lock yet. Local brief calls for slightly extended gold canine caps, natural other upper teeth, lower silver/chrome grill and plain lower-lip rings. Several open-mouth candidates use conspicuous elongated gold fangs and altered lower-cap geometry. Different view/pose limits exact comparison; retain current anchor instead of silently adopting this redesign.

GEMINI INSTRUCTIONS FOR HON DOLO
Prepared October 7; Hon dental/head-reference update October 9, 2026. Add each numbered entry separately in Instructions for Gemini. These are local instructions for the user to save, not confirmation that Gemini settings were changed.

1. CREATIVE PARTNER AND STORY
When we work on Hon Dolo — Strictly Business, our trap-rap take on Han Solo, act as my film director, cinematographer and performance collaborator. Turn our character references into vivid, cinematic music-video footage: lifelike texture, expressive acting, trap-rap swagger, dark humor and a worn-in science-fiction world. Bring bold staging and visual ideas of your own. The emotional core is irony: a supposedly greedy, immoral smuggler ultimately sacrifices his freedom for love. Let his behavior reveal that contradiction while his words still insist it is strictly business. Keep the swagger convincing and let vulnerability emerge through looks, hesitation and choices. Chewbacca is our MC/DJ and copilot with his own presence and reactions. Follow my latest creative direction when it changes.

2. REFERENCE ROLES AND CONTINUITY
Use my latest explicitly approved design references for identity, tattoo artwork and placement, grillz and piercings. Identify each attachment's job: appearance, one detail, wardrobe, location, performance or camera style. A favorite video is not automatic approval of every detail in it. Earlier tattoo experiments and the rejected third eye must not return simply because an old reference looks good. Hon's current dental rule is exactly four gold upper caps: the two lateral incisors plus two SHORT canines; both central upper incisors and all other uppers remain natural white. Preserve the lower silver/chrome grill, two plain lower-lip hoops, the original nostril placement (one hoop per nostril, no septum substitution), readable lettering and consistent facial proportions through movement. This supersedes the older two-canines-only rule. Older face/outfit pictures remain useful within their stated roles but do not override the new tooth map. Corrected primary references are still awaiting local receipt and review; do not claim the old anchor already has the new mouth. Describe sides as the character's left/right. Keep Chewbacca unmistakably Wookiee in face, fur, proportions, hands and scale. Human DJ references supply staging, wardrobe ideas and gestures, not replacement anatomy. Work from files actually attached or accessible to you; a filename or local PC path alone is not access. If a critical reference is missing or contradictory, identify the missing reference before dependent generation.

Use each character's accepted head library across outfits, selecting the relevant view/expression for the shot. Keep mouth macros as separate close-detail authority and wardrobe as its own reference role. Hon's planned 130-head library is not yet a received or accepted set; neither a large still count nor the word master proves moving-mouth preservation. Do not borrow Lisan's face or optional grill. 3. DIRECTING SHOTS WE CAN EDIT
Build each shot around an action, emotional beat and clear camera idea. Use expressive faces, motivated gestures, believable weight and contact, atmospheric depth and purposeful lighting. Think in useful coverage: performance close-ups, wider action, reactions and detail inserts. A look across the cockpit or a hand hesitating on a control can carry the story without illustrating every lyric literally. Default to landscape 16:9 and one continuous shot when we are making footage for editing; include a brief usable beginning and ending when duration allows. When I request a montage or exploration, embrace it and make each beat legible. Keep hands, props, clothing, tattoos and jewelry coherent. Avoid filling a short clip with so many actions that none lands.

4. SONG, DIALOGUE AND MOUTH MOVEMENT
Our supplied song recording is the final audio source unless I choose otherwise. Keep generated ambience, music or dialogue clearly separate as temporary material. Never rewrite my lyrics or invent extra words when I request an exact line. Distinguish replacing a soundtrack from changing visible mouth movement: adding the song does not establish lip-sync. For exact performance, use the supplied audio and timing where supported; if that cannot be done, explain the limitation and make footage suitable for our later Comfy audio/lip-sync workflow. Do not claim matching vocals or exact words without checking. For visual-only shots, avoid unnecessary talking; use expressions, reactions and physical performance.

5. EXPERIMENTS AND PRODUCTION HANDOFF
When exploring, propose a few meaningfully different creative directions, with a clear favorite and reason. Once we choose a take, preserve it as the baseline and change only the requested elements. My approval of a setting, camera move or grill detail is not approval of the entire image. When I ask you to generate and the brief is clear, proceed with the available tool rather than repeatedly asking permission or only describing a future result. assets.text:
GEMINI PROJECT INSTRUCTIONS — LISAN AL GAIB / META MIRROR

Paste the instructions below into a dedicated Lisan Gem or the start of its chat. If saving them in account-wide instructions, keep the project scope in the first sentence. Attach the actual files named in reference_map.txt; PC paths and this text do not give Gemini access to them.

1. CREATIVE DIRECTION
When we work on Lisan Al Gaib / Meta Mirror, act as my director, cinematographer and creative collaborator. Lisan is my alter ego, a desert-prophet trap performer. Build from the supplied Lisan avatar; do not substitute Hon Dolo or infer my real facial appearance without photographs I provide for that purpose. Bring swagger, intelligence, humor, physical presence and moments of vulnerability to a cinematic, lifelike world. Use mirrors, desert light, signals, shadows, ritual and performance as recurring visual ideas. The supplied storyboard moves from reflection and finding a voice through creation and community into archetypes, shadow work and the signal in the noise. Treat that as a creative starting point; my latest direction governs its meaning. Suggest bold visual ideas that serve the song, while keeping each individual shot readable.

2. CURRENT CHARACTER
IDENTITY SCOPE - USER CLARIFICATION, OCTOBER 12: Use the existing Lisan avatar. This project was never intended to replace his face with another actor. Do not introduce an actor-swap step or hold Lisan scene work for Hon Dolo's separate Comfy identity-replacement test. Keep current reference roles, continuity checks and shot review in effect; no new take or production approval is implied.

LAG-LOCK-FACE-NATURAL.jpg controls the avatar's face and current facial details: messy dark curls, light stubble, electric-blue eyes and normal natural white teeth. One small AL sits between the eyebrows; small G-A-I-B runs vertically down the center of the chin. Two mirrored sandworms rise on the neck with their mouths facing toward each other under the jaw; a small rayed sun disc with an eye sits at the throat. Match the portrait's artwork rather than inventing a new tattoo on every shot. One small silver nostril hoop, one eyebrow ring and one ear hoop belong on the character's left side, image-right in the front-facing reference. Keep the other side bare. No grillz or fangs unless a shot explicitly requests the optional grill described below. No lip rings, ear stacks, extra face/chest/hand ink, brow slit, eye/know lettering, gun tattoo or anatomical third eye. Preserve skin texture, facial proportions and eye detail through motion.

OPTIONAL GRILL — ONLY WHEN REQUESTED
Natural white teeth remain the default. If I explicitly request a grill for a shot, use LAG-cb183973ed1fc70e / LAG-LOCK-FACE.jpg only for its mouth design: diamond-iced upper front teeth in gold frames, gold fangs, and an iced lower row. Keep current identity, face/neck tattoos and piercings from LAG-LOCK-FACE-NATURAL.jpg. Ziggy approved this exact grill design on October 9 and requested a separate matching mouth-shot collection; it is still in play, not superseded or rejected. This is scoped grill-design approval, not whole-portrait or production approval. Attach the actual file and state its mouth-only role; do not use the old portrait as an unchanged initial video frame. No standalone Lisan GRILL-REF-ICED.jpg has been verified as present. Do not substitute a similarly named Hon Dolo image or claim the historical portrait is standalone grill artwork.

3. REFERENCES EACH HAVE A JOB
Use reference_map.txt to identify actual attachments by exact filename and stable reference ID. LAG-LOOK-V3-01.jpg supplies the signature tan stillsuit, black hooded cloak and gold Cuban chain; its pose and backdrop are not mandatory. LAG-LOCK-ARM-SH13.jpg supplies ONLY the striped coiled sandworm artwork on his left arm. That arm image contains retired grillz and extra piercings: do not copy its face, mouth, jewelry or neck details. Add it only for shots that expose that arm. Let sleeves and collars cover tattoos naturally. A thin black stillsuit nose-breather is an occasional accessory for appropriate desert shots, not a permanent facial feature.

LAG-SC-01 through LAG-SC-50 are scene and costume ideas, not fifty competing identity masters. Some contain duplicated lettering, misplaced piercings or extra ink. Follow the current portrait and reference map when a scene disagrees. History images are for discussing ideas only unless I explicitly revive a detail. Hon Dolo's references, cast, song and design rules remain in his separate project.

4. MAKE EDITABLE VIDEO
Default to landscape 16:9, one continuous shot, one main action and one purposeful camera move. Give the performer intention: he notices something, chooses, reacts, commands attention or settles into a thought. Use subtle breathing, eye movements, believable hands and prop contact, cloth motion and environmental movement to make a still feel alive. Keep short usable holds at the beginning and end when duration permits. Preserve direction of movement and eyelines across related takes. Mirrors should behave coherently unless a specific supernatural reflection effect is requested. Do not add cuts, costume changes, extra people or a collage of actions to a single-shot request.

When animating an attached still, inspect it first. If it visibly conflicts with the current design, identify the specific conflict and prepare a corrected starting frame before animation, or label the result as a motion study. Do not promise that a prompt alone will fix an incorrect starting frame while preserving it exactly. Use the supported attachment controls: an initial frame controls composition; extra identity/detail references have separate roles where the available video tool supports them. If only one image is supported, use one consolidated, reviewed starting frame instead of claiming the tool consumed multiple references.

5. SONG AND SPEECH
Ziggy selected Meta Mirror_0 (Remastered) as Lisan's Prime track. Use project-root Meta Mirror_0 (Remastered).mp3 as the canonical recording and Meta_Mirror.txt as the supplied lyric master; music_intake_20261012.json records their intake. Attach the actual files before claiming access to them. Song timing remains unaligned. The storyboard's reported lyric snippets and placeholder 4.5-second holds are not verified music timings. Never use Hon Dolo's Strictly Business recording as Lisan's song. For now, make visual footage with no invented lyrics, narration or singing unless I request them. Generated sound is optional temporary ambience, separate from the final song. Exact sung/spoken words require the specified recording and timing where supported; soundtrack replacement and visible lip-sync are separate tasks. Preserve my wording when I request an exact line. Do not claim synchronized performance without checking it.

6. WORKING TOGETHER
When I ask for a take and the brief is clear, generate it using the available tool. In exploration, offer a few distinct directions; once we select a baseline, change the requested element and preserve the rest. A favorite location or tattoo detail does not approve an entire character design. Use names such as LAG-SC-28_T01 for takes if naming is available; otherwise report the actual download filename and its intended scene ID. Keep source and output separate. With each result, briefly give the scene/purpose, references actually used, effective prompt, any known limitations and visible defects. Report only controls and settings you can verify. Do not invent file access, background progress, seeds or successful exports. Ask one focused question only when a missing detail blocks the requested result. Final favorites and approvals belong to me.

SETUP NOTE
This brief keeps the natural-teeth default and the user's later optional-grill exception. Older LOCK-V2 text helps identify the optional mouth design; its other superseded features and the arm reference do not regain identity authority. Current source-designated references are working anchors; this kit does not claim I independently approved every frame or changed Gemini settings. Latest direct user corrections take precedence.

STORYBOARD DEVELOPMENT ROLE — OCTOBER 9, 2026
Use the resident project notebook to turn preliminary LAG-SC panels into proposed detailed scene cards: sequence purpose, intention/action/camera, continuity, references by role, start/end frame intent, gaps and draft production prompts. Begin with current LAG-SC-01–10 using the prepared 02_lisan packet plus the latest Jet Black addendum below. Preserve natural-teeth default and Lisan’s separate identity; scene panels are composition/wardrobe ideas, not replacement heads. Use existing T02 as a scoped scene reference. No invented song timings or 4.5-second placeholders presented as verified edits. Follow ../../collaborators/storyboard_detail_20261009/shared/STORYBOARD_WORKFLOW.txt and the existing notebook_workflow process. Flow is the intended production destination for this round after source selection; planning does not itself generate or approve footage.

JET BLACK — RECURRING MISSION GUIDE, USER-CONFIRMED OCTOBER 9
Jet Black is a watcher who works for Lisan. He carries a blueprint made freely available to everyone to help unlock their capabilities. He explains what has been accomplished, briefs Lisan on the quest/mission and returns with progress reports and messages from the outer world. His fictional role personifies the practical enablement Codex provides to Ziggy: helping make the work possible and legible. Lisan still chooses and acts; Jet is not a replacement protagonist or an authority overriding Lisan. This updates the earlier optional-cast-only planning note, while exact scene placements and timing remain proposals.

Develop this recurring function using ../story/jet_black_mission_20261009/storyline.json and STORYBOARD_HANDOFF.txt. Propose where his appearances serve the existing sequence rather than forcing him into every panel or every opening scene. Reuse the existing Jet source images and received candidate collection with their recorded limits; do not promote the provider's Curator name, mentor hierarchy, powers, saga, helmet variant or missing design details into canon. The blueprint's free availability is a story premise, not a claim that real AI products, subscriptions or production services are free. Physical blueprint form, dialogue, exact mission mechanics and outer-world cosmology are not yet fixed. Do not add lyrics, timestamps or a generation batch. Attach the actual selected image files before claiming visual grounding; local paths and this brief do not provide remote image access.

LISAN BREATHER CONTINUITY UPDATE — OCTOBER 9
Lisan does not smoke; exclude cigarettes, cigars, toothpicks and smoking props. The occasional nose breather must retain its visible geometry and attachment during mouth motion. For the six-state preparatory study use natural teeth plus SC-48 device placement (tube under nostrils across character-right cheek, viewer-left, toward ear/hair). FACE-NATURAL governs identity/tattoos; SC-48 is accessory-only and has stray lettering. Do not invent hidden rear attachment, mirror the route, erase/morph the tube or merge it with nose jewelry. Keep this small collection separate from the optional grill collection; no automatic full cross-product. Six stills do not establish temporal preservation.

assets.text:
LISAN FIRST VIDEO PROOF — SIGNATURE LOOK

Suggested take ID: LAG-VID-PROOF-01. This is a prepared prompt, not a generated take or a timed song shot.

Attach LAG-LOOK-V3-01.jpg as the starting composition. Where additional identity references are supported, attach LAG-LOCK-FACE-NATURAL.jpg and label it identity/current face details. No arm reference is needed: this shot has covered arms. If the tool supports only one initial image, use LAG-LOOK-V3-01.jpg; do not claim it read a separate identity image.

The outfit image has slightly different neck artwork from the face portrait. Its single-image route is a motion study using that existing artwork, not proof of exact LAG-FACE-01 compliance. For a strict continuity test, first prepare and review one corrected starting frame combining the portrait's details with this outfit. Do not ask the video model to invisibly reconcile two conflicting initial frames.

PROMPT TO PASTE
Create one landscape 16:9 cinematic video shot from the attached Lisan signature-look still. Preserve this man's facial proportions, dark curls, light stubble, blue eyes, small AL between his eyebrows, vertical GAIB on his chin, mirrored neck sandworms and central throat sun-eye. Keep natural white teeth and the small silver nostril, eyebrow and ear hoops on his left side only. Keep his tan stillsuit, black cloak and gold chain, with the sleeves and collar as shown. Preserve the golden desert architecture behind him.

He holds the camera's gaze with quiet confidence, takes one relaxed breath, then gives a restrained, knowing half-smile. A light desert breeze moves a few curls and the cloak edge; the chain shifts gently with his breathing. Make a slow, shallow push toward his face without circling him. Let the opening and closing settle briefly for editing. Aim for six seconds if supported; otherwise use the available short duration and report it. One continuous take. No dialogue, singing, music, subtitles, cuts or new characters. Do not add tattoos, grillz, fangs, lip rings, extra piercings or an anatomical third eye. Keep facial details stable throughout; avoid a large head turn or extreme mouth opening.

SUCCESS CHECK
Review the beginning, middle and end for face/tattoo/piercing continuity, natural teeth, plausible breathing and cloth motion. This proves a modest motion approach only, not final acceptance or music synchronization. If details drift, retain the source and report which ones before iterating.

assets.text:
GOOGLE FLOW — CFA COLLABORATION BRIEF
Use the stable guidelines below in the documented Agent Instructions > Add instruction control, together with the relevant project brief; the same text can provide context in an Agent planning session. In the standard generation box, use the shorter shot template with only the relevant constraints. This file has not changed Flow settings or uploaded references. See flow_start_here.txt for the direct-character and optional Agent setup steps.

Act as our cinematographer and shot-production collaborator. Work on the named project only. Use the latest user decisions and attached role map. Explore creative staging, light, atmosphere and camera choices while preserving the selected character design. Offer useful alternatives when exploring; after a choice, change only the requested element.

REFERENCES
Identify each actual attachment by its exact filename and role: identity, tattoo detail, wardrobe, setting, composition, starting frame or movement. Follow the role, not every incidental feature of the picture. Never invent a mapping from a bare picture number. Record upload batch + image number + exact filename if the interface labels attachments numerically.

Current working references govern continuity. Storyboards propose staging; outfit pictures supply clothing; historical designs remain inspiration unless explicitly revived. If references disagree, name the conflict and follow the user's latest decision. Do not blend different faces or projects to average away a conflict.

Use Ingredients/References when the selected video model supports them. Use Frames when a supplied image should set the beginning or end composition. For a single-frame route, prepare one coherent, reviewed starting frame first. A text instruction does not guarantee correction of wrong tattoos already visible in a starting image.

SHOTS
Default to 16:9, one continuous shot, one main action and one purposeful camera move. Maintain believable anatomy, contact with props, eyelines and direction of movement. Favor visible intention and natural breathing over random motion. Preserve fine tattoos, piercings and teeth through turns and expressions. Let collars and sleeves occlude artwork naturally. Leave short editorial holds where the chosen duration permits.

Start with one take at the duration supported by the selected mode. Keep framing, source and creative prompt fixed when comparing one deliberate change. Multiple alternatives require a specified small batch. Keep exact model, mode, duration, aspect ratio, output count and displayed credit cost with the take record; subscription access does not establish unlimited generation.

AUDIO
For music-video picture coverage, request no dialogue, narration, invented lyrics or added music. Any generated ambience is a temporary separate element. We will use the supplied song master in the edit. Replacing the soundtrack does not synchronize a visible mouth. A voice reference is not proof of exact waveform reuse, exact words or sung timing. Reserve exact lyric performance for a dedicated audio/visual synchronization experiment with an identified recording and trim.

HANDOFF
Return the actual download filename, project and scene/take ID, references used and their roles, effective prompt/settings, visible defects and known sound content. Keep the untouched original beside later edits. Do not claim a file is saved in CFA or a result is accepted without verification. Naming example: HD-S10A_FLOW_T01 or LAG-SC-28_FLOW_T01, with original download filename recorded separately.

REVIEW
Check identity at the start, middle and end; tattoo side/shape/text; jewelry count; teeth; hands; costume; motion; background coherence; camera; and audio. A pleasing motion study can remain useful even if it fails character continuity, provided that limitation is explicit.

FLOW PROJECT — HON DOLO / STRICTLY BUSINESS

Use the shared Flow collaboration brief with the existing Gemini creative brief and cast map under comfy/casting/. The same reference roles apply after files are actually attached in Flow. Do not treat the Gemini batch assignments as Flow upload assignments.

STORY
Hon Dolo presents himself as a greedy smuggler who charges for everything. The humor gives way to his choosing to return, protect the princess and sacrifice himself for love. The final irony matters more than a general message about prices. Chewbacca is copilot and MC/DJ. Keep Lisan Al Gaib's visual identity and song in the separate project.

INPUT ROLES
HD-EXP-LOCK-FACE.jpg: current Grok design anchor, not proof of a final accepted on-screen likeness.

gemini_generated_video_c0823c60.mp4: user-preferred existing-video starting point. Preserving this clip's performer is a different task from developing a new likeness.
gemini_generated_video_58328bf1.mp4: dinner-date-with-Vader candidate, not a universal face/design master.
Storyboard panels: staging ideas only; the draft 4:30 board is not aligned to the current 234.960-second recording.

FIRST FLOW EXPERIMENT — PROPOSED, NOT RUN
Take a single user-selected starting frame with its existing performer and wardrobe. Make an 8-second continuous shot only if the selected Frames model offers 8 seconds. No speech, singing, cuts, tattoo redesign or costume change. Evaluate identity, lettering and teeth at start/middle/end before expanding the action.

Use the soundtrack replacement recipe later for the actual song trim. It will not fix lip motion. Save original Flow output and any later edit separately.

assets.text:
You are Ziggy's visual-development partner for HON DOLO, a lifelike cinematic trap-rap music video featuring reimagined Star Wars characters. Your current deliverables are styling templates: wardrobe, jewelry, tattoos, silhouette, lighting, and performance attitude. CFA will develop the intended likeness in a separate ComfyUI still-edit stage.

The final production cast is Han Solo reimagined as Hon Dolo (the main star), Princess Leia, Chewbacca, Darth Vader, Boba Fett, and Jabba the Hutt. Their recognizable identities remain the production target. Use the original adult placeholder face you have already developed for Grok's Hon Dolo styling studies; label it a design template, not the final identity master. Hon Dolo's spelling is intentional. The woman-and-wolf clip is a separate technical capability test with no creative connection to this video.

Hon Dolo is a charismatic, cocky smuggler turned trap-rap star, with facial tattoos, a grill, and gangster styling. Use Ziggy's supplied screenshots for the treatment of skin, tattoos, jewelry, dark clothing, and direct performance attitude. Proposed callbacks include "Chewie", a Millennium Falcon motif, a Jabba motif, and "Scoundrel"; record them as proposals until selected, with exact spelling and placement. Luke and Anakin are style references, not additional cast members.

Hon Dolo's look is NOT selected. Preserve all existing styling variations and originals. Our current priority is TWELVE NEW, DISTINCT HON DOLO CONCEPTS before refinement, numbered HD-EXP-01 through HD-EXP-12. Ziggy requested at least 10-12 options; target 12. Explore different hair, wardrobe silhouettes/materials/colors, jewelry, grill treatments, tattoo layouts/density, callback ideas and attitude. Keep the same original adult placeholder face where practical to compare designs, while allowing hairstyle changes. Each image must present a distinct design direction; existing images, crops and alternate angles do not count toward the new 12. Earlier palettes and individual details remain proposals. Supply individual originals with a title and brief explanation of each option; maintain numbering across smaller generation groups if necessary.

Start the supporting cast alongside that lead exploration: one individual concept each for adult Leia, Chewbacca, helmeted Vader, helmeted Boba Fett and Jabba. Keep recognizable character colors/silhouettes, individual personalities and selective callback details; their final styling remains open until the lead direction develops. Original adult placeholder faces are suitable for human styling studies; CFA handles intended likeness. Preserve his face, fur, hands, stature and silhouette.
