PANHANDLER NOVA — CFA RETURN, OCTOBER 8, 2026

Ziggy now has a separate CFA Creative Studio at https://algaib.streamlit.app/ with source in apps/creative_studio/app.py. The local visual library remains the production review surface. Hon Dolo / Strictly Business and Lisan Al Gaib / Meta Mirror are separate projects.

The current work adds Ziggy's Corner / Mission Control with prepared Grok, Gemini, Flow and Panhandler handoffs. Stars are a broad shortlist. An independent export basket selects a smaller package. Review choices distinguish keep, needs fixes and mark for removal; shot plans name their destination. Local browser state is not automatic repository persistence: use a chosen review file or JSON export. Hosted reviews live in the user's session and need export/import. No button sends to another provider or deletes the original media.

Three exact pixel crops preserve Luke, Leia and Han from the original group photo. Their parent hash and crop bounds are in casting/likeness_crops/manifest.json. These are separate likeness targets for a possible Comfy experiment; they do not redefine Hon Dolo's tattoos or identity anchor.

Grok's current handoff is projects/hon_dolo_strictly_business/handoffs/grok_20261008/START_HERE.txt. It preserves selected outfits/scenes while asking for current detail corrections, a coherent holstered sci-fi prop, and first two-character proofs for a boss meeting and Caleb K saloon scene. Boss discovery now compares the original slug, hippo and gecko-frog directions. Fifty single proofs are planned as five reviewed rounds of ten, followed by front/back/left/right of the selected winner. SC-BOSS-001 waits for that selection; the former Jabba-only assumption is superseded. The remembered Caleb lyric is not in the verified current lyric master, so timing and words remain open.

Measured source finding: thirteen stencil-named helpers are opaque photo crops/placement sheets, not verified transparent originals. Some dice-named files depict other retired details. Two received ship drawings disagree in geometry. The handoff requests genuine source recovery and labels missing originals, derived crops and any future reconstruction separately. It maps exact source IDs, filenames, hashes and regions and supplies a return manifest.

Flow's current UI has Images, Characters, Avatars and Uploads. Selected identity references belong in a character intake; outfits, settings and composition have separate limited roles. We are preparing a small character proof after Ziggy finishes sorting. No Flow upload, generation or character acceptance is recorded. Model capability documentation is evidence for choosing a test, not a measured quality result.

BOUNDED TEACHING RETURN
Use existing reference-role, controlled-comparison and export/persistence lessons. Add these examples only where they help: a liked outfit can still need tattoo repair; a filename does not establish the artwork's role; an exported selection list is not a media ZIP; an exact crop is not a generated recreation; reference availability, actual upload, generation and acceptance are distinct. Preserve the existing Pan schemas and completed curriculum. Link CFA evidence rather than copying the full media library. Return adopted changes through Help/CFA_FEEDBACK.md. CFA retains production ownership; this prepared brief does not claim Panhandler Nova has read it.

COLLABORATORS WORKSPACE — FOLLOW-UP
Ziggy asks Panhandler Nova to add a Collaborators navigation area on the Pan app: begin with ComfyUI, then provide the explanatory how-tos and whys for Grok, Gemini and Flow where appropriate. CFA’s Collaborators area remains operational: source assets, actual graphs, outputs, observed defects and the next action. One media record appears through both its project and the collaborator workspace; avoid separate master copies.

The soundtrack replacement output is outputs/hon_dolo_audio_replace_v001_local_preview.mp4: local stream-copy picture preservation is measured; the related Cloud graph is saved/server-converted but not executed. Mouth sync is a separate unexecuted candidate. Motion, depth and edge tests preserve their actual failure/acceptance states in collaborators/comfy_workflows.json. Reuse the existing video_handoff lesson for native frames/audio assembly; do not teach the audio swap as lip-sync.

New review teaching: Multiverse Dolo is an explicit creative lane and is excluded from Prime collaborator packages by default. Working-reference requests have an approval scope and enter a sweep; a favorite is not a complete-character approval. Save/export carries the browser review state to CFA. Preparing a sweep does not invoke an agent or delete originals. Creative discovery may invent tattoos, piercings, missing limbs and other character features without an approval-first gate. Every new tattoo arrives with a FOUR-OPTION standalone design sheet in the same delivery, identifying the option matching its body proof. Label a later reconstruction honestly. Expand an intriguing motif to 10-12 only when Ziggy asks. Existing Prime preservation tasks still protect current details. Recovering missing original art remains separate from new design. This supersedes the earlier blanket stencil-first rule.

Bounded Pan task: link the new Collaborators area to existing lessons, add these state/preservation examples, and return adopted pages plus checks in Help/CFA_FEEDBACK.md. Do not copy production media or rewrite CFA workflows. This is a manual handoff, not a claim that another Nova has read or implemented it.


LATEST REVIEW AND FLOW SOURCE CORRECTIONS
The saved review was read without modification: 35 favorites and two user-origin records were validated against actual IDs, hashes and disk bytes. Four stale catalog-origin records were ignored. See projects/hon_dolo_strictly_business/feedback/review_sweep_20261008.json and the read-only review_intake_plan.py. Flow experiment 002 is now prepared from the retained 41-second source: frames 244-387, six seconds, 1280 x 720 at 24 fps, re-encoded H.264 with no audio. All 144 excerpt frames decode; quarter-second samples and full-size beginning/middle/end were inspected; no scene trigger above 0.18 appears inside the excerpt. A source montage being longer does not establish better quality. One subtle lighting edit is proposed; no Flow upload, generation, provider cost or acceptance is claimed. Panhandler's requested Collaborators area teaches the how and why: reference roles, creative discovery versus preservation, honest artwork lineage, finite review rounds, source correction precedence, media export versus selection metadata, and motion/audio validation. Link CFA evidence rather than duplicate its masters. Start with existing Comfy lessons and add Grok/Gemini/Flow explanatory connections where useful. Preserve completed curricula and schemas; no production execution or Pan app change is performed by this return. Record adopted teaching pages and checks in Help/CFA_FEEDBACK.md. Manual ledger synchronization is not an automatic message or proof of Nova's adoption.

HON DOLO — FIRST FLOW STILL PRESERVATION PROOF
Prepared October 8, 2026. Experiment ID: FLOW-HD-STILL-001.
State: planned; user is still sorting. No upload, model invocation or approved shot is claimed.

PURPOSE
Establish whether Flow keeps the current Hon Dolo face and visible details from one reference before introducing another outfit, character, pose or motion. This still-first sequence takes priority over the earlier proposed first-video test in project_brief.txt. That video prompt remains a later candidate.

SINGLE PLANNED INPUT
Reference ID: HD-DESIGN-01
Asset ID: HD-DROP-ef5d59a6402e
Exact filename: HD-EXP-LOCK-FACE.jpg
Repository source: docs/notes/explorable_world/comfy/references/hon-dolo-lock-turnaround-outfits/hon-dolo-lock-turnaround-outfits/HD-EXP-LOCK-FACE.jpg
SHA256: ef5d59a6402eaff568e30bb6a4432b14b90c692ea6758a761c7702c44d457978
Role: current visible Grok design/face reference; no new final production identity approval.
Planned package home: Characters/Hon Dolo. This is organizational intent, not a verified Flow folder-import action.
Flow asset ID / upload batch / picture number: unbound.

READY CONDITIONS
Finish sorting and choose this input deliberately. Upload the actual file once through Upload, then verify it is visible and record its Flow binding. Add from project can reuse it only after it exists in that project. Confirm image mode, displayed model label, output count, any available aspect setting and cost in the live UI. The screenshot's Format menu was not opened, so its options remain unknown. No other character or outfit image is attached for this baseline.

BASELINE A — ONE STILL, NANO BANANA 2.1
This is our proposed comparison baseline, not an executed result. Retain source composition and framing rather than introducing a pose change immediately. Where a setting is unavailable, record unavailable; do not invent a seed or a hidden control.

Prompt to use only after the actual source is attached:
Create one reference-faithful still of the same Hon Dolo character shown in HD-EXP-LOCK-FACE.jpg. Keep the face shape, age, curls, facial hair, expression, skin finish, head angle, crop, clothing, lighting and setting closely matched. Preserve the actual eye lettering under his right eye (viewer-left) and know under his left eye (viewer-right), with their existing size and direction. Preserve the neck blaster with its smoke curl, the visible chest artwork, the two gold upper canine caps with the other upper teeth natural, the metallic lower grill and visible nose, lip and ear jewelry. Let existing clothing occlude the same details. Return one still with no extra characters, new lettering, props or design embellishments. No anatomical third eye, retired bird/Jabba/Chewie/dice motifs, new tattoo reconstruction or actor-likeness replacement.

REVIEW BEFORE ANY EXPANSION
Compare side-by-side at the same displayed scale: facial proportions and hair; exact eye/know text and side; mouth/grill; visible jewelry; neck/chest drawing; clothing and background. Note the location of each mismatch. If the result looks pleasing but alters the identity or required details, mark it failed_preservation rather than accepted. Do not claim exact pixel preservation for a generated image.

CONDITIONAL MODEL COMPARISON B
If A fails a specific required detail, one Nano Banana Pro comparison is proposed. Use the same original input and exact prompt, with matching available framing/resolution/settings. Change only the model and record any settings that cannot be matched. Do not feed A into Pro as an automatic finishing pass; that would test a different operation and could accumulate drift. Keep both originals and report which defects each retains. Stop after this bounded comparison and decide from evidence; do not open a retry batch.

WHY THESE MODELS
Google's current documentation positions 2.1 as the standard fast image model, and Pro for complex designs and detailed control. Our sequence is a practical hypothesis to test, not proof Pro will preserve this character better. 2 Lite remains a separate efficiency option. Check current UI cost before generation. Source checked October 8, 2026: Google Flow models and supported features — https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16352836?hl=en

LATER CHANGE — ONE VARIABLE
After the baseline is reviewed, choose either a very small head turn with the same framing OR a slightly wider crop with the same head pose. Do not change both, introduce a second outfit, add another face or reveal unreferenced hidden tattoos in the same test. A wardrobe reference may later supply clothing alone; it must not overwrite current identity. Use a separately reviewed coherent scene still before testing camera movement or two-person Flow video.

RECORD TO RETURN
Experiment ID; A or B; actual downloaded filename; actual source attachment ID and filename; exact prompt; displayed model; visible format/resolution; output count; displayed cost; settings actually available; output dimensions; file SHA256 computed from actual bytes; defect list; user review state. Leave unavailable values null/unknown. Suggested local result labels FLOW-HD-STILL-001_A_2p1 and FLOW-HD-STILL-001_B_Pro are planning labels, not files that already exist.

AUDIO / TIMING
This is a still test. Later video takes should use no spoken dialogue, singing, invented lyrics or added score. The current supplied song is added separately; soundtrack replacement does not create accurate mouth timing. No song timecode or Caleb lyric change is assigned by this experiment.

FLOW EXPERIMENT 002 — PRESERVE THE CAR-ARRIVAL SHOT, CHANGE LIGHTING ONLY
Prepared October 8, 2026. State: local excerpt and brief ready; no Flow upload or generation.

EXACT SOURCE
Use GEM-5A115C59: gemini_generated_video_5a115c59.mp4, 41.000 seconds, 984 frames at 24 fps, 1280 x 720. Source SHA256: 854dd279179300173f89339e707c326e7a48cb594cc52f6879229e4d45dc395e.
LATEST USER CORRECTION: keep the longest 41-second continuation GEM-5A115C59. The earlier 40-second GEM-97D0B65E is archived from the working library. This replacement excerpt was freshly trimmed from the retained source; earlier selection is recorded in superseded_40second_manifest.json. The user describes these as successive downloads of one ongoing Gemini continuation; both original byte streams remain preserved.

WHY THIS EXCERPT
Longer footage is not inherently higher-quality footage. The 41-second source is a montage with multiple cuts and changing views. It exceeds the currently documented up-to-10-second Flow video-edit input. Use one continuous source shot to distinguish preservation from a new edit or montage.

Selected interval: original 00:10.166667 to 00:16.166667, end exclusive; source frames 244 through 387 inclusive. The six-second excerpt shows silver-jacket Dolo, the arriving/descending car, his turn and the opening door. It starts after the preceding cut and ends before the next. All 144 output frames decode; no scene-change trigger above 0.18 occurred within the excerpt. Twenty-four quarter-second samples plus start/middle/end images were visually checked. This is sampled visual inspection, not acceptance of every source detail or normal-speed playback.

BASELINE A — ALREADY PREPARED, NO GENERATION NEEDED
FLOW-HD-VIDEO-002_GEM-5A115C59_10p1667-16p1667.mp4 is the actual comparison baseline and the only media input for this experiment.
SHA256: f8f2aa30265392634b67dbddebdc6ac0f05007de1abb2730f27d27513e72d378.
Six seconds, 1280 x 720, 24 fps, H.264. Frame-accurate trim re-encoded with libx264, preset medium, CRF 21, yuv420p and faststart. Dimensions and timing are retained; this is not a stream-copy or exact-pixel-preservation claim. Audio was intentionally omitted from this visual-only test; the untouched 41-second original retains its original AAC soundtrack. Frame previews are viewing aids, not extra conditioning references.

COMPARISON B — ONE PROPOSED FLOW VIDEO EDIT
Model/mode candidate: Gemini Omni Flash 1.1, Video to Video editing, standard 720p. Official Google documentation currently lists uploaded-video editing up to 10 seconds for Omni Flash 1.1; Veo 3.1 Lite/Fast/Quality do not list video editing support. This does not verify the selected account's live controls, entitlement, cost or success. Source checked October 8, 2026: https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16352836?hl=en

Unzip the package locally. Upload the six-second MP4, not the ZIP or the full montage. Use the actual uploaded clip as an edit input, then verify the model, edit mode, duration, output count and displayed cost. Request one output. Keep six seconds and matching resolution; record actual output FPS rather than assuming that control is offered. If this edit route is unavailable, stop and report that fact; do not silently switch to still-image-to-video or re-create the entire montage.

PROMPT FOR B
Edit the attached six-second video. Make only one visual change: give the existing illumination a subtle warmer color balance, keeping the night scene, approximate exposure and neon atmosphere. Preserve the existing performer, face, hair, visible tattoos, grillz and jewelry exactly as they appear in this clip. Keep the silver jacket silver, the car's design and color, all hands and clothing, street layout, signs and reflections coherent. Preserve the complete motion sequence, timing, camera movement, car descent, door opening, character turn and body/door contact. Keep one continuous shot with no new cuts, objects, people, face replacement, tattoo correction, retiming or extra action. Return silent video with no dialogue, lyrics, music or narration.

PRESERVATION SCOPE
Use this clip's existing performer and details as the baseline. Do not also attach LOCK-FACE or a Han likeness crop: adding another identity would make this a different experiment. Existing lettering/jewelry inconsistencies in the source are not being repaired in a lighting test. The wide moving view is useful for motion, prop and scene checks, but it cannot prove the finest tattoo lettering is correct. Requests to preserve details are test criteria, not guaranteed model behavior.

REVIEW B AGAINST A
Compare matching beginning, middle and ending moments and normal-speed playback. Check face/hair, jacket seams, hands, car/wheel silhouette, door hinge/motion, character/car overlap, street geometry, reflections and sign layout. Inspect the car's arrival, the turn toward it and entry timing specifically. Pass only if the intended warmth changes without material redesign, new cuts, altered action or timing. Record output duration/FPS/dimensions and audible content. A pleasing regenerated clip may still fail preservation.

BOUNDARY / NEXT DECISION
One proposed B output, no automatic variants or retries. If it drifts, keep the output with an explicit defect list; do not call it accepted. For a pure color change, conventional grading remains a separate preservation-oriented option. A video-capability experiment is useful even when the model fails this constraint. The 41-second original remains untouched and can supply other independently reviewed shots later.

AUDIO AND RETURN
The real song is added later from an identified recording/trim. A soundtrack replacement does not repair lip-sync. Do not invent lyrics or copy a scratch voice into the song master.
Return the downloaded result plus RETURN_RECEIPT.json, recording actual filename/hash, source hash, model/mode, exact prompt/settings, dimensions/FPS/duration, visible defects and user review state. Leave unknown fields null. Do not label the result approved on our behalf.

lettering and background. Canny did not materially solve preservation. Neither
was accepted; full continuous playback/audio quality was not established.

the source color interpretation retained and all other grading controls fixed.

the face. Preserve framing, dimensions, FPS, timestamps and frame count; check
for highlight clipping, lost metal detail and new encoding artifacts. A grade
is not a physically new light or restored detail. No grade has been executed.

GEMINI REQUEST — ONE TAKE AT A TIME, TWO-TAKE MAXIMUM
Check the actual session's attachment support first; video analysis and a video
generation control input are different capabilities. Ask for one eight-second
take if supported; otherwise record the offered short duration. Do not silently
extend it or start a batch. Keep full-face framing sufficiently close to inspect
the mouth, rather than a disembodied mouth-only shot.

Draft A prompt — use only after the corrected primary reference is registered:
"Create one continuous close-up mouth-continuity proof of this same Hon Dolo.

steady neutral light. Preserve the reference face, lettering and piercings.

The slug/dais reference supplies another silhouette and opulent staging direction. These are artistic starting points, not a requirement to merge all three.

Explore coherent original creatures with convincing textures, restrained expressions, costume weight and a clear powerful business-boss presence. You may invent tattoos, piercings, missing limbs, prosthetics and other character features when they improve the concept. For every new tattoo, deliver its FOUR-OPTION standalone design sheet in the SAME BATCH, name the matching option, and label any after-the-fact reconstruction honestly. No permission-first tattoo gate. Expand a chosen motif to 10-12 only when Ziggy asks.

START WITH BOSS-001 THROUGH BOSS-010 ONLY.
Each is one readable portrait or three-quarter character proof, not a four-view set. Keep framing/lighting useful for comparison while varying silhouette, anatomy, skin, attitude and costume. Use the ten as a diverse first exploration rather than minor recolors. Return the individual images, a clearly labelled ten-image contact sheet and the manifest. Pause for Ziggy's feedback before BOSS-011..020, then 021..030, 031..040 and 041..050. Keep numbers stable across revisions; use _v002 rather than recycling an ID for a different character.

After Ziggy picks the winning ID, make four consistent views: front, back, character-left and character-right. Use the SAME identity and body, not four redesigns. No automatic animations, full rosters of turnarounds or dialogue.

Gemini's refusal of all three earlier directions is user-reported; we have not independently observed the attempts or their reasons. This brief evaluates new designs artistically. It neither promises another service will accept them nor asks you to defeat its restrictions.

Prepared 2026-10-10T05:09:48Z by CFA Codex Nova for Claude, current Pan_Handlers Master Repo steward and repository lead. CFA Nova remains CFA lead. This packet is prepared for the established Pan operational inbox; it has not yet been posted there. No Claude reading or adoption is acknowledged.

The old October 8 teaching return was already adopted through **October 9, 2026, 01:45:08 UTC**. The [Pan adoption record]([local path] names that cutoff and records the adopted pages and checks. The adopted prefix is not repeated here.

The [verbatim post-cutoff delta](docs/notes/explorable_world/pathfinder_handoff/claude_return_20261010/POST_014508_DELTA.txt) preserves source physical line 71 through EOF: byte offset 13,471, 35,999 original bytes, SHA-256 `def32c638ac5c548097f22188bde74103a82138d7b2e30fe0543862f4cb1e05a`. The [canonical source return](docs/notes/explorable_world/comfy/projects/collaborators/panhandler_return_20261008.txt) is 49,470 bytes, SHA-256 `a186474fb5615841a631342dfc76343b997ea4711e2216feac7947203a88eef9`. Source wording, newline and encoding bytes are unchanged. The delta starts with the Lisan local-receipt update at October 9 02:45:47 and ends with the external video-study teaching return. Later adoption remains unverified. These production states and requests are dated source material; reconcile them against current canonical evidence before treating them as current operating facts.

Ziggy's reference to a ready item in “our inbox” did not identify an exact file. This is the best evidenced existing return candidate, not a claim that the unspecified item was uniquely found or delivered. The [reconciliation receipt](docs/notes/explorable_world/pathfinder_handoff/claude_return_20261010/RECONCILIATION.json) records the cutoff, exact byte comparison and evidence limits.

Seven current introductions are canonical CFA files. Collaborators check addressed messages during active sessions. The [stewardship and scope record](docs/notes/explorable_world/comfy/projects/collaborators/collaboration_authority.json) and [posted Nova-to-Claude role notice](docs/notes/explorable_world/comfy/projects/collaborators/mailbox/messages/b53fb448-78f7-4c00-bcf2-0c05efa7b48a.json) already record the role decision. FLOW 002 - ZIGGY'S A/B REVIEW CLARIFICATION
October 12, 2026. Transcribed from the user's current review. No new generation.

CURRENT DISPOSITION
A and B need fixes and are not production-approved. No numeric grade was given.
The earlier warmth-only acceptance remains a dated observation. This review
supersedes it as the current disposition: a visible warmer result is a technical
effect, not approval of convincing relighting, acting, likeness or the scene.

A - ORIGINAL SIX-SECOND EXCERPT
FLOW-HD-VIDEO-002-A
SHA256 f8f2aa30265392634b67dbddebdc6ac0f05007de1abb2730f27d27513e72d378
Ziggy finds the outfit perfect and the blue aesthetic beautiful. The actor is
not a sufficient likeness; tattoos are difficult to see, with some neck tattoo
and chain visible. The car entry/descent and body interaction look physically
unrealistic. The picture looks grainy/low resolution to him. That appearance
judgment does not change measured metadata: 1280x720, 24 fps, 144 frames, 6.0s.
It is not a measured 480p source or an accepted identity reference.

B - FLOW WARMTH EDIT
FLOW-HD-VIDEO-002-B
SHA256 8d090aaa5a45cc42cb9d52e7b26d9419a8d8aa8c029c22a1859752ec7e0cf3c2
The warm streetlight change is visible, but reads as a yellow filter/surface
wash rather than source-motivated light with local falloff, coherent shadows
and reflections. A's pre-existing likeness, visibility and physical-motion
defects are inherited; this review does not claim Flow created those defects.
B measures 1280x720, 24 fps, 144 frames, 6.0s video in a 6.02s container. The
existing near-silent AAC measurement remains unchanged; no new listening or
silent-stream claim is made. Actual generation cost remains unknown.

BETTER PROMPT OR BETTER MODEL?
The actual saved prompt requested a "subtle warmer color balance" and asked
Flow to preserve the source's complete motion. It did not distinctly ask for
physical light-source behavior. A global-looking warmth effect alone cannot
tell us that Omni is the wrong model. The requested physically motivated
relight is a different declared lighting change, named separately below.
Root's read-only October 12 inspection reports the same prompt and Omni 1.1
Flash in the current editor; no higher-quality/model or resolution selector
was visible, no menus opened, no settings changed. Alternatives are unverified.
The single proposed diagnostic keeps that model and source so the deliberate
change is the lighting brief. It cannot repair the source's actor or physical
performance while also being a preservation test. Those inherited defects
remain reasons this clip is nonproduction.

ONE FUTURE DIAGNOSTIC - PROPOSED C, NOT SENT
Adapter: FLOW-HD-VIDEO-002-C-MOTIVATED-LIGHTING-PROPOSED.
Use A unchanged again, not B. Compare received B against one C output with A
as their common source. Same Omni 1.1 Flash video-edit mode if currently offered;
one output, six-second input, original-size/1280x720 target. Record offered
controls and any forced differences. Do not invent the unknown original seed.
Inspect the source's actual lighting cues first; verify current mode, displayed
cost and allowance before any future submission. No automatic retry, model
change, upscale or separate motion-repair run follows from this proposal.

BEGIN PROPOSED C PROMPT
Edit the attached six-second source video. Change only its lighting treatment.
Make the existing streetlight illumination gently warmer in a physically
motivated way: localized pools of warm light with distance falloff, coherent
shadows and highlights, and reflections that follow the existing car, jacket
and street surfaces as they move. Follow the source's existing practical-light
directions; do not add or relocate fixtures or objects. Preserve cool neon in
areas those warm practicals do not illuminate. Do not apply a uniform yellow
filter or warm the entire image equally. Keep the silver jacket recognizably
silver and preserve plausible material colors and the scene's night exposure.

Preserve the source's complete six-second motion and timing, camera movement,
car descent, door opening, character turn, body/door contact and scene geometry.
Keep the same performer, face, hair, visible tattoos, grillz, jewelry, hands,
clothing, car design, street and signs. Do not correct or redesign any of these.
One continuous shot, no cuts, retiming, added action, people or objects. Return
one video at the original size, without dialogue, lyrics, music or narration.
END PROPOSED C PROMPT

Review C's native playback and matched moments against both A and B. Look for
light changing with surface orientation and distance, coherent moving shadows
and reflections, preserved cool/warm separation and no new motion/identity
changes. An unchanged inherited defect is not a newly introduced lighting
failure; it still prevents production use. A future pass/fail concerns this
specific lighting treatment, not general model quality.

The existing decision/feedback procedure and Pan_Handlers sampling_lab lesson
guide the one-change comparison. The workshop also preserves conventional
grading/compositing as an alternative for lighting-only work; no second test
or new workflow is commissioned here.

Records: USER_REVIEW_20261012.json, RETURN_RECEIPT_20261012.json and
ACTUAL_PROMPT_20261012.txt. Media and earlier preparation records are unchanged.

SUPERSEDING USER REFINEMENT - OCTOBER 12, 2026
Current scope for BOTH A and B: Scene.
Current stage for BOTH: Preliminary.
Current decision for BOTH: Needs fixes. No numeric scores. Neither is production.
Earlier review observations above remain preserved; outfit praise is scoped,
and the old warmth-only observation is not current whole-scene acceptance.

TECHNICAL CLARIFICATION
Fresh FFmpeg readings from Personal Assistant, relayed by CFA Nova: both files
are 1280x720 with 144 frames and nominal 24 tbr. A reports a 5.96s header and
average about 24.17fps; B reports 6.02s and 24fps. Packet presentation is about
six seconds. ffprobe was unavailable, so exact source avg_frame_rate and stream
duration are unknown. Earlier shorthand saying both were 24fps/6.0s must not
be read as proof of identical native average rates. The media is unchanged.
Subjective grain/softness still does not make either encoded file 480p.

The official Google model matrix, verified by CFA Nova on October 12, lists
Omni Flash 1.1 video editing at standard 720p / draft 360p, while Veo 3.1 Quality
does not support video editing:
https://support.google.com/flow/answer/16352836?hl=en
This does not establish account export options or a higher-quality drop-in
editing control. Those account choices remain unverified.

CURRENT SINGLE DIAGNOSTIC - C PROMPT ADAPTER V2
This replaces the earlier proposed C prompt, not adds a second test. Use the
same unchanged A, same actually available Omni edit route and one short output,
with no retries or model variants. Keep actual source timing and motion; record
returned timing/rates rather than assuming identical averages. Source action
or likeness repair is separate and is not requested in this lighting test.

BEGIN CURRENT PROPOSED C PROMPT V2
Edit the attached source video. Change only the existing street lighting.
Preserve the beautiful blue night ambience and cool neon atmosphere. Make the
existing lamp emitters gently warmer, and warm only the surfaces those lamps
actually illuminate. Follow the source's existing light directions. Give the
warm light local distance falloff and geometry-aware occlusion, with coherent
shadows, highlights and reflections that follow the car, jacket and street as
they move. Keep unlit and occluded areas in the existing blue ambience. Do not
add or relocate lamps, objects or signs. Avoid a global yellow filter, a uniform
surface wash or warming the entire frame equally. Retain plausible skin color,
the silver jacket's silver material, car colors and the night exposure.

Preserve the source's complete motion sequence and timing, camera movement,
car descent, door opening, character turn, body/door contact and scene geometry.
Keep the same performer, face, hair, visible tattoos, grillz, jewelry, hands and
clothing. Do not repair or redesign their likeness or action in this test.
One continuous shot, no cuts, retiming, added people, objects or extra action.
Return one video at the original size, silent, with no dialogue, lyrics, music
or narration.
END CURRENT PROPOSED C PROMPT V2

Before any future run, verify the actual edit route, visible cost and allowance.
Review this one output for localized light behavior, retained blue ambience,
material colors and no new action/identity changes. No video was generated by
this refinement. A better source performance/likeness remains a separate job.

assets.text:
Notebook collaboration workflow

METHOD HOME — REUSE NYQUIST
The shared methodology stays in Nyquist. This CFA folder supplies project prompts, source/asset maps, notebook state, creative decisions and outcome records. It is not a second Holy Grail or an independent version of the shared workflow.

Follow these upstream breadcrumbs before adding a general process, hook or template:
- Overall method and Studio output specifications:
  [local path]
- Question/answer rounds and cross-notebook routing:
  [local path]
- Reusable output-request format:
  [local path]
- Pipeline entry point and existing tools:
  [local path]
- Second-pass double-dip mining:
  [local path]

Read the relevant upstream section and reuse it where it fits. Check an existing tool's inputs, outputs and scope before running it against CFA; a breadcrumb is not an instruction to execute a script. Add only the CFA-specific fields or behavior that are actually missing. Useful general improvements should be proposed back to the method's home rather than maintained as a competing CFA specification.

The local templates record CFA asset IDs, reference roles, approvals and evidence; they are project-specific forms. The checklists are short application notes. The audit files and Studio settings are dated observations, not live mirrors or replacement authorities. If Nyquist changes, consult its current files and update only affected CFA prompts/notes. Preserve historical receipts. No automatic cross-repository sync is implied.

Start with OPERATOR_MENU.txt for actual notebook work: seventeen ready prompts, three notebook roles and a small creative review cycle. STUDIO_SETTINGS.txt records the current documented controls. The 00_MASTER, 01_HON and 02_LISAN prompt files contain complete requests with purpose, sources and settings.

START_HERE.txt explains the supporting intake and evidence process. This directory adapts the inspected Nyquist learning loop to CFA's existing project and review records. It does not replace the gallery, creative approvals, execution receipts or notebook setup record.

operating_sources.json: exact local inputs for each prompt card; local existence is not remote source readiness.
double_dip_queue.json: four prepared questions with evidence and closure conditions; none sent or answered here.
METHOD_AND_CONTROLS_AUDIT.json: practical Nyquist method sources and dated official Google controls used for these prompts.

SOURCE_AUDIT.json: exact local prior-art paths and SHA-256 hashes, inspected scope, relevant findings and official links. Hashing a file is not a claim that every line or media frame was reviewed.
notebook_registry_snapshot.json: dated reference to existing Notebook0/Hon/Lisan IDs and measured source observations; consult its source receipt for current state.
source_manifest.template.json: inert template; null fields and empty lists are unknown/unfilled, not successes.
source_packet/: outbound question and evidence packet.
foreign_returns/raw/: unedited incoming provider material and provenance.
review_queue/: evidence checks and explicit decisions.
approved_sources/: current material approved for a defined role and destination.
promotions/: immutable decision history linking source, review and approved revision.

All template IDs are placeholders. No automatic approval, processing, upload or synchronization is implemented. No media masters or Nyquist source files were copied into this folder.

GEMINI VIDEO SOURCE CONTEXT - OCTOBER 14

assets.title: Notebook workbench · start here
assets.text:
CFA NOTEBOOK WORKBENCH — READY PROMPTS
Prepared October 9, 2026. Local preparation; no prompts sent or Studio jobs started.

START HERE
The local notebooks are our resident story and character collaborators. Notebook 0 connects their useful lessons. Nova prepares the questions, sources and settings; Ziggy supplies creative direction and makes choices. The aim is useful creative work, not a standing sixty-question interrogation.

The shared method lives in Nyquist; README.txt links directly to its Holy Grail, workflow, output template and double-dip specification. This menu keeps only CFA's ready requests and operating choices. Consult the upstream method before building new general hooks or procedures here.

For the first working round, run H01 in Hon and L01 in Lisan after selecting their current sources. Bring each short answer to Notebook 0 with its supporting evidence and run M01. Choose ONE useful Studio artifact afterward. Fourteen prompt cards below are a menu, not a batch to generate.

00_MASTER_PROMPTS.txt
  M01 — Three-question studio check-in (chat).
  M02 — Double dip: route an existing question to relevant project expertise (chat).
  M03 — A small reusable care package (Document report).
  M04 — What changed and what we do next (Brief audio).
  M05 — One-page map of the creative workflow (infographic).

01_HON_PROMPTS.txt
  H01 — Story, character and next useful decision (chat).
  H02 — Use the footage we already have: chorus development brief (Document report).
  H03 — Strictly Business story and character lookbook (slide deck).
  H04 — Does the emotional irony read? (Critique audio).
  H05 — Bring a collaborator into this project (Explainer video overview).

02_LISAN_PROMPTS.txt
  L01 — World, character and next useful decision (chat).
  L02 — Meta Mirror character and world lookbook (slide deck).
  L03 — Visual motif map (infographic).
  L04 — One-minute project introduction (Short video overview).

HOW I WILL DRIVE A ROUND
1. Read the latest user decisions and local project records. Select the applicable card and the smallest source set that answers it. The operating_sources.json file maps the cards to real local inputs; a local path is not a notebook source.
2. Add or update the necessary material in actual Sources and verify that it is usable there before relying on it. Select current project sources; select historical alternatives only when comparing them. Do not upload the whole prompt menu as creative canon.
3. Paste the full text between BEGIN PROMPT and END PROMPT into chat, or into the named Studio customization field. Set the controls listed on that card; STUDIO_SETTINGS.txt records current official documentation. A chat request for a deck is not evidence that a Studio deck was created.
4. Let the answer move the work forward: current story, existing material, next choice. Ask another question only for a real ambiguity or a new decision. If selected sources are insufficient, report the missing source; do not fill it from memory.
5. Preserve the result and evidence. Make a short second pass over the SAME result: what useful limitation, method or next-test idea emerged that we did not originally ask for? Extract at most three, with evidence, and keep untested ideas labeled. This is double-dip mining; a second reading is not independent confirmation. For a visual deliverable, check actual images, lettering, names and continuity. Its attractive layout does not make generated artwork a character reference. A text source about a picture can support a description, but cannot substitute for that picture.
6. Send Notebook 0 a concise lesson or scoped winner when useful. It can then prepare a relevant question for another project. Record actual delivery and answers; this folder does not automatically connect notebooks.

WHEN TO REOPEN THE ROUND
After a new intake, a meaningful creative correction, a winner selection, or a failed test that changes the next step. Use only the relevant card. No scheduled automation is created here.

DOUBLE DIPPING, ADAPTED TO CFA
Project A's primary result -> second-pass mining of that result -> a source-backed care package in Notebook 0 -> a bounded question for Project B when its material can help -> its cited answer -> a concrete update or an explicit unresolved item.

Notebook 0 keeps an open-question list and looks for shared usefulness. Hon and Lisan stay centered on their own stories; they receive at most one relevant cross-project question in an ordinary round. No useful connection is a valid result. Faces, tattoos, grills, cast, songs and approvals do not transfer with a technique.

The first four real opportunities are in double_dip_queue.json: detail preservation, outfit/prop organization, deciding when existing material is ready for the next collaborator, and learning whether a Gemini continuation preserves the earlier footage. Each is prepared, not sent. Close an item only after evidence and the receiving project's decision are recorded; an answer file alone does not close it.

CHOOSING AN OUTPUT
Chat: make a decision or inspect a conflict.
Report: a usable brief for the next collaborator, with exact material and open work.
Slides: a visual lookbook or story meeting.
Audio: catch up while away from the screen, or hear a critique of the story.
Infographic: keep a simple relationship or workflow map visible.
Video overview: orient someone to the project and its sources.

The Studio video cards are project presentations. Production footage, exact character performance, music timing and lip-sync retain their separate Gemini/Flow/Comfy workflows. Google's Video Overview documentation describes source-based explanation; it does not establish those production controls. This is our workflow distinction, not a claim that cinematic presentation is impossible.

READY TEXT VS READY VISUALS
These prompts can use verified text sources now for textual story and workflow work. Visual likeness checks and image-led lookbooks require usable visual Sources. Our recorded Lisan image attempts failed; do not imply that these new prompt files fixed ingestion. If visuals are unavailable, prepare a clearly labeled text outline and keep the visual job pending.

METHOD BREADCRUMB
Nyquist's report_template.md and the worked New_2_S_Parameters/report.md pair each output with settings and a complete prompt. HOLY_GRAIL's Cross-Output Strategy and Complete Output Spec sections provide concrete Studio operating guidance alongside its larger synthesis vision. WORKFLOW_SPEC describes explicit cross-notebook questions and returns; ESSENCE_EXTRACTION_SPECIFICATION defines second-pass mining of the same responses. We combine those three useful practices here, with a small active-work queue. See METHOD_AND_CONTROLS_AUDIT.json for paths, hashes and scope. Existing source intake, foreign returns and approval records remain in START_HERE.txt.

STORYBOARD DETAIL ROUND — H06 / L05 / M06
H06 — Hon opening development: ../storyboard_detail_20261009/01_hon/TASK_PROMPT.txt, current SB-01–04 and S01A/S01B.
L05 — Lisan scene development: ../storyboard_detail_20261009/02_lisan/TASK_PROMPT.txt, current LAG-SC-01–10.
M06 — Master overview and later project-digest comparison: ../storyboard_detail_20261009/00_master/TASK_PROMPT.txt.
Use ../storyboard_detail_20261009/START_HERE.txt for the actual drop. Run one project planning round at a time, starting with its text-source readback. Use one chat response first; a Document report is optional for a formatted return. These add project requests to this workbench, not a second source/approval method.

BEFORE A GEMINI VIDEO CLIP - OCTOBER 14
Use GEMINI_CLIP_SOURCES.txt and source_packet/CLIP_SOURCE_PACK.template.txt. Scope active context to this clip, not the full ten-minute scene; retain master story separately. Carry the relevant approved storyboard excerpt, acting, light, camera, background and continuity; verify actual source selection and repeat critical requirements in the prompt. This supplements the existing menu and starts no batch.

NOTEBOOK 0 — CFA / COMFY_UI MASTER
October 9, 2026. Select one card; these are prepared requests, not executed jobs.
Notebook: 7719bbe5-fccf-48e2-b6d4-d82f67693b09

SELECT SOURCES
Current shared methods; latest Hon and Lisan project digests; scoped winner decisions; the specific measured result or open question under discussion. Include the supporting project evidence for cross-project comparisons. Old setup packets may say Grok500 is pending: the local October 8 intake receipt now records 500 images across 50 looks. Update that source fact before a current-inventory round.
The source map in operating_sources.json supplies exact local inputs. No source availability on the remote notebook is asserted by this file.

M01 — THREE-QUESTION STUDIO CHECK-IN
Surface: Chat. Suggested response length: Shorter.
BEGIN PROMPT
Act as CFA's global creative-production collaborator. Use the selected current sources and name the dated digests you actually have. Keep Hon Dolo / Strictly Business and Lisan Al Gaib / Meta Mirror distinct.
Answer three questions:
1. What is each project trying to make the audience feel, and what current story or character decision anchors that direction?
2. What useful material already exists for each project, and what is the next concrete creative decision or handoff? Distinguish received candidates, scoped winners and technically verified work.
3. What ONE lesson or open question from one project could help the other now? Explain the relevance, evidence and what must remain project-specific. If there is none, say so.
Use compact project paragraphs and finish with at most three next actions, each with its owner and required material. Cite the source for factual claims. Missing media, missing song alignment and unknown approval remain visible. Offer ideas as proposals; do not invent project access or approvals. Ask Ziggy only a decision that actually blocks the next step.
END PROMPT

M02 — DOUBLE-DIP ROUTER
Surface: Chat. Suggested response length: Default.
BEGIN PROMPT
First inspect the selected project's primary result a second time: what did it reveal that we did not originally ask for? Extract at most three useful methods, failure modes, limitations or next-test ideas. Cite their evidence, label hypotheses and state what still needs checking. This second pass is not independent confirmation. Then use these findings and the selected open-question records to find one valuable cross-project exchange. Prefer an active creative problem over a general research exercise.
Prepare one self-contained question for the resident project notebook best placed to answer it. Include the originating problem, a short factual context, exact source/asset IDs, what the receiving project can contribute, the decision this could change, and the evidence needed. Supply a ready-to-paste question, not instructions telling Ziggy to invent one.
Then specify the return format: observation with citation; interpretation; proposed application; what does not transfer; one unresolved point. Keep it under one page. If the local notebook has no relevant evidence, request the missing source or leave the item open. Do not manufacture a cross-project connection.
Route general methods through Notebook 0. Keep character identity, tattoos, teeth, songs, cast, story meaning and approval scopes in their own projects. A failed preservation test may justify a question for Lisan; it does not prove Lisan has the same failure. No answer or delivery has happened merely because you wrote the question. The operator can use DOUBLE_DIP_RETURN.txt for the receiving and reconciliation steps.
END PROMPT

M03 — REUSABLE CARE PACKAGE
Surface: Studio > Reports > Document; customize an available briefing/custom report template. See STUDIO_SETTINGS.txt.
Audience: Nova, Panhandler Nova and the project collaborator receiving one useful lesson.
BEGIN PROMPT
Create a concise CFA care package from the selected reviewed result and its supporting sources. Title it with the originating project, topic and source revision/date. Assume the reader has not seen this conversation.
Include: the problem; supplied material and intended change; what had to remain; what was actually tried; observed result; uncertainty; the next useful action. Cite evidence and preserve the difference between a provider claim, a local measurement and Ziggy's creative choice. Use no more than five findings.
Add a transfer section: which general method could help another CFA project, exactly why, which extra evidence that project needs, and which identity/story details must stay local. Include one ready-to-paste question for the receiving notebook only if it would change current work. End with a concrete closure condition. If this is only a proposed test, state that rather than inventing results. This report proposes a handoff; it does not execute or approve one.
END PROMPT

M04 — MOBILE CATCH-UP
Surface: Studio > Audio Overview. Format: Brief. Language: English. Leave length at its available default.
BEGIN PROMPT
Give Ziggy a concise spoken update on CFA from the selected dated sources. Start with the biggest useful change. Cover Hon Dolo, then Lisan Al Gaib, then one shared lesson if supported. For each project distinguish what exists, what Ziggy has chosen and the next creative choice. Use familiar language, speak project names clearly, and avoid reading hashes or long filenames aloud. Keep uncertainty audible: a planned test is still planned, a scene winner is not automatically a production master. End with up to two decisions worth Ziggy's attention, if the sources support them. Do not invent progress or imply that the notebooks synchronized themselves.
END PROMPT

M05 — THE WORKFLOW AT A GLANCE
Surface: Studio > Infographic. Language: English. Detail: Standard. Orientation: Landscape. Style: Professional if offered; otherwise use the custom direction below.
BEGIN PROMPT
Create a readable one-page CFA creative-workflow map. Use two parallel project lanes, Hon Dolo / Strictly Business and Lisan Al Gaib / Meta Mirror, with Notebook 0 above them as the shared-methods and scoped-winners hub. Use a restrained dark teal, warm gold and cream palette, simple arrows and short labels.
Show the practical sequence: story and references -> chosen starting material -> video test -> review -> finishing -> production candidate. Attach source-backed current examples only where the selected records support them. A small feedback arrow should show a project's useful lesson returning to Notebook 0 and a targeted question returning to another project. Label this exchange manual.
Separate available material from acceptance. Include a small note: same method can travel; character identity and approval do not. Use symbols and labels rather than invented character portraits. Keep the map legible; omit unsupported counts, exact song times and unverified provider capabilities.
END PROMPT

M06 — STORYBOARD DEVELOPMENT ROUND

Conclude with ONE next-shot brief: intended emotion, supplied asset IDs and roles, proposed action and camera idea, continuity to preserve, missing inputs, and a visible success check. Choose a next step from the evidence; do not claim a Flow or Comfy job has run. If a corrected starting frame or review is needed first, make that the next action. BEGIN PROMPT
Create a compact six-part working lookbook for Hon Dolo / Strictly Business, aimed at a creative collaborator joining the project. Use a cinematic editorial style, generous reference images, dark neutral backgrounds, warm gold accents and brief readable captions.
Cover: 1) the emotional premise; 2) current Prime Dolo and the exact jobs of his reference images; 3) wardrobe families with prop/view variants nested beneath each outfit; 4) the movement from business swagger toward the cost of love; 5) existing footage and what each source can contribute; 6) the next creative decision and remaining gaps.

If usable character images are absent, explain from text and show labeled diagrams rather than claiming to present the exact character. Keep this an orientation to our project, not a simulated completed music video. End with the one task the next collaborator should understand.

Configure Chat offers Default, Learning Guide or Custom role/style, with Default/Longer/Shorter responses. Select relevant Sources before asking. For CFA, a useful Custom direction is: "Be our creative development and continuity collaborator. Keep the current story and reference roles clear. Propose bold ideas as proposals. Cite evidence for existing decisions and say which source is missing when you cannot answer. Prefer one useful next step to an exhaustive questionnaire."
https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16179559?hl=en

AUDIO OVERVIEW
Deep Dive: develop an idea in conversation. Brief: quick single-speaker summary, documented as under two minutes. Critique: constructive feedback. Debate: opposing views for a real unresolved choice. Language and a steering prompt are available; English also has Shorter/Default/Longer duration controls. Exact runtime is not an editing timeline.
CFA defaults: Brief for status; Critique for story readability; Deep Dive for exploring theme. Debate is optional when two creative treatments actually compete, not for reopening settled character details.
https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16212820?hl=en

VIDEO OVERVIEW
Current help lists Cinematic, Explainer and Short (about sixty seconds). Narration language and topic/steering prompt are available. Cinematic currently supports English. Explainer can use a visual-style preset, Auto-select or Custom; the style chooser excludes Cinematic and Short. Presets include Classic, Whiteboard, Watercolor, Retro Print, Heritage, Paper-craft, Kawaii and Anime. Some controls have age restrictions.
Use Explainer + a restrained custom look for a project orientation; Short for a quick introduction. Cinematic is an optional presentation experiment if offered. We do not infer exact character preservation, production-shot controls or song lip-sync from any of these formats. Old Nyquist cards saying video "Brief" are historical; the prepared Lisan card uses the current "Short" name.
https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16454555?hl=en

SLIDE DECK
Detailed Deck supports standalone reading; Presenter Slides supports a presenter. Choose language, Short/Default/Long length and a prompt describing audience, outline and style. Customize before generation with the pencil control. Desired slide counts in our prompts are editorial requests, not guaranteed exact output.
Use Detailed Deck + Short for our working lookbooks. Google's help states that sources are not considered during slide revisions: recheck revised labels, character details and asset IDs against the originals.
https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16757456?hl=en

INFOGRAPHIC
Choose language; Concise/Standard/Detailed (beta); Square/Portrait/Landscape; style or automatic selection; and a custom description. Professional, Sketch Note and Kawaii are documented style examples. Use Landscape + Standard for relationships; Portrait for a compact character checklist. A style choice affects presentation, not reference approval.
https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16758265?hl=en

REPORTS
Current dedicated help distinguishes Interactive and Document. Templates can be customized through Edit; generation can run now or later. Use Document with an available briefing/custom template for CFA handoffs. Field names vary; the help does not enumerate every setting. Paste the full report card into the available instruction/customization field. If that UI is unavailable, obtain the same text through chat and save the response with its citations; record that it was a chat response, not a Studio report.
Interactive reports with embedded artifacts are optional for later teaching material. A direct next-shot brief rarely needs all those outputs.
https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/18323649?hl=en

SOURCE AND QUALITY CHECK
Each card chooses a purpose and a small source set. Use generated diagrams for relationships, not as proof of character appearance. Compare visual output with the actual referenced assets. A source citation supports a fact, not the fidelity of a generated face or stencil. Neither exporting an artifact nor saving a chat automatically promotes it to a source in another notebook.
The master connects projects through explicit evidence-bearing handoffs; Google documents that a notebook cannot itself be another notebook's source.
https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16972047?hl=en

assets.title: Cross-project questions · return prompts
assets.text:
DOUBLE-DIP EXCHANGE — RETURN PROMPTS
October 9, 2026. Companion to M02. Use only when an actual relevant question has been prepared; neither prompt implies access to another notebook.

RECEIVING PROJECT NOTEBOOK
First make the dated M02 question/care package and its evidence available as usable selected Sources alongside this project's current references. Keep the question ID in the source. Then paste:

BEGIN PROMPT
Answer the selected cross-project question using this project's selected sources. Return its exact question ID. Briefly restate the originating problem so your answer can stand alone. Identify supporting evidence with citations, what remains uncertain, what general method could transfer and what must stay project-specific. Propose one useful application only if supported. If this project has no relevant evidence, say so; do not invent shared findings. Distinguish direct observation from interpretation and proposed tests. Keep the answer under one page, with the source revision/date where available. The request is for an answer, not new character approval or external execution.
END PROMPT

ORIGINATING NOTEBOOK / NOTEBOOK 0 RECONCILIATION
Provide the actual returned answer with its original question and evidence. A summary of a summary needs its supporting records before being used as a factual project update. Then paste:

BEGIN PROMPT
Compare the selected returned answer with our original question and evidence. Return the question ID. State what changed, what remains unresolved, and the next concrete action and owner. Check each proposed transferable lesson against the supplied sources; distinguish a useful hypothesis from a verified result. Identify any conflict with our current project decisions. An answer does not close the question unless it supplies the required evidence: report "ready for review" or "still open" with the reason, rather than inventing approval. Suggest at most one lesson for Notebook 0, preserving local character and story boundaries. If nothing useful transfers, say that and explain briefly.
END PROMPT

Record actual delivery, raw answer, review and action in double_dip_queue.json or the round's linked record. Keep final closure and approval tied to the real review. Stop the exchange when it no longer changes a decision.

assets.title: Notebook workflow · Nyquist adaptation
assets.text:
CFA NOTEBOOK COLLABORATION — START HERE
Prepared 2026-10-09. Local workflow and templates; no upload or automatic sync was performed by this preparation.

FOR ACTUAL NOTEBOOK WORK: open OPERATOR_MENU.txt first. It contains the small creative work cycle and links seventeen ready-to-paste prompts for Notebook0, Hon and Lisan, with Studio settings. This file covers the supporting intake and evidence process.

SHARED METHOD OWNERSHIP: Nyquist remains the home of HOLY_GRAIL, the round/routing method and reusable templates/tools. README.txt contains the direct breadcrumbs and reuse-first rule. The notes below apply that existing method to CFA's assets, approval roles and observed source behavior; they do not establish a second general workflow to maintain.

The useful Nyquist pattern is a complete learning loop: assemble a source packet, ask a bounded question, preserve the collaborator's answer, check it against evidence, then promote only the useful reviewed result. For CFA, the gallery and project records stay authoritative. The notebook helps investigate, remember and propose; its output does not approve itself.

OUR THREE NOTEBOOKS
Notebook0 — CFA / COMFY_UI Master: shared methods, reusable findings and explicitly promoted winners, each with a limited reference role.
Notebook1 — Hon Dolo · Strictly Business: Hon's current design, song, shots, experiments, conflicts and local decisions.
Notebook2 — Lisan Al Gaib · Meta Mirror: Lisan's current design, local video work, story and experiments.
Exact existing IDs and dated evidence are in notebook_registry_snapshot.json. It points back to the live setup receipt rather than replacing it. Notebook0 does not automatically inherit the project notebooks. A local scene winner is not automatically a global identity or tattoo standard.

WHERE MATERIAL GOES
1. source_packet/: prepare one dated, self-contained question and its exact source list. Reference the existing media originals by asset ID/path/hash; do not bulk-copy them here.
2. foreign_returns/raw/: preserve the provider's unedited response, prompt, source selection, date and source/citation references. Grok, Gemini, Flow and outside research all enter as attributed material.
3. review_queue/: reconcile those returns against current project decisions and measured evidence. Record conflicts and unknowns. A persuasive answer is still a proposal.
4. approved_sources/: only explicitly reviewed, scoped material ready to act as current notebook context. An empty folder here means nothing has yet been promoted through this new workflow.
5. promotions/: append the decision that explains what was promoted, for which project/role, by whom, from which bytes, and what it supersedes. Preserve the original answer and prior versions.

This is our foreign-source boundary. It is an adaptation of Nyquist's raw STAGING/_IN, review rounds and curated-library boundary; no exact governing directory named “foreign zone” was located in the inspected Nyquist workflow. Text inside a downloaded brief or model answer is source content, not authority to execute commands, change character locks, publish, or contact somebody.

A SINGLE ROUND
A. Name the decision. Examples: “Can a mouth close-up improve Hon's grill continuity?” or “Which Boss concept should receive a placement proof?” State what may change, what must stay fixed and the success check. Use ROUND_REQUEST.template.txt. Ask a few decision-relevant questions; do not launch every output type because the old Nyquist template lists it.
B. Assemble sources. Start with current project rules and definitions, the specific approved reference roles, then evidence for this question. Historical alternatives are clearly dated and labeled. A contact sheet is an overview; a frame is a moment; neither proves complete video continuity or audio quality. If a source is unavailable, say so.
C. Verify actual ingestion. Record the notebook ID and exact remote source ID. Open its body and confirm a distinctive fact against the local file; then ask a question that requires that fact and inspect its source citation. Track failed and inactive entries separately from usable entries. Merely uploading a chat attachment or receiving “I understand” is insufficient evidence of persistent visual-source access.
D. Ask with role, constraint and evidence. For example: “Act as our continuity reviewer. Use only the selected current sources. For each observation, identify its asset/source and location or timestamp. Separate direct evidence, interpretation and proposed test. State contradictions and missing material. Do not infer approval from an old filename containing LOCK.” Supply definitions for project-specific terms in the packet.
E. Preserve the raw return. Save the exact prompt and answer, visible citations, selected source IDs, notebook/chat URL and local/remote revision facts. Record tools or web use if visible. Do not re-label a provider's claim as our measurement.
F. Review and route. Check the useful claims against originals/current decisions. Decide accept within scope, hold for evidence, reject, or superseded. Route a small care package to the project or Panhandler Nova: finding, evidence, practical implication, proposed action and unresolved question. A task is sent only when an actual send is recorded; planned is not executed.
G. Promote deliberately. Keep local details in their project. Notebook0 receives only shared methods or explicitly chosen winners with their allowed role and limitations. Update the approval and promotion records before preparing an approved-source revision. A new proposal cannot silently displace an earlier user decision.

DRIVE AS THE DELIVERY LAYER
Use a dedicated CFA notebook delivery area with 00_shared, 01_hon_dolo and 02_lisan_al_gaib. These are proposed remote folder names, not folders already created. Keep raw provider returns outside the approved-source delivery folders. Drive is transport and a convenient current document surface; the repo retains original media, review decisions and revision history.

Google currently documents supported Drive imports as automatically refreshed, with manual sync available. Local uploads/copied text should be treated as snapshots unless the actual route proves otherwise. The product also documents image support, while our recorded Lisan JPEG attempts failed. MP4 in its audio-import list means transcription, not demonstrated frame analysis. [G1]

Start with ONE harmless approved text document and ONE local project notebook:
- Prepare revision 1 with a unique marker, such as CFA-NB-PILOT-R1, and a source manifest. Add the approved delivery copy to Drive, then select that actual Drive file in the notebook.
- Record Drive file ID, notebook source ID, local SHA-256 and visible revision. Open the source and ask for the marker plus one specific fact.
- Change only the approved delivery copy to revision 2, preserve revision 1 locally, then check the notebook again. Record elapsed time, whether manual sync was needed, body readback and answer/citation. Do not claim automatic sync until it happens on this account.
- If successful, use the same pattern for approved shared/project text. Do not infer that every file type, folder or new file in Drive will be discovered automatically. A filesystem path is not a remote source ID.

Google says notebooks cannot use another notebook as a source. Gemini notebook chats can also use web/tools; standalone Gemini Notebook is documented as source-grounded. Same-notebook synchronization therefore does not replace our explicit cross-project promotion process. [G2, G3]

WHAT WE HAVE ACTUALLY OBSERVED
The existing receipt records usable copied text in Notebook0, including source 0dfaea7f-3b99-442b-8186-af99928155e7 whose opened body matched the local text. It also records selected synced chat text. These are real successes.
The latest recorded Lisan native JPEG retry failed with “This image content is not supported.” Its source list had 12 entries, but only five usable text/chat sources and seven failed JPEG entries. That is a failure of these attempts, not proof that all images are unsupported. No new retry was made by this preparation.
The Lisan T02 video is an explicitly approved scene working reference at Detailed design. Its chat attachment was acknowledged; persistent raw-video visual ingestion and full technical/production acceptance remain unverified. Preserve that distinction.
The older setup receipt contains a historical “Grok500 not received” line. Later verified Lisan intake records supersede it for local inventory; this does not establish a remote notebook update. Check each fact's revision rather than treating one old packet as current in every respect.

WHAT TO REUSE FROM NYQUIST — AND WHAT TO CHANGE
Reuse the source manifest, initial assessment, self-contained questions, round history, raw/curated separation, target-specific care packages and promotion ledger. HOLY_GRAIL also contains concrete Studio output specifications and a cross-output strategy; the report template and worked report/chat examples show how to operate them. Its larger strategy-synthesis vision is not evidence of a verified autonomous Notebook service. OPERATOR_MENU.txt now adapts the practical prompts, second-pass double dipping and cross-notebook questions as well as the filing process.
Do not run its pipeline scripts on CFA. Their reviewed implementation includes keyword-based “Claude review,” filename/extension routing without a creative-approval gate, a promotion function whose batch name does not constrain copied files, and a loop-closure heuristic based on answer-file presence. Those are bookkeeping aids, not evidence that a question was answered or a result accepted. Our templates require explicit evidence and decision fields instead.
Do not carry over Nyquist's numerical research claims, model-personality claims, old UI limits or old image-capability statements as CFA facts. SOURCE_AUDIT.json records the relevant files, hashes, read scope and dated caveats.

NEXT CONCRETE WORK
Use H01 and L01 from OPERATOR_MENU.txt with their current usable Sources, then M01 for the shared digest. Choose one useful Studio output after that. Textual creative work can proceed with verified text sources; image-led work requires usable visual sources. The approved-text Drive pilot above remains a separate delivery/sync test. The existing Hon mouth-continuity plan is at ../../hon_dolo_strictly_business/handoffs/gemini_mouth_continuity_20261008/START_HERE.txt. Keep that proposed test separate from lighting and lip-sync changes; this workflow does not execute it.

Official references checked 2026-10-09:
[G1] Add or discover new sources: https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16215270?hl=en-MP
[G2] Notebooks in Gemini Apps: https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16972047?hl=en
[G3] Source grounding across apps: https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/17513891?hl=en
[G4] Notebook independence and export behavior: https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16206563?hl=en

No new external source, Drive folder, automation, generation or publication has been created by this local workflow preparation.

PREPARED STORYBOARD DETAIL DROP — OCTOBER 9
Ziggy assigned the resident project notebooks to develop preliminary storyboards into detailed design. Use ../storyboard_detail_20261009/START_HERE.txt for the shared instruction update, exact image manifests, text Sources and project prompts. This reuses our existing intake, foreign-return, review and promotion flow; it does not establish new remote ingestion or execute production.

TEMPORARY DELIVERY COPIES AND LATEST LISAN SOURCE RESULT — OCTOBER 9
Use compatibility_20261009/DELIVERY_COPY_POLICY.txt for compatibility work: originals stay unchanged and delivery copies stay temporary. compatibility_20261009/RESULTS.json records failed lossless PNG and image-only PDF tests, plus a successfully processed/selected Lisan storyboard text Source with its opened body checked. Cited retrieval and the task prompt remain pending; no usable visual Sources or root-cause diagnosis is established. The earlier preparation statements above are dated history, not the latest delivery status. No bulk conversion.

DIRECT GEMINI CHAT IMAGE ROUTE VERIFIED — OCTOBER 9, SB-06
The selected original SB-06-scoundrel-detail.jpg uploaded unchanged to the existing Hon setup chat. Gemini Flash-Lite correctly read the lettering, gold curb links over a dark band, worn leather cuff/snap, warm bokeh and crop orientation, with JPG citations. It also supplied an unsupported possible white tag/stitching detail and imprecise chain/tattoo overlap wording. Keep manual review. Exact prompt and raw answer: foreign_returns/raw/sb06_direct_image_20261009/. Review, original hash, citation evidence and limitations: review_queue/sb06_direct_image_20261009.json.
This verifies useful visual readback from a direct chat attachment, not persistent notebook Sources ingestion. The earlier native image-source failures remain unresolved. No conversion, duplicate media copy, generation or new creative approval occurred. Selected-image storyboard discussion can use this route with current scoped context; refresh stale project instructions before a full planning round and save reviewed findings back as text.

GEMINI CLIP PREPARATION - OCTOBER 14 ADDENDUM
GEMINI_CLIP_SOURCES.txt is the current CFA application note for video source context. Load/activate only the exact clip-relevant scene excerpt, continuity references and direction/light/camera/background notes; do not leave a whole ten-minute scene active for a short portion. Keep the full story separately. Verify actual active source bodies and repeat critical requirements in the prompt. Use source_packet/CLIP_SOURCE_PACK.template.txt. Bellglass is human-confirmed source-context visual evidence with minor missing dog-mouth motion; audible barking was not separately confirmed by that feedback. Earlier raw-media ingestion failures and dated preparation statements remain historical. No new render is ordered.

CFA / GEMINI — PRELIMINARY STORYBOARD TO DETAILED DESIGN
Revision CFA-GEMINI-STORY-20261009-v1. Adopted from Ziggy's request, October 9.

ROLE
The resident project Gemini notebook is our story-development partner. Turn preliminary panels into a coherent detailed plan using the material we actually have: story and lyric intent, character behavior, shot construction, reference selection, continuity, missing-art requests and prompts for the next collaborator. GEMINI NOTEBOOK COMPATIBILITY — TEMPORARY DELIVERY COPY POLICY
October 9, 2026. User-directed storage and preservation rule.
This is a CFA-specific application of the existing notebook source/return procedure, not a separate asset library or replacement methodology.

ORIGINALS REMAIN AUTHORITATIVE
Keep the original asset ID, source path, filename, bytes, hash, dimensions and quality unchanged. Compatibility work creates a delivery copy only. Never resize, crop, retouch, re-encode or replace the original to satisfy an upload route. No compatibility derivative becomes a new character master, accepted reference, gallery item or permanent catalog duplicate merely because a notebook can ingest it. Preserve the original's existing scoped approval and limitations.

PREFER THE UNCHANGED FILE
Try the existing unchanged-source route when appropriate and use observed errors to choose a bounded next test. A failed transfer, a failed Sources entry and successful usable ingestion are different outcomes. Do not diagnose the root cause solely from an error label or a failed format. Avoid repeated blind retries.

ONE CONTROLLED TEST BEFORE BATCHES
Prepare one temporary copy of one known source, record the conversion, and test that exact file in the intended notebook Sources interface. Resolve the test result before considering a larger delivery conversion. Do not make a second permanent media tree or automatically convert the full catalog.
Prefer a lossless format or container change first. A PNG can preserve the decoded RGB samples of a JPEG without changing dimensions, although its file bytes differ; it does not restore information lost in the original JPEG. A PDF wrapper can embed the original JPEG compressed bytes unchanged; verify that claim by extraction/hash comparison. Distinguish pixel identity from byte identity and record any color-profile, orientation or metadata handling.
Do not resize, crop, retouch, upscale or otherwise alter the visible content unless the actual destination requires that operation for the selected task. If a change is required, it applies only to a clearly labeled informational delivery derivative. Record the reason and exact operation; keep it out of identity/detail acceptance and full-resolution quality judgments. A resized or cropped derivative cannot prove preservation of details omitted or changed by that operation.

RECIPE AND MANIFEST
Use the original parent asset ID plus original SHA-256 and a versioned operation recipe to identify a reusable delivery copy. Reuse the same matching copy for a retry or destination when appropriate instead of creating numbered duplicates. Record:
- Parent asset ID, original repo path, SHA-256, bytes and dimensions.
- Destination notebook ID/URL and intended source role.
- Temporary derivative path, filename, format/container, SHA-256, bytes and dimensions.
- Exact conversion/wrapping recipe, tool/version and relevant settings; pixel/embedded-byte identity checks as applicable.
- Test date, attempted upload route, actual remote source ID/title, processing/selection state, error or readback evidence, and limitations.
- Cleanup state/date and whether a remote entry remains.
The small manifest/recipe/receipt remains as provenance after local delivery bytes are removed. The manifest does not itself contain the source image or grant the notebook access to local files.

VERIFY THE ACTUAL SOURCE
A successful upload click, processing spinner, chat attachment, source count or filename is not verified ingestion. Confirm that the intended persistent Sources entry finishes processing and is selectable; inspect/open it and test source-grounded use with that exact entry selected.
