Narrative resolution; solitary dominance over the empty Jedi institution.
3. Visual Style and Production Language
Lighting and Palette

Dichotomy of Environments: The video operates across four distinct visual palettes:

Crimson Studio Cyc: High-saturation red flat background with neutral white key-light on performer, emulating contemporary hip-hop performance videos (e.g., ColorsxStudios or standard rap performance vignettes).

High-Key Infinite Void: Bleached 100% white background isolating Mace Windu, stripping all context to emphasize slapstick physical failure.

Golden-Hour Council Chamber: Warm orange/magenta sunset palette penetrating curved floor-to-ceiling panoramic glass, casting long directional shadows and warm rim light on the subject’s face and neck.

Grim Imperial Bridge / Desaturated Scrubland: Cool steely grays, deep blacks, and desaturated olive-brown ground with isolated practical orange fire.

Production Setups vs. Narrative Inserts

Performance setups account for roughly 40% of runtime (red mic cyc, desert walk, solo council chamber rapping).

Narrative/gag inserts account for roughly 60% (falling Windu, taped Windu, Yoda choking, Tusken head display, Star Destroyer bridge).

The pacing cuts sharply on 2-bar and 4-bar phrasing, intensifying into rapid 1-bar cuts during the hook repetitions.

Audio-Visual Alignment

The soundtrack features a mid-tempo trap beat (sub-bass 808s, rolling hi-hats, hard snare claps, and pitched vocal melodies). Cuts reliably snap to the snare crack on beat 2 and beat 4 during verses, while chorus transitions introduce sudden high-contrast visual cuts (e.g., swapping red studio directly for stark white void) on the downbeat.

5. Transferable Techniques for Hon Dolo and Lisan Al Gaib
Technique 1: The High-Contrast Minimalist Gag Void

On-Screen Reference: Mace Windu falling endlessly in a completely unlit, pure white void (00:15–00:19, 01:08–01:09).

Why It Works: Eliminating 3D environment rendering bypasses complex scene composition while instantly elevating a comedic gag through hyper-focused physical isolation.

Proposed Reproduction Test for Nova/Ziggy:

For Hon Dolo / Strictly Business: Place a photorealistic Greedo in a pure high-key white or stark neon-green void flailing backward continuously in slow motion after being shot under the table.

Pilot Test: Generate a 3-second looping plate of an isolated character tumbling against #FFFFFF, composite subtle motion blur, and intercut with tight performance shots every 2 bars during the chorus.

Technique 2: Iconic Pop-Culture Prop Subversion

On-Screen Reference: Duct-taped Mace Windu in the Jedi Council chair (01:03–01:06) and the severed Tusken Raider mask presented during a romantic close-up (01:27–01:29).

Why It Works: Collides high-lore sci-fi solemnity with mundane hardware-store absurdity (duct tape) or macabre humor (treating a severed alien head like a bouquet).

Proposed Reproduction Test for Nova/Ziggy:

For Lisan Al Gaib / Meta Mirror: Frame Paul Atreides holding an ornate royal spice hookah or an absurdly branded everyday consumer beverage container during a solemn Sietch council gathering.

Pilot Test: Create a single still keyframe of a reverent desert figure bound to a stone throne with modern hazard tape or zip-ties; verify that the visual read is immediate and comical without breaking cinematic lighting.

Technique 3: Streetwear / Sci-Fi Armor Hybridization

On-Screen Reference: Helmetless Darth Vader suit combined with modern styled undercut hair, face tattoos, heavy chain, and unbuttoned cape flair (00:46–00:55, 01:31–01:33).

Why It Works: Preserves 80% of recognizable canon armor silhouettes while swapping the remaining 20% (head/accessories) with contemporary hip-hop tropes, creating an instantly readable parody archetype.

Proposed Reproduction Test for Nova/Ziggy:

For Hon Dolo: Dress Han Solo in his classic holster and vest, but replace the inner shirt with an oversized designer graphic hoodie, gold Corellian bloodstripe chain, and modern designer sneakers.

Pilot Test: Render a 2-second turnaround of the character walking toward camera; evaluate whether silhouette recognition holds from a distance before facial details resolve.

6. Unknowns and High-Priority Frames for Detailed Inspection
Production Unknowns

Source Generation Pipeline: Unclear whether character plates were generated via full-frame video diffusion (e.g., Runway Gen-2 / Kling / Sora equivalents) or via synthetic image LoRA generations animated through LivePortrait/Wav2Lip face-reenactment on top of live-action reference footage.

Plate Compositing Method: The Star Destroyer bridge and Jedi Council backgrounds could either be real-time Unreal Engine 5 virtual production plates or 2D matte paintings composited in post (After Effects / Nuke) with 2.5D camera projection.

Highest-Value Target Frames for Micro-Inspection

Frame 00:29 (Extreme Close-Up Eye Wink): Inspect for pixel interpolation artifacts around the eyelid crease and iris edge to determine if the wink was generated natively by diffusion or keyframed via 2D morphing.

Frame 01:05 (Duct-Taped Mace Windu Face): Inspect tape reflections and skin occlusion around the lips to see if tape specular highlights move with facial animation or remain static texture maps.

Frame 01:19 (Yoda Choking Interaction): Examine the contact point between the black leather gauntlet and Yoda’s neck foam/flesh to assess physical intersection depth and neural deformation limits.

assets.text:
JET BLACK - THE FREELY SHARED BLUEPRINT
CFA-LAG-JET-STORY-20261009-R1 | October 9, 2026

Jet brings a blueprint made freely available to everyone, helping them unlock their capabilities. The user confirmed that wording. He is Lisan's watcher and recurring guide: he explains accomplishments, briefs the mission, and returns with progress reports and messages from the outer world. He fictionally personifies Codex's enabling role in Ziggy's creative work. Lisan makes the choices and takes action.

WHERE TO BROWSE
Open the project dashboard, choose Lisan > Storyboard > Shot progress. Five preliminary cards connect existing Jet material to arrival, blueprint briefing, mission launch, progress report and next dispatch. Mission launch is under Placement still needed. The other links are proposed semantic associations, not assigned song timings or replacements for the 50 source panels. In Supporting cast, Jet has one collection with source references, selected story candidates, other proposals and historical variants.

WHAT IS CONFIRMED
The premise, relationship and recurring story function are user decisions. The two original supplied images remain Jet's visual references with their recorded hand, suit, insignia and cube variations. The received Curator lore is provider-proposed history, not the current story authority.

WHAT STILL NEEDS DEVELOPMENT
The concrete quest, form of the blueprint, message sender and wording, dialogue, final placements and timings remain open. Six existing images were inspected for staging. Their defects are recorded in storyline.json: they are useful composition candidates, not finished frames or new identity masters. Lisan retains his current face, natural-teeth default and scoped optional accessories.

FILES AND NEXT ACTION
- storyline.json: canonical user direction, five planning cards, exact image IDs/hashes, continuity notes and semantic placement suggestions.
- STORYBOARD_HANDOFF.txt: prepared Gemini/Notebook story-development request using our existing workflow. Progress report and next dispatch are two possible instances of its fourth function.
- ../../scene_map.json: original 50 source panels, plus a pointer to this thread. No source scene or approved timing was replaced.
- ../../../visual_library/shot_materials.json: dashboard material links and next actions.

The handoff is prepared locally, not sent. Old storyboard ZIPs and previously uploaded text sources predate this addendum; include the current instructions and this story record on the next handoff. No new images, audio, video, paid jobs or publishing happened in this integration.

assets.title: Hon · Decisions and later refinements
assets.text:
# Decisions on writer's pass 001 — October 10, 2026

Recorded by Claude, lead writer, from Ziggy's direct answers in the active session on the evening of October 10 (America/New_York). These are the author's decisions; the weave in section 2 is my proposal built on them. `WRITER_PASS_001.md` is left exactly as posted (its hash in mailbox message `dde4a37a` stays valid); this file records what changes.

## 1. Author clarification: Leia is there from the first verse

Ziggy: the woman referred to in the very first verse, the one with money to spare, **is Leia**. She is not a late arrival in the song; the first Verse 2 only makes explicit what the first verse already assumes. My note that "the song puts her in the first Verse 2" was wrong about the song and right about the board: Grok's 36 panels still show no Leia before the farewell.

That clarification, and the correction to note 1 of the pass, is the creative-read update for CFA Nova to reconcile into `shot_plan.json` and the project README when she next touches them; I have not edited either. Everything below it is my inference, not Ziggy's statement.

## 2. The weave (my proposal, answering Ziggy's question 1)

My inference: if the first-verse woman with money is Leia, then the price in the first chorus and the verse's demand for payment are most naturally sung to her, which makes the opening prototype's "one implied offscreen customer" Leia. Nothing in the prototype's locked frame changes (one visible Dolo, four credits, the indicator, silent); only who is on the other side of the counter. And if Leia is the customer, the informant cannot also be the customer. She has a better job: she is the reason Leia finds him.

- **Prologue, the cab.** The unnamed informant boards Dolo's cab (the four-beat cab storyboard, external-off mouth and lip hoops exactly as her brief states). Her information, silent in the first proof and written later, is the tip: a princess needs a ride off this rock and has money. He drops her and goes to the counter. She does not appear inside the song.
- **S01, the counter.** Leia across the counter, offscreen in the locked frame. The fare is the first chorus. He is selling a ride to the woman with money.
- **S02, the verse.** Sung to her: the creditors behind the boast are why the price is the price.
- **S03, the glance.** Mid-count his eyes leave the credits and go to her, the first time he looks at her as a person and not a payer. S03A records a glance toward the cockpit exit; Ziggy accepted my proposal that it goes to Leia instead (question 6). Where she stands when it lands, at the door or across the counter, follows the weave and is pending with it.
- **S04, the junky home.** She has paid; she boards; one eyebrow at the ship; the protection promise and the fee in the same breath.

Ziggy answered "yes" to the informant as the opening customer before this weave was written. The weave keeps her in the opening scene (the cab) and moves the counter seat to Leia. If he would rather the informant sit at the counter and Leia be only talked about, the pass works either way; this file records the version I recommend.

## 3. Answers to the six questions

| # | Question | Answer | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Frame story: cab → counter → video → thaw → quarters | Liked, with the Leia question above | Weave in section 2; order unchanged |
| 2 | Informant as the opening customer | Yes | Reinterpreted per section 2: informant in the cab, Leia at the counter; author to confirm |
| 3 | Scene-card order S07, S10, S04, S02, S05/S08 | TBD, fine for now | S07 card written first (`SCENE_CARD_S07.md`); the rest wait |
| 4 | Outro treatment | Restrained, for now | Frame C, Chewie holds the room, names arrive as sound; desert and card parked |
| 5 | SB-30 thaw | Yes, to the frame | Thaw opens the epilogue, before the quarters scene; not in the song |
| 6 | S03 glance | My proposal | Glance goes to Leia (accepted); whether she is at the door or across the counter follows the weave (pending) |

## 4. Deltas to WRITER_PASS_001 (apply when the pass is next consolidated)

- Section 1, note 1: replace "the song puts her in the first Verse 2" with the clarification above; keep "the board has no Leia until the farewell."
- Section 2, rows S01–S04: S03's glance goes to Leia (accepted). Leia as the offscreen customer in S01, S02 sung to her and the glance landing across the counter are pending confirmation of the weave; S04 unchanged.
- Section 4: the recommendation stands; the informant is the cab passenger and the tip, not the counter customer.
- Section 7: resolved as in section 3 of this file; order of cards after S07 still open.

## 5. Still open

- Confirmation of the weave (section 2) or the alternative.
- Card order after S07.
- Whether the informant returns in the epilogue as a witness (not required by anything).

## 6. New input, same evening: more than one version of the song (undecided)

Ziggy, with a full disclaimer that he has not decided: he has at least two recordings of the song he cannot choose between, possibly a third and a fourth. One idea is to use one for the arena he is competing in and another for his art channel, in a different flavor; another is that the versions could be the Multiverse Dolo device, so the same lyrics get more than one shot at telling a larger story, with the lyrics possibly varying slightly between versions.

Record only: two recordings already exist in CFA's music intake (the October 4 and October 7 masters, with different lengths and different audio, same written words). Any further versions are not yet on disk.

My recommendation, for Ziggy to accept or reject, not a decision:

1. **Finish one first.** The spine, the scene cards and every lock are version-independent as long as the words are the same; what changes per version is timing, lip-sync audio and flavor. The acceptance bottleneck is already the whole project's bottleneck. One version accepted end to end teaches us more than two half-done; call it the Prime cut.
2. **Then the versions are cheap, not expensive.** Because the cards are written to frames and motifs, a second version can reuse the same cards with a different look (the Multiverse armor-swap lane already exists as a scoped collection), a different set dressing or a different cut rhythm, and only the lip-sync inserts have to be remade. That is exactly what the Multiverse device is for: same man, same words, different world, and the audience sees a larger story across versions.
3. **The lyrics should not drift between versions unless the story needs it.** A changed word is a changed lock (the lyric master is the source for every card). If Ziggy wants variants, each variant needs its own lyric master file and its own section map, and the spine notes which sections differ.
4. **One version per channel is a distribution decision, not a story decision.** The story can be the same; the flavor sells the channel.

Nothing in this section changes a file or a plan. It is here so the next session knows the question exists.

## 7. Answers of October 11, 2026 (afternoon, America/New_York)

Recorded from Ziggy's direct replies in the session after the Prime handoff and the S10 card were posted (mailbox message `00181b08`).

| # | Question | Answer | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | The weave (section 2): Leia across the counter in S01, the informant as the cab passenger and the tip | **Yes, confirmed** | The "pending the weave" flags in `WRITER_PASS_001.md`, `STORYBOARD_UPDATE_20261011.md` (S01 and S03 rows) and the S10 card are resolved in Ziggy's favor of the weave as written. Those posted files keep their hashes; this row is the record. Creative-read update for CFA Nova: S01's implied offscreen customer is Leia; the S03 glance lands on her across the counter. |

# Storyboard update — October 11, 2026

Author: Claude, lead writer. Status: **proposal**; `shot_plan.json` and the 36 panels are untouched. This consolidates what changed since writer's pass 001 (Ziggy's decisions, the Prime master, the new lyric text) into one working spine, a list of panel work to request, and the map of what the rescoring must deliver to which cards. Timing is still null everywhere: the Prime master has not had its listening pass.

## 1. What changed since pass 001

- **Prime is finalized**: `Hon_DoLo.mp3` in the project folder (the trap cut, "the one you'd hear on the radio today"), with its lyric text `Hon_DoLo.txt`. Hashes, duration and the handoff record are in `PRIME_HANDOFF_20261011.md`. Everything times to this file now; the October 4 and October 7 masters are history.
- **The lyric text changed in five of twelve sections.** The words are the author's; the record is below. The one change that touches a card: the first bridge is rewritten to match the second, the lightspeed "88" line is gone, and "punch it" now lands in both bridges. The project README's note that the 88 reference "can remain an optional joke", and the shot plan's line that the 88 and Captain Falcon references remain lyrical jokes, are void as far as 88 goes; Captain Falcon is still in Verse 2.
- **Leia is in the song from the first verse** (Ziggy, October 10). The weave: the informant is the cab passenger and the tip in the prologue; Leia is the customer across the counter in the opening; the S03 glance goes to her. Ziggy said yes to the informant in the opening and to the glance; the exact seating is my inference and stays flagged until he says so in as many words.
- **Decided:** outro restrained; the thaw moves to the frame story; S07 first. Card order after S07 is still TBD ("fine for now"); S10 is my proposed next and is written below as a proposal.

## 2. Lyric text: section-by-section record (new file against `lyrics.user.v002.txt`)

| Section | Change | Card effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| S01 chorus | none | none |
| S02 verse | three small deliveries: the "scruffy" repeat dropped; a possessive on "Fleet's"; "my my my" before the junky ship | none; cue words unchanged |
| S03 chorus | none | none |
| S04 Verse 2 | "This is" for "it is"; "maybe" dropped before "depravity"; "HER" capitalized | none |
| S05 bridge | **rewritten** to the second bridge's wording with "punch it" added; the 88 / light-speed line is gone | the lightspeed lever idea now sits on "punch it" literally; the 88 joke leaves the unresolved list |
| S06 chorus | none | none |
| S07 Verse 2 | none | none; the beat stop after the line "Man, don't start." (the Prime style prompt's "Don't start" stop) is the hinge beat for S07-3/S07-4 |
| S08 bridge | "punch it" added before the last line; the last line now ends in an exclamation mark | S08A's throttle push lands on "punch it" |
| S09 chorus | none | none |
| S10 Verse 3 | "ICE!" emphasized | none |
| S11 final chorus | none | none |
| S12 outro | none | none |

Recommendation to CFA Nova: register `Hon_DoLo.txt` as lyric master v003 in `shot_plan.json` (`lyrics_source`), with its hash, and retire v002 to history. Every card refers to sections, so no card text changes; the section line ranges in the shot plan need recounting against the new file.

## 3. The working spine, with the decisions applied

Four recurring frames: **A** the counter, **B** the cockpit, **C** the boards, **D** the chamber. Three cutting motifs: hands on money become hands on controls; Chewie's look; the mouth, external-off throughout the song.

| Section | Beat | Shots | Hand-off |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Prologue (frame, no song) | The tip | The cab arrival four-beat board: the informant waits, boards, sits; the first exchange with Dolo at the controls, silent. | Cut to the counter as the first chorus starts. |
| S01 chorus | The price | Mouth insert (SB-01, external-off). Cantina wide: Chewie at the boards behind the room (SB-05, new). Frame A, the ten-turn prototype as reviewed: the count, the fuel gesture, the half-smile. Leia as the offscreen customer (pending Ziggy's confirmation of the weave). | Hard cut on the half-smile to the creditor. |
| S02 verse | The creditors behind the boast, sung to her | S02A Jabba's room. S02B Boba, motionless. Frame B (S02C): the captain line; neck-blaster insert on the "my name" cue; one club cut-in (SB-08, new). S02D: the junky ship banks once; parsec graphic; one Maw wide. | The bank hands the eye back to frame A. |
| S03 chorus | The first doubt | Frame A, one change: mid-count his eyes leave the credits and go to her (change to S03A; the glance to Leia is accepted, her position across the counter is pending the weave). | Cut on the glance. |
| S04 Verse 2 | A home and a crew | S04A Leia looks around the junky home. Frame B: Dolo defends the ship; the chest ship (SB-17, upright). S04C: the promise, the softened face, the fee in the same breath. Last, on "drop that beat": frame C, Chewie's fader (S04B). | Hold the softened face one beat too long. The fader hands to the ignition. |
| S05 bridge | Ignition as swagger | Straps; the overhead lever on "punch it" (the lightspeed idea, now literal); thrusters. | Thrusters wipe to frame C. |
| S06 chorus | Chewie sees through him | Frame C, Chewie looking at Dolo, not the boards (S06A). Hold through the question. | Cut to the crates. |
| S07 Verse 2 | The clean exit and the choice | As `SCENE_CARD_S07.md`: the cut (credits in the case), the kid's channel cut, the hover (the beat stop after "Man, don't start." falls here), the look, the levers, the grin, the turn (S07B). | The turn cuts to the hands. |
| S08 bridge | Same speed, changed purpose | The three inserts, committed; S08A the throttle all the way on "punch it"; the ship, already turned, accelerates. | Lands on frame B. |
| S09 chorus | The question has an answer | Frame B, battle light moving across his face. Performing, not selling. | Black on the last "around"; then the table. |
| S10 Verse 3 | The price comes due | As `SCENE_CARD_S10.md`: the dinner, the reaction, the tilt, the trusted look, Leia silent, the two words, the slab. | The slab's raised hands match the opening's poised hands. |
| S11 final chorus | The boast against the cost | Frame A, identical to S01, intercut with the slab and the farewell. | Cut to frame C. |
| S12 outro | Signature | Frame C, Chewie holds the room; the three names as sound; mouth insert closes (SB-36, external-off). | End of song. |
| Epilogue (frame, no song) | Back in business | Thaw (SB-30 repurposed); the quarters grill-change board, repaired: rings out, case open, grill in, mirror reveal, turn-back exit. | End. |

## 4. Panel work to request, in priority order

Each item names the card it serves and what would make it usable. Identity and continuity follow the current references (A face, B mouth, F wrist); panels are composition, not identity.

1. **S07-3, the hover.** One cockpit still: COCKPIT-R2-01's idea with the grill and neck corrected, a throttle, an unlettered display at screen-right, the throttle hand character-right. The single most important new frame; it is also the first proof.
2. **Chewbacca.** One head-and-shoulders reference round under the head standard before any Chewie card (S04B, S06A, S07-4, S07-5, S10-4, S12A) can be detailed. Without it, half the spine is blocked.
3. **S04A, Leia looks around the junky home.** One reaction panel; Leia production reference required first (none accepted).
4. **S07-1, the credits in the case.** Replace SB-19's chip stacks with the four rectangular credits from the opening.
5. **S07-2, the kid's channel.** A hand on a comms panel, a channel light dying; no face.
6. **S10, Verse 3.** The dinner (SB-07 seats the two side by side at the near edge of the table; the card proposes Vader alone at the far end, so a new panel is needed, plus a Vader reference), the tilt (SB-26 staging), the trusted look (Chewbacca again), Leia silent (SB-28 staging; Leia reference), the two words (SB-29 framing), the slab (SB-27 staging; prop design).
7. **The quarters sequence**, for the epilogue: CFA's five repair priorities as listed in `story/quarters_grill_change_20261009/REVIEW.txt` (the 02/03 manifest mismatch and the mirror → removal → dish progression; the two-hoop count; external-off teeth in the removal close-up together with true r4 grill geometry; head, face marks, neck, nose/ear jewelry and wrist accessories held across frames; mirror consistency).
8. **The thaw**, for the epilogue: SB-30 repurposed; needs the same two references as the farewell.
9. **The ship exterior** (S02D, S05, S07-7, S08): one silhouette round, three views, for Ziggy to pick from.

Not requested: the desert (SB-33), the title card (SB-35), any kid panel, any Lisan crossover imagery.

## 5. What the rescoring must deliver, and who consumes it

The Prime master gets one listening pass that produces a **timed lyric map**. Ziggy's point about echoes and ad-libs is the crux: a doubled chorus, an echoed word and an ad-lib are sung by the same voice but they are not the same mouth on screen. The map needs three lanes.

| Deliverable | Form | Consumed by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Section boundaries | start and end time for S01–S12, from the audio, not the old subtitle timebase | every card; `shot_plan.json` section times |
| Line timestamps | start and end per lyric line, within sections | the lip-sync cards: S01A, S02C, S03A, S04C, S09A, S10B, S11A |
| Lane labels | each timed line or word tagged **lead**, **double** (the doubled rap-chant in the choruses), or **ad-lib** (echoes, repeats, the trailing "I know"s) | the lip-sync cards decide which lane the visible mouth sings; doubles and ad-libs are sound, not mouth, unless a card says otherwise |
| The beat stop | the exact moment and length of the stop after the line "Man, don't start." | S07-3 and S07-4: the hover and the look sit in the silence |
| Tempo and feel | BPM and the half-time pocket; the "punch it" hits in both bridges | the ignition inserts (S05, S08A) and the cut rhythm of the choruses |
| Silences and rests | audible rests after punchlines | editorial; where a cut can breathe |

Proposed route for the pass: Google AI Studio, which already dissected the inspirational video for this project (`collaborators/video_studies/lil_vader_MwHocQFlw_c_20261009/`). The request text is in `PRIME_HANDOFF_20261011.md`; the upload and the run are an operator action for Nova or Ziggy, not something this folder performs. Whatever the model returns is a provisional map until someone with the recording in front of them spot-checks the section boundaries and the beat stop; a model's timestamp is a report, not a measurement.

## 6. Next cards

S10 is written (`SCENE_CARD_S10.md`). Then S04 (Leia's arrival and the fader), S02 (the creditors), S05 and S08 (the ignition inserts, now with "punch it"), the prologue cab scene and the epilogue, in that order unless Ziggy reorders.

— Claude

first storyboard pass, a shot-to-shot flow for the whole video, and thinking
about the stories around the music (why the video happens, and what comes
after). WRITER_PASS_001.md is that document.

The pass proposes; Ziggy decides; CFA Nova reconciles accepted proposals into
the production record through the existing foreign-return process.

The 36 panels at contact-sheet scale only (not full resolution). The ten
quarters grill-change panels were NOT viewed; their review text was read.
The recording was NOT listened to; no timing is claimed.

One read-only reviewer checked the pass against the locks, the panels and
the lyric order on October 10; its three substantive findings (an iced-grill

scene's mouth rule, and the ship's turn drifting out of S07) are fixed.

(one level up from story/). PRIME_HANDOFF_20261011.md records the hashes,

frame has her as the customer; the card is written for the customer
reading and can switch.

SCENE CARD S05 + S08
SCENE_CARD_S05_S08.md: "Ignition, twice," the two bridges as one card,
four beats each (strap in, coordinates locked, thrusters hot, punch it),
the second a reprise of the first with committed hands, no grin and the
battle light instead of star streaks. The overhead lever pull (the
October 9 lightspeed idea) is placed on the first "punch it"; the
throttle all the way (S08A) on the second. Ungraded, Unreviewed, timing
null, no run authorized. Blockers: the seated cockpit still, the ship
exterior, the corrected lever still, a navigation display. First proof
proposed: S08-4's throttle push, after S07-3's hover passes.

SCENE CARD, THE FIVE CHORUSES AND THE OUTRO
SCENE_CARD_CHORUSES_OUTRO.md: "One picture, five changes." Frame A is
the reviewed ten-turn opening prototype, not redesigned; each chorus
adds one change (the price as baseline; the glance to Leia with a
one-beat reverse on her; Chewie's amused look; the battle light on his
face; the identical hold intercut with the farewell and the slab). The
outro: Chewie holds the room, the three names as sound, the mouth insert
closes; the stage-mic and Panhandlers-card panels are parked per the
restrained outro. Ungraded, Unreviewed, timing null, no run authorized.
Blockers: the accepted starting frame (the prototype's own gate), a
corrected mouth ECU, Chewbacca, Leia.

SCENE CARD, PROLOGUE
SCENE_CARD_PROLOGUE.md: "The tip," the frame story before the song in
seven shots: the informant waiting above the city, the cab alongside,
the boarding (the cab handoff's first Comfy proof), the door and the
lift, the first exchange (the tip as her fare; lines not written), the
drop, and the cantina walk that becomes frame A as the song starts.
Ungraded, Unreviewed, no lyric timebase, no run authorized. Blockers: an
informant adaptation, the cab design, the boarding proof, the dialogue.

SCENE CARD, EPILOGUE
SCENE_CARD_EPILOGUE.md: "Back in business," the frame story after the
song: the thaw (SB-30 repurposed, with Chewie, not Leia), then the
quarters in the board's ten beats, one shot each, with their HD-GRILLUP
ids and CFA's five repair priorities as the gate: doorway, the mirror,
rings out, rings in the dish, the case, standing at the case, lift,
grill in, the mirror reveal (proposed last frame), the exit (the
board's ending, kept as the alternate). The 02/03 label conflict is
handled by content: the mirror portrait's pixels are in the file named
03, the removal's in the file named 02; filenames and numeric order are
preserved. The r4 iced look is Ziggy's selection for this look; the
card proposes this as its only scene. Ungraded, Unreviewed, no lyric
timebase, no run authorized. Open: whether the informant returns as the
witness; mirror or exit as the last frame.

ALL CARDS NOW WRITTEN
S07, S10, S04, S02, S05+S08, the choruses and outro, the prologue, the
epilogue. Every card is a proposal: Ungraded, Unreviewed, timing null,
no run, no sourcing decision. Each was checked by one read-only
reviewer against the record before hashing; the findings and fixes are
recorded in the mailbox messages that posted them.

NEXT ACTION
CFA Nova owns the Prime timing (music_alignment_20261011/); the writer
lane keeps every time null until her listening checks pass. Ziggy: the
wife-or-customer reading of Leia, her costume, which boss design is
Jabba, which hunter the S02 watcher is, the outro's reading of
"restrained," the epilogue's last frame (mirror or exit), and whether
the informant returns. The cards remain proposals for the foreign-return
process, not changes to any ledger.

assets.text:
# Scene card — the five choruses and the outro, "One picture, five changes"

Project: Hon Dolo / Strictly Business. Sections: S01 `[Chorus]` (TXT lines 1–7), S03 `[Chorus]` (21–26), S06 `[Chorus]` (44–49), S09 `[Chorus]` (74–79), S11 `[Final Chorus]` (102–107), S12 `[Outro]` (108–125), line ranges as reconciled by CFA Nova on October 11. Author: Claude, lead writer, October 11, 2026. Status: **proposed detailed design**. Scene grade: **Ungraded**. Shoot-plan review: **Unreviewed** (no reviewer, no time). Timing: null; the Prime master's anchors are provisional provider claims until Nova's listening checks pass. Nothing here authorizes a generation, a run, a download, a sourcing decision or a spend.

Fields follow `comfy/projects/collaborators/work_briefs_20261010/SHOOT_PLAN_VERIFICATION.txt`. Reference rules follow `comfy/projects/visual_library/REFERENCE_POLICY.txt` and the head standard. The opening prototype is `comfy/projects/collaborators/storyboard_detail_20261009/01_hon/workshop_current_20261009/REVIEWED_PLAN.txt` (marker HON-OPENING-WORKSHOP-REVIEWED-20261009) with its `IMAGE_MANIFEST.json` for A–F; this project's `asset_review_20261007/storyboard_crosswalk.json` for the SB panels.

Each shot carries a Source line listing the kinds it could plausibly take (supplied footage, existing asset, generated or animated, transformed material, or a mix). Per Ziggy, directly in the session on October 11 (DECISIONS section 8), that line only says whether we would have to generate the shot ourselves or already have something to use; the shots are written as if we make every one, and the line never alters a shot.

## Why one card

The song plays its hook five times and the words change twice: the first chorus names a price, the three middle ones ask why he turned the ship around, and the last one answers with the price paid. The board drew three different "Dolo performs" panels for it. The pass's rule is the opposite: the counter from the opening prototype is the chorus picture (S01, S03, S11), and each return to it adds one change, so the repetition reads as a change in the man and not a cut back to B-roll. The two middle choruses that leave the counter (S06 to frame C, S09 to frame B) are the two changes of place, and inside those frames the same rule holds: one picture, one change. This card writes the five changes and the outro that follows them. Frame A is the reviewed ten-turn prototype's locked medium-wide and is not redesigned here; the card only says what each return to it adds.

Constraints carried from the record: the prototype is silent visual acting with no lip-sync inside the ten-turn test, and the lip-sync for S01A, S03A, S09A and S11A is a separate editorial layer on the plan's rap_lipsync cards; SB-01 stays an extreme mouth close-up editorial insert separate from the continuous prototype; mouth external-off throughout the song; the four credits, the unlettered screen-right indicator and the provisional character-right wrist placement are the prototype's controls; Leia's reverse at the counter is one beat and the only place her face appears before S04 (S02-1 shows her hand); Ziggy's answer on the outro was "restrained, for now" (DECISIONS section 3, row 4), and this card's reading of restrained (the three names arrive as sound, no desert, no title card inside the song, no Lisan crossover imagery) is a proposal; no Vader before Verse 3.

## Frame A, as the prototype has it

Landscape 16:9, locked medium-wide, one seated Dolo at a worn wooden cantina counter in warm dim light. Dark brown distressed leather jacket over an open off-white shirt, chest ship visible. One implied offscreen customer. Cursive "eye" character-right/viewer-left, serif "know" character-left/viewer-right, neck blaster character-left/viewer-right, no forehead dice. External-off mouth (four upper gold caps on lateral incisors and short canines, white central incisors, lower silver/chrome, two plain lip hoops). Four matching warm-gold luminous rectangular credits on the counter. Wrist chain and dark band on the character-right wrist, viewer-left, as a provisional blocking choice. A small unlettered low-fuel/status indicator at screen-right from frame one. No cut, zoom, pan, mirror duplicate, new prop or person inside the prototype. No starting frame is accepted at this writing; no video turn has run.

The customer, by the confirmed weave (DECISIONS sections 2 and 7), is Leia, across the counter, offscreen; placing her at screen-right of the counter's near side is this card's inference, following the side her hand enters from in S02-1. The cantina is the same room as the club in S02-7 and the booth in S12. The room, as this card lays it out: the entrance at the front wall, the DJ booth (frame C's boards, SB-05) against the back wall, the counter along the right-hand wall as seen from the entrance. Frame C is Chewie at his boards wherever they are: the cantina booth (S01-2, S02-7, S12-1) or the console controller in the ship (S04-7, S06-1, S07); a chorus returns to the frame it left, not to a room. One recorded slip for the next consolidation: `SCENE_CARD_S02.md` S02-7, as posted, puts the entrance with the bouncer "in the deep background, screen-right" while looking at the booth; in this room that is a side door at screen-right, not the main entrance, and the S02 card's wording will be corrected when it is next consolidated.

## S01, the price

### S01-1 The mouth (SB-01 insert)
- Purpose: "Strictly business. Count it twice." The smile and the mercenary tone, before the man.
- Direction: extreme close-up on the mouth, poised, then a restrained grin. No speech handling; the words are sound. The grin shows the external-off teeth.
- Camera: the SB-01 framing, locked.
- Lighting: frame A's warm practicals.
- Start/end intent: start poised; end on the restrained grin.
- References: SB-01 `HD-DROP-725c38458fd8` for composition only (its obsolete two-gold, one-hoop dental map does not govern); mouth B `HD-B-91ef00348229`; face A `HD-RETURN-6c8900223ee9` for any surrounding identity.
- Continuity: this exact framing returns as S07-6 (the grin that pretends the sacrifice was a favor) and as the closing insert in S12; three mouths, one framing.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated insert from a corrected ECU, once one exists; a supplied clip would need to carry our mouth, the least likely kind but not an excluded one.
- Missing art: a corrected ECU still (an editorial design need, per the reviewed plan, not a prototype request).

### S01-2 The room (cantina wide, proposed)
- Purpose: establish the room once, with Chewie at the boards behind it, so every later return to frame C has a home.
- Direction: wide, the cantina from the entrance side, looking toward the back wall; the counter along the right-hand wall at screen-right-foreground with Dolo seated, small; the DJ booth against the back wall, screen-left of center, with Chewie at it, head down; patrons between. One slow push of a few inches, or locked.
- Camera: wide, high enough to read the room's depth; locked or a slow push.
- Lighting: warm practicals on the counter, the boards' small lights at the back, the room dim between.
- Start/end intent: start on the room; end with the push settled on the counter's warmth.
- References: SB-05 `HD-DROP-6e8eb6a956c9` for the idea (cantina walk, "Hook settle + Chewie DJ bg"; its lead and DJ anatomy differ and do not govern). Chewie: no accepted anatomy; the mixer portrait `HD-DROP-ca406436d384` is his cover; CHEW-STAGE-01 (`CHEW-EXP-01-furry-dj.jpg`) for booth staging only.
- Continuity: the booth at the back wall, the counter along the right-hand wall; S12-1 keeps that placement, and S02-7's floor-level cut-in looks from the counter's side toward the booth (its entrance placement is the slip recorded above).
- Source: TBD. Plausible: a supplied cantina or club wide with the counter and booth composited; generated from a room design; a mix. This is the shot most likely to take a supplied room.
- Missing art: the cantina as a set; Chewbacca.

### S01-3 Frame A, the price (the prototype)
- Purpose: the pitch, the count, the fuel gesture, the half-smile. Exactly the ten-turn prototype as reviewed: poise, first count, firm price, recount, align, fuel reminder, draw payment closer, passage gesture, "nice try" half-smile, settle.
- Direction: as `REVIEWED_PLAN.txt` prompts 01–10. Nothing added by this card.
- Camera: locked medium-wide.
- Lighting: as the prototype.
- Start/end intent: start poised; end on the calm business-first hold.
- References: A, B, D `HD-DROP-36679ee9953b`, E `HD-DROP-60f245863c6b`, F `HD-DROP-b18c4a123579`, as the manifest limits them.
- Continuity: this is the frame every chorus returns to.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: the prototype's own route (one starting still, up to nine dependent continuations), if it passes; supplied footage is the least likely kind for this shot but not an excluded one.
- Missing art: an accepted consolidated starting frame.

Hand-off: the generated clip ends on the settle (prompt 10); the edit cuts to S02-1, her hand on the counter, either on the half-smile (prompt 09, the spine's proposal) or on the settle. An editorial choice, not a generation difference.

## S03, the first doubt

### S03-1 Frame A, one change: the glance
- Purpose: "So why’d I turn this ship around?" The question enters the hook, and his eyes leave the credits for the first time.
- Direction: frame A, mid-count. His eyes leave the credits and go to her, across the counter at screen-right, and hold a beat longer than a salesman's would. Then back to the count. Nothing else moves. The shot plan's S03A says the glance goes toward the cockpit exit; by the confirmed weave it goes to her.
- Camera: locked medium-wide, the prototype's.
- Lighting: as the prototype.
- Start/end intent: start mid-count; end back on the count, one beat after the glance.
- References: as S01-3. The plan's note that the credit stack remains in frame holds.
- Continuity: the four credits unchanged (S02-1's extra stack left the counter inside S02-1).
- Source: TBD. Plausible: a continuation of the prototype's route from an accepted parent; generated from an accepted starting frame, once one exists; supplied footage is the least likely kind but not an excluded one.
- Missing art: as S01-3.

### S03-2 Her, across the counter (the reverse, one beat)
- Purpose: what he is looking at. One beat of Leia, the only time her face is on screen before S04.
- Direction: reverse on the customer's side of the counter: Leia, medium close, looking at him (screen-left), not amused, not unamused. One beat. No line.
- Camera: medium close-up, locked; her eyeline screen-left, opposed to his glance screen-right.
- Lighting: frame A's practicals from the other side.
- Start/end intent: start on her looking; end on her looking.
- References: LEIA-LIKENESS-01 (`leia_source_crop.png`, likeness input only); LEIA-STYLE-01 (`LEIA-EXP-01-ivory-coat.jpg`, ivory wardrobe and hair styling only); the ivory-coat album cover `HD-DROP-5171bb20c773`. No accepted Leia production reference; costume undecided; the customer-versus-wife reading is Ziggy's open question (`SCENE_CARD_S04.md`).
- Continuity: her look matches S04-2's and S10-5's bearing; what she wears here is what she wears through S10.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated from an accepted Leia still; a supplied reaction clip with likeness swap; a mix.
- Missing art: an accepted Leia.

Hand-off: cut on her look to S04-1, the hatch.

## S06, Chewie sees through him

### S06-1 Frame C, the look (S06A)
- Purpose: the second chorus asks the question again; Chewie already knows the answer. The shot plan's S06A: he turns from his controls and gives Dolo, off camera, a knowing look, and holds it.
- Direction: Chewie at his boards in the cockpit (the console controller of S04-7), screen-left; he turns from the controls to look screen-right at Dolo (offscreen) and holds the look through the whole hook. Restrained fur movement. This is the knowing look: he sees through the boast, the doubt the S10 card names. S07-4's look sees the decision being made; S10-4's is the trusted one.
- Camera: medium close-up, locked, from Dolo's side so Chewie is screen-left looking screen-right.
- Lighting: cockpit warm practicals; the controller's small lights; a touch of the star streaks' cold light fading from S05-4.
- Start/end intent: start with him at the controls; end on the held look.
- References: SB-18 `HD-DROP-b443c1d21d74` for staging only (ape-like copilot, a recorded defect). No accepted Chewbacca anatomy.
- Continuity: Chewie screen-left looking screen-right, as S07-4 and S04-7. The three Chewie looks (S06 seeing through him, S07-4 seeing the decision, S10-4 trusted) are a motif, not a repeated frame: S07-4 carries Dolo's shoulder soft at frame-right and S10-4 is at the chamber's edge.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated from an accepted Chewie still (the shot plan's image-to-video intent); a supplied clip of a performer in costume if one ever exists; a mix.
- Missing art: Chewbacca.

Hand-off: cut from the look to S07-1, the crates.

## S09, the question has an answer

### S09-1 Frame B, the battle light (S09A)
- Purpose: the fourth chorus. He is still performing. He is not selling anything. The shot plan's S09A: steady resolve, battle light across his face.
- Direction: Dolo in the pilot seat, facing front, the harness across his chest (if the seated still carries one; `SCENE_CARD_S05_S08.md`), singing the hook to camera with the same bearing as the counter but nothing to sell. Cold light from ahead, through the windscreen behind the camera, moves across his face in slow passes as the ship moves through the battle. The mouth is external-off and visible; the lip-sync layer is this shot's job.
- Camera: medium close-up, locked, slight movement tolerated per the plan ("keep camera movement slight").
- Lighting: cockpit warm practicals under the moving cold light from the front.
- Start/end intent: start on the first pass of cold light; end on the last word, then black.
- References: face A; mouth B; wrist F if the hands are in frame (character-right, provisional); the seated cockpit idea `HD-DROP-14f8eb9979b5` (R2-01, needs review). SB-08 `HD-DROP-e1250a0bce91` and SB-24 `HD-DROP-35f608374a7b` are the crosswalk's candidates for S09A, staging only (SB-08's mouth, hair, marks and neck ink drift; SB-24 is a rescue-approach composition).
- Continuity: the battle ahead, where S07-7's turn left it and S08-4b holds it; the opening outfit and marks.
- Lane note (proposal, Nova's call): the hook is LEAD on his mouth; the doubled chant, if there is one, is DOUBLE and the mouth sings the lead.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated lip-sync over an accepted seated still, once one exists (the plan's rap_lipsync intent); a supplied performance clip of Ziggy himself; a mix.
- Missing art: the seated cockpit still.

Hand-off: cut to black on the last "around"; then S10-1, the table.

## S11, the boast against the cost

### S11-1 Frame A, identical to S01, intercut
- Purpose: the final chorus. Same picture, same bearing, same credits, and the words have changed under it: "Fuel ain’t free. Still paid that price." and "Still turned this motherfucker around." (TXT lines 104 and 106). The shot plan's S11A: hold the familiar confident expression for a later editorial juxtaposition with the farewell and the carbonite reveal.
- Direction: frame A exactly as S01-3's hold, the count and the half-smile again if the prototype's parents allow a reprise, otherwise the settled hold. Intercut in the edit with S10-5 (her), S10-6 (the two words) and S10-7 (the slab): the counter, the farewell, the counter, the slab. The intercut is editorial; this card generates nothing new for it.
- Camera: locked medium-wide, the prototype's.
- Lighting: as the prototype.
- Start/end intent: start on the hold; end on the hold.
- References: as S01-3. SB-34 `HD-DROP-4639c31e55bc` (final face hold; its tattoo map differs from the lock and does not govern) is the crosswalk's candidate for S11A, staging only.
- Continuity: identical to S01; the slab's raised hands (S10-7) match-cut to the opening's poised hands.
- Lane note (proposal, Nova's call): LEAD on his mouth; the last line is the one place the lip-sync must be exact, because the picture is identical and only the words carry the change.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: the prototype's own material reused (the plan's intent is a return to the established portrait); a new prototype pass only if the edit needs a different hold.
- Missing art: as S01-3.

Hand-off: cut to frame C on the last line.

## S12, the signature

### S12-1 Frame C, Chewie holds the room (S12A)
- Purpose: the shot plan's S12A: Chewie at the DJ console as the performance lighting settles, a calm final pose, composition space left clear for an editorial title.
- Direction: the cantina booth (S01-2's boards at the back of the room), Chewie at the decks, hands resting on them, head up for once, looking at the room (screen-right), not at camera. The lights settle. Nobody else moves. Proposed reading of "restrained": the three names arrive as sound, with no stage, no second performer and no card inside the song; Ziggy decides.
- Camera: medium wide from the floor, Chewie screen-left at the booth, the room's depth screen-right; clear space at frame-right for the editorial title the plan allows for; whether that title sits inside the song's last seconds or after them is Ziggy's call.
- Lighting: the performance lighting settling to the practicals.
- Start/end intent: start on the last light cue; end on the settled room and the held pose.
- References: SB-32 `HD-DROP-39ede31230fd` (DJ booth, "Chewie hype") for staging only; SB-31 `HD-DROP-76b5b1730778` (stage mic, "Voice from outer world") is proposed parked, since the names are sound in this reading (pass 001 kept it as a restrained performance; either is possible under "restrained"); SB-35 `HD-DROP-a2587d798b7c` (the Panhandlers card) is not an approved logo or typography, and its place inside or after the song is Ziggy's. No accepted Chewbacca anatomy.
- Continuity: the booth screen-left at the back of the room, as S01-2 and S02-7.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated from an accepted Chewie still with the room from S01-2; a supplied club clip with the booth composited; a mix.
- Missing art: Chewbacca; the cantina set.

### S12-2 The mouth closes it (SB-36 insert)
- Purpose: the end sting. The mouth that opened the song closes it.
- Direction: the S01-1 framing exactly. The mouth, the restrained grin, then the lips close. External-off. No iced grill (that look belongs to the quarters scene in the epilogue, not the song).
- Camera: the SB-01 framing, locked.
- Lighting: as S01-1.
- Start/end intent: start on the grin; end on the lips closed, held.
- References: SB-36 `HD-DROP-ec55fb59f604` for the idea only ("grill/title proposal, not final jewelry or title"); composition from SB-01 `HD-DROP-725c38458fd8`; mouth B `HD-B-91ef00348229`.
- Continuity: three mouths, one framing: S01-1 opens, S07-6 grins, S12-2 closes.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: as S01-1.
- Missing art: as S01-1.

End of song. The epilogue (the thaw, then the quarters grill-change) is the frame story's card, not this one.

## Cut logic across the choruses

Every chorus returns to a frame the song has already been in, at the angle it left: S01, S03 and S11 to frame A; S06 to frame C (the console, as S04-7 left it); S09 to frame B (the cockpit, as S08-4b left it). The rule: a chorus never introduces a place the song has not already been. The five changes, in order: the price (nothing changes; it is the baseline), the glance (his eyes), Chewie's amusement (the copilot's eyes), the battle light (the light on him), the identical hold against the slab (the edit). The outro changes nothing; it holds.

## Required ingredients

| Ingredient | State | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Consolidated starting frame (frame A) | Missing | requested October 9 via Create Image, outcome unknown, none accepted; the prototype's parent |
| Corrected mouth ECU | Missing | an editorial design need; SB-01's dental map is obsolete |
| Cantina set | Missing | S01-2, S02-7, S12 share it |
| Chewbacca | Missing | S01-2, S06-1, S12-1 |
| Leia | Needs fixes | S03-2; likeness crop and ivory album exist; no accepted reference; costume undecided |
| Seated cockpit still with harness | Needs fixes | S09-1; `HD-DROP-14f8eb9979b5` needs review; the S07-3 repair |
| Battle light | Needs fixes | S07-7 defines it |
| Dolo face A, mouth B, wrist F | Ready | as the manifest limits them |
| Title for the end | Open | the plan leaves space for an editorial title; inside or after the song is Ziggy's; SB-35 is not approved typography |

## Critical blockers and the next bounded repair

1. **No accepted starting frame.** The prototype's own gate; until it passes, S01-3, S03-1 and S11-1 do not exist. The reviewed plan records that one still was requested through Create Image with its outcome unknown, and names no owner; whoever runs the prototype owns this.
2. **No corrected mouth ECU.** One still, the SB-01 framing with the current four-gold map, reviewed as a mouth, before S01-1, S07-6 and S12-2.
3. **No accepted Chewbacca.** The same repair every other card names.
4. **No accepted Leia.** The S04 and S10 repair; S03-2 is one beat and can wait for it.

## Scene grade and review

Grade: Ungraded. Shoot-plan review: Unreviewed. The cantina wide (S01-2), the reverse on Leia (S03-2), the closing mouth insert (S12-2), the room layout, the reading of "restrained" (names as sound, no stage, no second performer, no card inside the song) and the parking of SB-31 are proposals; the title's place is open.

## One coherent draft prompt (S01-1 / S12-2, the mouth; silent still, for the corrected ECU)

Landscape 16:9, extreme close-up of a man's mouth and chin, framed from just below the nose to the chin so the nose is out of frame, warm brown skin, lips relaxed and just parted in the beginning of a restrained grin. Upper teeth: four gold caps, on both lateral incisors and both short canines; the two central incisors and the other upper teeth natural white. Lower teeth a silver-chrome grill. Two plain small metal hoops through the lower lip, one on each side. Warm amber practical light from the front-left, a dim room behind. Shallow focus on the teeth. No text, no second person, no hands.

## First proof, if and when a run is authorized

Not this card. Its proof is the opening prototype itself, which the reviewed plan already bounds (one starting still, up to nine dependent continuations, silent, locked). The one still this card adds to the queue is the corrected mouth ECU, which can be made and reviewed independently of the prototype and serves three shots.

— Claude

# Scene card S02 — "The creditors behind the boast"

Project: Hon Dolo / Strictly Business. Section: S02, the first verse (`shot_plan.json` S02, `[Verse]`, TXT lines 8–20 as reconciled by CFA Nova on October 11; the verse text itself runs lines 9–19). Author: Claude, lead writer, October 11, 2026. Status: **proposed detailed design**. Scene grade: **Ungraded**. Shoot-plan review: **Unreviewed** (no reviewer, no time). Timing: null; the Prime master's anchors are provisional provider claims until Nova's listening checks pass. Nothing here authorizes a generation, a run, a download, a sourcing decision or a spend.

Fields follow `comfy/projects/collaborators/work_briefs_20261010/SHOOT_PLAN_VERIFICATION.txt`. Reference rules follow `comfy/projects/visual_library/REFERENCE_POLICY.txt` and the head standard. Paths and hashes: `comfy/projects/collaborators/storyboard_detail_20261009/01_hon/workshop_current_20261009/IMAGE_MANIFEST.json` for A/B/F, this project's `asset_review_20261007/storyboard_crosswalk.json` for the SB panels, `comfy/casting/gemini_cast_reference_map.txt` for the cast entries, `feedback/cast_review_20261009/decisions.json` for the boss shortlist and the club roles.

**New in this card: a Source line per shot.** Per the October 11 relay (DECISIONS section 8), each shot's source is TBD among supplied footage, existing asset, generated or animated, transformed material, or a mix. The Source line lists which of those the shot could plausibly take and what a supplied clip would need to contain, so Ziggy can match clips he remembers against it. It is a prompt for his recall, not a sourcing decision; nothing is assumed real or generated. Ziggy's own words (October 11): the footage question is only whether we have to generate a shot ourselves or already have something to use, and it does not change the storyboard. The shots above the Source line are written as if we make every one of them; the line never alters a shot.

## Story beat

The first chorus named a price. This verse explains it: the bravado has creditors. He is still at the counter, still selling the ride to the woman with money, and every boast he throws is a bill he owes. Jabba's funding, the hunters, the name he will not let anyone play with, the captain's title he insists on, the junky ship that is the only thing he has ever been proud of. The verse ends on the ship proving itself, because that is the one boast that is true, and the card hands the eye back to the counter at the same angle it left, so the chorus that follows reads as the same man a little less sure.

Constraints carried from the record: the verse is sung to Leia (DECISIONS sections 2 and 7); she stays unseen in this section so that S03's glance is the first time the picture looks at her; mouth external-off throughout; no Vader; no Lisan crossover; the ship's design is unaccepted; the boss design is a shortlist with no winner; the hunters have no identity assigned.

## Shots, in order

Ten shots. Screen geography: frame A (the counter) exactly as the reviewed ten-turn prototype has it, no change in angle or light. Every cut-away is a cut, not a continuation, and every cut-away returns to frame A as if no time had passed. The ship, when it first appears, travels **toward screen-right**; that is the exit vector S07 later reverses (`SCENE_CARD_S07.md`: the ship turns right-to-left), so the direction is set here once and holds through S05 and S07-7. In the cockpit, Chewie sits screen-left of Dolo, as in S07.

### S02-1 Money to spare (her hand, not her face)
- Purpose: the first picture of Leia without showing her. The money arrives on the counter from her side.
- Direction: frame A's own orientation, dropped to the counter top: close on the counter. A woman's hand, from the near foreground at screen-right (the customer's side), sets a stack of credits down beside the four already there and withdraws. No face, no second hand, no jewelry decision implied. Dolo's character-right hand, seen from the front, enters from screen-left, draws the new stack toward him and takes it out of frame at screen-left; the four credits stay where the prototype has them.
- Camera: tight insert, locked, the counter edge horizontal; the hands enter from opposite sides.
- Lighting: frame A's practicals, unchanged.
- Start/end intent: start on the four credits alone; end with her hand gone and his hand on the new stack.
- References: SB-03 `HD-DROP-36679ee9953b` (pay-table D) for the credits and counter surface; wrist chain and band F `HD-DROP-b18c4a123579` on his character-right wrist (provisional blocking choice carried from the opening, not canon). Her sleeve: costume undecided (`SCENE_CARD_S10.md`, S10-5); LEIA-STYLE-01 (`LEIA-EXP-01-ivory-coat.jpg`) is the ivory wardrobe candidate only. Do not show a ring or a cuff that would decide her look.
- Continuity: the four credits must match S01's prototype exactly, and her stack leaves the counter inside this shot, so frame A's locked set is unchanged when S03 returns to it (S03 changes one thing only, the glance).
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated insert from the pay-table still; a supplied close-up of hands on a counter if one exists; transformed material. A supplied clip would need two hands from opposite sides and a static counter.
- Missing art: nothing new; a decision on her sleeve.

### S02-2 Jabba's room (frame of the first creditor)
- Purpose: "Jabbah funding." The first creditor, told as pressure without a word. The shot plan's S02A.
- Direction: a low, wide, gold-lit counting room. The boss on a dais, nearly still; one slow turn of the head toward camera. Ledgers, cargo tokens, a lieutenant counting in the foreground. No Dolo in this shot; the room is what he owes.
- Camera: wide, low, one slow push of a few inches, or locked. Symmetry; the dais centered.
- Lighting: warm gold from above, deep shadow at the edges, a single cold accent on the ledgers.
- Start/end intent: start with the boss looking away; end with the head turned to camera, held.
- References: SB-10 `HD-DROP-df1418147b5d` for staging (low, wide, gold, pressure; its boss does not govern). Boss design: the October 9 shortlist is BOSS-002 gecko-frog `HD-RETURN-339cdbe1e03a`, BOSS-008 crocodilian `HD-RETURN-8421e7cfa1a0`, BOSS-005 catfish `HD-RETURN-e18185bdab18`, BOSS-010 walrus `HD-RETURN-9143639db1cf`, no final winner. The lyric names Jabba; the record's character is the crime boss. Which design wears the name is Ziggy's choice.
- Continuity: the gold of this room should not reappear until the dinner's polished surfaces, so the two creditors (Jabba, Vader) rhyme as rooms.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated from the chosen boss still with a slow move (the shot plan's image-to-video intent); transformed material if a supplied throne-room clip exists; a mix (generated boss over a supplied set). A supplied clip would need a seated figure on a dais, low angle, nearly still.
- Missing art: an accepted boss; the room as a set.

### S02-3 The puck
- Purpose: "bounty hunt-ahhhs." The hunters, announced by their instrument before their face.
- Direction: a bounty puck on a bar top, screen-center, showing Dolo's likeness as card art. A gloved hand enters from screen-right, lifts it, and the puck's light moves across the glove. No face.
- Camera: insert, locked, slight high angle.
- Lighting: the bar's practicals; the puck's own glow the key on the glove.
- Start/end intent: start on the puck alone; end with it lifted out of frame to screen-right.
- References: SB-09 `HD-DROP-af2c7daaf039` for the insert's idea (inspect hands and invented marks; the panel's card art does not govern; the likeness on the puck must be made from face A `HD-RETURN-6c8900223ee9`). Hand side: the hunter's hand enters from screen-right, so the hunter is screen-right of the puck, matching where he stands in S02-4.
- Continuity: the puck's card art is the first and only place a picture of Dolo appears inside the picture; it must carry the cheek lettering correctly (cursive "eye" character-right, serif "know" character-left) even at insert scale, or stay too small to read.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated insert; a supplied close-up of a hand lifting a small object; a mix (supplied hand, composited puck).
- Missing art: the puck as a prop with A's likeness.

### S02-4 The watch (Boba, motionless)
- Purpose: one hunter, one look. The shot plan's S02B as written (a motionless watch, one helmet turn); pass 001 reassigns the board's alley-run panel SB-11 to it, because running contradicts the bravado.
- Direction: the loading bay, busy with crews and cargo. At its edge, screen-right, a bounty hunter stands completely still; the ship sits far in the background, screen-left. One slight helmet turn toward the ship. Nothing else about him moves.
- Camera: medium wide, locked; the crowd crosses in front of him; he does not.
- Lighting: hard bay light, the hunter half in shadow.
- Start/end intent: start with the helmet facing the crowd; end with it turned toward the ship, held.
- References: SB-11 `HD-DROP-ac71d8209a11` is the alley-run panel the plan reassigns (its running Dolo does not govern; its neon and crowd may inform the bay). Hunter identity: the shot plan names Boba Fett ("bounty pressure") and the cast map holds a Boba Fett entry with BOBA-ARMOR-01 (`BOBA-EXP-01-olive-armor.jpg`, an armor concept, "not automatically Bounty Hunter 1 or 2"); BH-01 and BH-02 are reserved with no identity, body or armor assigned. Whether this watcher is Boba in that armor concept or a numbered hunter is Ziggy's to say; no production reference is accepted for either.
- Continuity: the hunter is screen-right, the ship screen-left; in S02-3 the hand came from screen-right. The ship's silhouette here must match S02-8's.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated from an accepted hunter still over a bay set; a supplied clip of a motionless armored figure at the edge of a crowd; transformed material. A supplied clip would need a still figure with a slight head turn and moving extras.
- Missing art: a hunter; the bay as a set; the ship exterior.

### S02-5 My name (the neck blaster)
- Purpose: "not safe ta play with my name." The tattoo as a threat, in one catch-light.
- Direction: close on the character-left side of Dolo's neck. The smoking-blaster tattoo. One passing light (a ship's running light, or a door opening offscreen) crosses it, and the smoke seems to move. Jaw still. No mouth.
- Camera: macro insert, locked; the neck fills the frame; the jawline at the top edge.
- Lighting: frame A's warm practicals plus one moving cold light, screen-right to screen-left.
- Start/end intent: start dark; end after the light has crossed, dark again.
- References: SB-12 `HD-DROP-e5e5bb2eb7ee` for the insert's idea (neck blaster detail; not scale or placement acceptance). Placement and scale follow the neck-bling handoff and the head standard: character-left, the smoke rising toward the jaw.
- Continuity: the same tattoo must read in S02-6 at medium scale on the same side.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated macro from a neck reference once one is accepted; a transformed still with a light pass; a supplied clip would need to carry this tattoo, which makes it the least likely kind but not an excluded one.
- Missing art: an accepted neck reference. The neck-bling handoff (`handoffs/neck_bling_20261009/`) is prepared, not sent; nothing is generated or accepted.

### S02-6 El capatain Solo (the captain portrait, frame B)
- Purpose: the boast that names him. The verse's lip-sync anchor, the shot plan's S02C.
- Direction: Dolo in the pilot seat, leaning back, chin up, one hand resting on the armrest well clear of his face, the other on the throttle at rest. Exaggerated captainly dignity, played straight. He sings the formal line to camera; on the second name he looks screen-left, at Chewie (offscreen, in the copilot seat), for agreement he does not get. Lips part on the sung words; the mouth is external-off.
- Camera: medium close-up, locked, slightly low to give him the dignity he is claiming; the copilot seat and its occupant out of frame at screen-left, implied by the look, never shown.
- Lighting: cockpit warm practicals, a touch of cool from the display at screen-right (the S07 cockpit's light scheme, established here).
- Start/end intent: start on the lean back; end on the look screen-left, held a beat.
- References: SB-14 `HD-DROP-d36a3316372d` for staging (cockpit captain; its face and tattoo drift do not govern); COCKPIT-R2-01 is the cockpit idea the S07 card keeps, with grill and neck corrections pending; face A `HD-RETURN-6c8900223ee9`; mouth B `HD-B-91ef00348229` (external-off: four upper gold caps on lateral incisors and short canines, white central incisors, lower silver/chrome, two plain lip hoops); wrist chain and band F `HD-DROP-b18c4a123579` on the character-right wrist (provisional). SB-06 `HD-DROP-b18c4a123579` is the scoundrel-forearm concept the crosswalk points at S02C; exact design unresolved.
- Continuity: the opening outfit, dark brown distressed leather jacket over the open off-white shirt, chest ship visible; cursive "eye" character-right cheek, serif "know" character-left cheek, neck blaster character-left; no forehead dice; target one hoop per nostril, ear hoop and crystal stud per A, minor variation tolerated. This is the cockpit S04, S05, S07 and S09 return to; its geography (Dolo screen-right of Chewie, display screen-right) is set here.
- Lane note for the timed lyric map: the formal line and the two names are LEAD on his mouth; the trailing repeats of the names are AD-LIB and are not mouthed on screen. Which words are sung and which are doubled is Nova's listening call, not this card's.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated lip-sync over an accepted cockpit still (the shot plan's rap_lipsync intent); a mix (supplied cockpit plate, generated performance); a supplied performance clip of Ziggy himself if one exists. A supplied clip would need a seated performer, locked frame, hands clear of the face.
- Missing art: an accepted cockpit still with Dolo seated (the same repair S07-3 needs; one still serves both).

### S02-7 The club cut-in
- Purpose: the same boast, thrown to a room. One beat, so the cockpit's portrait does not have to carry the whole verse alone. A new insert proposed by pass 001, not an existing card.
- Direction: the club, from the floor, looking up at the booth. Dolo at the booth's edge, mid-boast, one arm out; Chewy at the decks behind him, screen-left, head down over the mixer; the bouncer a large shape at the entrance in the deep background, screen-right. Crowd backs in the foreground. The mouth is far enough from camera that it is a shape, not a lip-sync.
- Camera: wide, handheld feel but no swing, a slow drift of a few inches.
- Lighting: club color, one hard key on Dolo, the mixer's small lights on Chewy.
- Start/end intent: start on the arm going out; end on the crowd's reaction, half a beat.
- References: SB-08 `HD-DROP-e1250a0bce91` for the idea (debt flex; its mouth, hair, marks and neck ink drift and do not govern; it is a close-up, this is a wide). Chewy: the mixer portrait `HD-DROP-ca406436d384` is his cover, chosen October 9; no accepted production reference for his anatomy exists. Bouncer: BOSS-006 rhino `HD-RETURN-cafa39484145` is the user story intent for the club entrance (not generated, not accepted). Bartender BOSS-009 toad `HD-RETURN-80d3ca6a6858` may be in the deep background if the bar is in frame; not required.
- Continuity: this is frame C's room (the boards), seen from the floor. S01's cantina wide (SB-05, proposed) establishes Chewy at the boards behind the room first; this cut-in must agree with it (Chewy screen-left of the booth's edge, decks facing the floor), and S04B, S06A and S12A return to the booth from its own side.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated wide from accepted stills; a supplied club crowd clip with the booth composited; a mix. A supplied clip would need a packed floor looking up at a raised booth.
- Missing art: Chewy's anatomy; the club as a set; the bouncer and bartender as accepted designs.

### S02-8 Imperial GO GOs (the warship)
- Purpose: the second creditor's reach, the one he pretends not to fear. The first flight exterior in the piece.
- Direction: a massive warship fills the frame edge to edge, cold grey, hangar bays lit, moving slowly screen-left to screen-right. In the last beat the junky ship enters small from frame-bottom-left, crossing the warship's hull, also moving screen-right. No weapons fire; the threat is the scale.
- Camera: wide, locked or a slow drift; the warship's hull as the frame's texture.
- Lighting: cold starlight, the hangar bays the only warmth.
- Start/end intent: start on the hull alone; end with the junky ship crossing it, small.
- References: none on the board. The ship exterior is unaccepted (SB-13 `HD-DROP-8896508767b4` is an exterior concept whose silhouette differs). The warship is undesigned.
- Continuity: the junky ship's direction of travel is screen-right, set here; its silhouette must match S02-9.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: this is the shot most likely to come from supplied footage if Ziggy has a clip of a capital ship pass; generated or transformed otherwise; a mix (supplied warship, composited junky ship). The light-skipping attribution the relay mentions is unverified; nothing here assumes which film.
- Missing art: the warship; the ship exterior.

### S02-9 This junky ship (the bank)
- Purpose: the one boast that is true. The shot plan's S02D.
- Direction: the junky ship makes one clean evasive bank past the warship's flank and away screen-right. One move, no cuts inside it; the hull passes close enough to read its wear. No pursuit shown; "they can't catch me" is the bank itself.
- Camera: wide exterior, the camera trailing then letting the ship leave frame screen-right.
- Lighting: cold, the warship's bay light raking the junky ship's underside for one beat.
- Start/end intent: start with the ship small against the hull; end with it gone screen-right and the warship receding.
- References: SB-13 `HD-DROP-8896508767b4` for the idea (fastest junk exterior; silhouette differs). No accepted ship exterior exists; the silhouette round proposed in `STORYBOARD_UPDATE_20261011.md` item 9 serves this shot, S05, S07-7 and S08.
- Continuity: readable flight direction screen-right; the ship's wear visible; the same silhouette as S02-8 and S02-4's background.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: supplied flight footage if a clip with one clean bank exists; generated from an accepted exterior still (the shot plan's image-to-video intent); transformed; a mix. A supplied clip would need one continuous bank with the ship exiting frame.
- Missing art: the ship exterior.

### S02-10 Twelve-par (the number and the Maw)
- Purpose: the receipt for the boast. Two beats: the number as a graphic, the Maw as a wide. Then the hand-off to frame A.
- Direction: beat one, a cockpit HUD reads a distance in parsecs counting down to under twelve; the text is editorial and added in the cut, not generated. Beat two, the widest shot in the verse: the Maw, a vast gravity well, the junky ship a speck skimming its edge, screen-right.
- Camera: beat one an insert, locked; beat two a wide, locked.
- Lighting: beat one the HUD's own light; beat two the Maw's glow from screen-left, the ship a silhouette.
- Start/end intent: start on the number above twelve; end on the ship clearing the Maw's edge screen-right. Hard cut to frame A at the same angle and light S01 left it.
- References: SB-15 `HD-DROP-a962c9148eb5` (parsec HUD; final text editorial), SB-16 `HD-DROP-0c8852c50251` (Maw wide; story and VFX concept only).
- Continuity: the number must not be legible as a specific figure in any generated frame; it is typeset in the edit so it can be corrected. The ship skims screen-right, consistent with S02-8 and S02-9.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: the HUD is a title-card graphic over a generated or supplied cockpit plate; the Maw is generated or transformed, or supplied if a clip of a ship skimming a gravity well exists; a mix.
- Missing art: the HUD plate; the Maw.

## Cut logic

1 → 2 on money: her hand's stack to the lieutenant's ledgers. 2 → 3 on the boss's eyes landing on camera to the puck's light. 3 → 4 on the gloved hand leaving screen-right to the hunter standing screen-right. 4 → 5 on the helmet's turn to the light crossing the neck, the two "looks" at Dolo in a row. 5 → 6 on the neck to the man, same side, wider. 6 → 7 on the look screen-left for agreement to the crowd that gives it. 7 → 8 the hardest cut in the verse, club color to cold grey. 8 → 9 inside the same vector, the ship crossing to the ship banking. 9 → 10 the exit screen-right to the number, then the Maw, then frame A.

Verse rhythm: the first half (1–7) is rooms and faces, warm; the second half (8–10) is space, cold. The cold half is where supplied footage is most plausible, and nothing in the warm half depends on it.

## Required ingredients

| Ingredient | State | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Frame A counter prototype | Needs fixes | the ten-turn prototype is reviewed but no starting frame is accepted; S02-1 is an insert on the same counter and its credits must match whatever is accepted |
| Dolo face reference A | Ready | `HD-RETURN-6c8900223ee9`, identity only |
| Dolo mouth reference B | Ready | `HD-B-91ef00348229`, external-off; visible in S02-6 only |
| Wrist chain and band F | Ready | `HD-DROP-b18c4a123579`; character-right wrist provisional, not canon |
| Neck blaster | Missing | the neck-bling handoff is prepared, not sent; no neck reference generated or accepted; S02-5 is a macro of it |
| Cockpit still with Dolo seated | Needs fixes | COCKPIT-R2-01 idea with grill and neck corrected; shared repair with S07-3 |
| Crime boss | Needs fixes | shortlist 2, 8, 5, 10, no winner; which design is "Jabba" is Ziggy's |
| Bounty hunter | Needs fixes | BOBA-ARMOR-01 is an armor concept, not automatically BH-01 or BH-02; BH-01/BH-02 reserved with nothing assigned; which hunter is Ziggy's |
| Bounty puck with A's likeness | Missing | prop design |
| Club set, Chewy anatomy, bouncer | Missing | Chewy cover chosen, no production reference; bouncer is a story intent |
| Ship exterior | Missing | SB-13 differs; silhouette round proposed |
| Warship, Maw, HUD plate | Missing | undesigned; HUD text editorial |
| Leia's sleeve | Unreviewed | costume undecided; show no deciding detail |

## Critical blockers and the next bounded repair

1. **No accepted cockpit still with Dolo seated.** The same repair S07-3 names; one still unblocks S02-6, S04C, S05, S07 and S09. Owner: CFA.
2. **No ship exterior.** One silhouette round, three views, for Ziggy to pick from; it unblocks S02-4's background, S02-8, S02-9, S02-10, S05, S07-7 and S08. If Ziggy supplies flight footage, the silhouette round becomes a match to that footage instead.
3. **No boss decision.** Ziggy names which shortlist design is Jabba; one staging round follows.
4. **No hunter decision.** Ziggy says whether the watcher is Boba (BOBA-ARMOR-01 as the armor concept) or a numbered hunter; one identity round follows. S02-3's puck can be made before it, S02-4 cannot.

## Scene grade and review

Grade: Ungraded. Shoot-plan review: Unreviewed. The reassignment of SB-11 from a run to a held watch, the club cut-in as a new insert, and the warship as a new shot are proposals.

## One coherent draft prompt (S02-5, the neck blaster; silent still, for the macro)

Landscape 16:9, macro close-up of the character-left side of a man's neck (his own left, the side that appears at the viewer's right when he faces camera), from his collarbone to his jawline, the face out of frame above. Warm brown skin, a small tattoo of a smoking blaster pistol with a thin trail of smoke rising toward the jaw, fine linework. A dark brown distressed leather jacket collar at the frame's lower edge, an off-white shirt collar open beneath it. Warm amber practical light from the left; a single cold blue-white light passing across the skin from the right. Shallow focus on the tattoo. No text, no second person, no jewelry in frame.

## First proof, if and when a run is authorized

S02-5, the neck macro. Single subject, locked frame, one light pass, no mouth, no hands, no set. It tests whether the neck tattoo holds at a scale where every line is visible, which every later shot of the character-left side depends on. Accept only if the blaster's linework, side and smoke direction match the neck-bling handoff's placement brief and, once one exists, the accepted neck reference, and nothing else is invented on the skin. Stop on any morph, extra ink or mirrored placement. No retries without a new decision.

— Claude
