# Scene card, prologue — "The tip"

Project: Hon Dolo / Strictly Business. Section: none; this is the frame story before the song, ending on the cut into S01. Author: Claude, lead writer, October 11, 2026. Status: **proposed detailed design**. Scene grade: **Ungraded**. Shoot-plan review: **Unreviewed** (no reviewer, no time). Timing: null, and unlike the song's cards it has no lyric timebase at all; its length is an editorial decision for later. Nothing here authorizes a generation, a run, a download, a sourcing decision or a spend.

Fields follow `comfy/projects/collaborators/work_briefs_20261010/SHOOT_PLAN_VERIFICATION.txt`. Reference rules follow `comfy/projects/visual_library/REFERENCE_POLICY.txt` and the head standard. Sources: the cab handoff `handoffs/informant_cab_144607296_20261009/START_HERE.txt` (HON-INSP-CIVITAI-144607296-20261009, prepared, not executed) and the cast intake `cast/unnamed_informant/intake_20261009.json` (HON-UNNAMED-INFORMANT); the opening prototype `comfy/projects/collaborators/storyboard_detail_20261009/01_hon/workshop_current_20261009/REVIEWED_PLAN.txt` for frame A; the workshop `IMAGE_MANIFEST.json` for A–F; `asset_review_20261007/storyboard_crosswalk.json` for SB-05.

Each shot carries a Source line listing the kinds it could plausibly take (supplied footage, existing asset, generated or animated, transformed material, or a mix). Per Ziggy, directly in the session on October 11 (DECISIONS section 8), that line only says whether we would have to generate the shot ourselves or already have something to use; the shots are written as if we make every one, and the line never alters a shot.

## Story beat

Why the video is about to happen. A woman with information gets into Dolo's cab. This card's proposal for the exchange: she has no fare, so she pays with the only currency she has, the tip from the confirmed weave (DECISIONS section 2): a princess needs a ride off this rock and has money. He takes the tip as the fare, drops the informant where she asks, walks into the cantina, sits at the counter, and the first chorus starts on the customer the tip was about. The song is Dolo's pitch to one specific person, and the prologue is how he knew to make it. The informant's name, backstory and exact information remain open in the record; "no fare" is a story proposal, not a biography.

What this does for the piece: it puts the irony in place before a note plays (a man who charges for everything has just been paid in information), it gives the informant a job without inventing a biography, and it keeps her out of the song's ending, so the farewell stays between him and Leia. Whether she returns after the song, as the witness at the thaw, is open (DECISIONS section 5).

Constraints carried from the record: the informant is not Leia and has no name, backstory or relationship assigned (cast intake, Ziggy's own words: "a unknown generic informant for now"); her pictured look (short silver hair with pink ends, cream cropped jacket, mechanical forearm, wet neon ledge) is external inspiration only and no production adaptation is accepted; Dolo's face, mouth (external-off, four gold caps, two plain lip hoops), cheek lettering, neck blaster, chest ship and wrist accessories are the current references exactly as the cab handoff lists them; the wrist side is set explicitly for this scene and is not canon; one coherent outfit must be chosen before cabin frames (this card proposes the opening outfit; no source records that choice for the cab); the first proofs are silent; dialogue is a separately prepared step; the r4 iced look is not imported. Whether the informant returns in the epilogue is still open (DECISIONS section 5).

## Screen geography

The landing is at screen-right; the cab arrives from screen-left and stops alongside with its passenger door and step facing the landing; she boards moving screen-left into the cabin. The cab leaves by lifting, turning its nose away from camera and sliding into the traffic in depth, so it never crosses the landing it came alongside; the same at her stop. Interior: a side-by-side cabin seen from the front through the windscreen, Dolo at the controls screen-left, the informant in the passenger seat screen-right; her eyeline to him is screen-left, his glance to her is screen-right. The cantina, as the choruses card lays it out: the entrance on the front wall, the booth on the back wall, the counter along the right-hand wall. The cantina walk (P-7) is shot from the booth's side looking toward the entrance, the reverse of S01-2's view, so the door is in frame and he walks toward camera to the counter at screen-right.

The wrist chain and dark band go on the character-right wrist for this scene, matching the opening prototype's provisional blocking choice, so the frame story and the song agree without either claiming canon.

## Shots, in order

### P-1 Waiting above the city (the handoff's P01)
- Purpose: establish her, the landing and the incoming cab, and that she is waiting for something she cannot afford.
- Direction: a wet landing high above a neon city, a large moon. The informant sits at the landing's edge, screen-right, weight on one hand. Far off at screen-left, a cab's lights separate from the traffic and come toward her. She does not look up until they do.
- Camera: wide, locked, the city below; a safe continuous surface under her, not a void.
- Lighting: neon from below, moonlight from above, wet reflections.
- Start/end intent: start on the city with her small in it; end with the cab's lights grown large at screen-left and her head turning.
- References: the user-supplied screenshot `cast/unnamed_informant/source/civitai_144607296_user_screenshot.png` (inspiration only; the original clip was never downloaded or played; no production adaptation exists). Her design is open.
- Continuity: her look, once adapted and accepted, holds through P-6.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated from an accepted informant adaptation and a city plate; a supplied clip of a figure on a ledge above a city with the likeness replaced; a mix.
- Missing art: the informant as a production character; the landing and city as a set.

### P-2 The cab comes alongside (P02)
- Purpose: the vehicle, and the geometry every later cab shot depends on.
- Direction: the cab brakes and settles level with the landing, its passenger door and step toward her, hover height held. She stands and turns toward the opening. The door opens; she does not board yet.
- Camera: medium wide from the landing's side, locked; door, step and the gap between cab and landing all visible.
- Lighting: the cab's running lights on the wet surface; neon.
- Start/end intent: start with the cab arriving; end stopped, door open, her turned toward it.
- References: none; the cab exterior, door, step and interior are undesigned (cab handoff, "Missing now").
- Continuity: the door side, hover height and the landing gap are fixed here and do not change in P-3.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: this is the shot most likely to take supplied footage if a clip of a hover vehicle settling at a ledge exists; generated from a cab design; a mix.
- Missing art: the cab.

### P-3 Boarding (P03)
- Purpose: the physical-action proof the handoff is built around: one connected boarding that keeps geometry and contact.
- Direction: a stable side three-quarter view. One hand to the door frame, one foot to the step, weight transfers into the cabin, she sits. The door stays open for the proof. One informant throughout; no teleport, no duplicate.
- Camera: side three-quarter, locked, the cab stopped.
- Lighting: as P-2.
- Start/end intent: start with her outside, hand reaching; end with her seated inside, door still open.
- References: as P-1 and P-2. The handoff's accept and stop rules govern this shot as written there (they are not restated here).
- Continuity: her seat position at the end of this shot is her position at the start of P-5.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated (the handoff's prepared first Comfy proof, image-to-video from a reviewed start frame toward a designed end state, which is a review target unless the chosen graph has a verified end-frame input); a supplied boarding clip with the likeness replaced; a mix. Whether the task needs explicit start/end control or an authored motion source is the open research question in the handoff.
- Missing art: the informant adaptation; the cab; a reviewed start frame and end state.

### P-4 The door and the lift (new)
- Purpose: the later beat the handoff separates: the door closes and the cab goes.
- Direction: the door closes; the cab lifts a hand's width, turns its nose away from camera and slides into the traffic in depth, growing small. The landing is empty.
- Camera: the P-2 framing, locked; the cab leaves into depth, not across the landing.
- Lighting: as P-2.
- Start/end intent: start on the open door; end on the empty landing.
- References: as P-2.
- Continuity: the cab departs into depth here and in P-6; it never crosses a landing it has come alongside.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: as P-2; the most footage-friendly shot in the prologue.
- Missing art: the cab.

### P-5 The first exchange (P04)
- Purpose: the tip. The handoff's interior two-shot: informant in the passenger seat, Dolo at the controls, a restrained businesslike acknowledgment. The first proof is silent; the lines come later.
- Direction: through the windscreen, side by side: Dolo screen-left at the controls, eyes on the traffic; the informant screen-right. She looks at him (screen-left). He glances once (screen-right), takes her in, looks back at the traffic. In the silent proof that is the whole shot. For the written version, this card proposes the exchange's content (the record leaves her exact information open): she has no fare; she has something better; a princess needs a ride off this rock and has money; he asks what that is worth to her; she says the ride; the half-smile. The lines themselves are not written here and are a separate step.
- Camera: frontal two-shot through the windscreen, locked; both faces readable; hands clear of faces.
- Lighting: dashboard practicals warm from below, neon passing cold across both faces from screen-right to screen-left as the cab moves.
- Start/end intent: start on both looking forward; end after his glance, both forward again, his half-smile just arriving.
- References: face A `HD-RETURN-6c8900223ee9`; mouth B `HD-B-91ef00348229` (external-off; the lips stay closed or minimally parted in the silent proof); wrist chain and band F `HD-DROP-b18c4a123579` on the character-right wrist (set for this scene, not canon); the opening outfit (dark brown distressed leather jacket over the open off-white shirt, chest ship visible) as the one coherent outfit; the informant as adapted. Cheek lettering cursive "eye" character-right/viewer-left, serif "know" character-left/viewer-right, neck blaster character-left, no forehead dice, one hoop per nostril and ear hoop with crystal stud as targets.
- Continuity: this is the piece's only two-character frame built for dialogue (the cantina wides hold Dolo and Chewie at a distance), and the handoff makes it the proof after boarding is accepted. The mouth, cheek and neck art and wrist jewelry are explicit failure checks.
- Lane note: not a song shot; if dialogue is later recorded, whether it is spoken or sung is a decision for then, and the external-off mouth rule holds either way.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated two-shot from a reviewed cabin still (the handoff's next proof after boarding); a supplied clip of two people in a vehicle with both likenesses replaced; a mix.
- Missing art: the cab interior; a reviewed two-character cabin frame; the informant; the dialogue.

### P-6 The drop (new)
- Purpose: she gets what she paid for; he gets what he came for. She leaves the song here.
- Direction: the cab sets down at a street landing, screen-right. She steps out (the P-3 action in reverse, door open, one hand to the frame), does not look back, and walks off screen-right into the crowd. The cab lifts, turns its nose away from camera and goes into the traffic in depth.
- Camera: medium wide from the street, locked.
- Lighting: street neon, the cab's lights.
- Start/end intent: start on the cab settling; end on the cab gone and her gone, the street as it was.
- References: as P-2 and P-3.
- Continuity: she does not appear inside the song. If Ziggy wants her back as the witness in the epilogue (DECISIONS section 5), the epilogue card's E-1 gains one beat; nothing here changes.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: as P-2 and P-4.
- Missing art: the cab; the street as a set.

### P-7 The cantina walk (SB-05, the last shot before the song)
- Purpose: Dolo walks into the cantina and sits at the counter. The walk is the prologue's last beat; the song starts on the cut that follows it. This is the reverse of the choruses card's S01-2, which looks from the entrance toward the back wall with him already seated.
- Direction: the cantina from the booth's side, looking toward the entrance on the front wall; the counter along the right-hand wall at screen-right; the booth's edge and Chewie's shoulder at frame-left foreground, out of focus. The door opens; Dolo enters at the far wall and walks toward camera through the room to the counter at screen-right. He sits.
- Camera: wide, locked, from the back of the room.
- Lighting: warm practicals on the counter, the door's spill at the far wall.
- Start/end intent: start on the closed door at the far wall; end on him seated at the counter, settled.
- References: SB-05 `HD-DROP-6e8eb6a956c9` for the idea (cantina walk; its lead and DJ anatomy differ and do not govern). Chewie: no accepted anatomy.
- Continuity: the counter along the right-hand wall, the booth on the back wall, the entrance on the front wall, as the choruses card; the seated position is frame A's.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: a supplied cantina or club wide with the walk and the booth composited; generated from a room design; a mix.
- Missing art: the cantina set; Chewbacca.

Hand-off: hard cut from the settle to S01-1, the mouth insert, as the song begins; then S01-2 (the room from the entrance side, Dolo already seated) and S01-3 (frame A) as the choruses card has them. The customer the tip was about is across the counter, offscreen.

## Cut logic

1 → 2 on her head turning to the cab arriving. 2 → 3 on the door opening to her hand on the frame. 3 → 4 on her seated to the door closing. 4 → 5 on the cab leaving the landing to the windscreen two-shot, the first time we see Dolo. 5 → 6 on his half-smile to the cab settling at her stop. 6 → 7 on the cab leaving to the cantina's far door opening. 7 → S01-1 on the settle, the mouth insert, and the song.

The prologue has no mouth insert and no lip-sync of its own. Its dialogue two-shot (P-5) is the handoff's second proof and is not attempted before boarding is accepted.

## Required ingredients

| Ingredient | State | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Informant, production adaptation | Missing | HON-UNNAMED-INFORMANT; screenshot is inspiration only; anatomy of the mechanical arm needs design |
| Cab (exterior, door, step, interior) | Missing | undesigned; geometry fixed in P-2 |
| Landing, street and city | Missing | sets |
| Reviewed boarding start frame and end state | Missing | the handoff's first proof inputs |
| Reviewed two-character cabin frame | Missing | the handoff's second proof input |
| Dolo face A, mouth B, wrist F | Ready | as the manifest limits them; wrist side set for this scene only |
| Opening outfit for the cab | Proposed | the handoff requires one coherent outfit chosen before cabin frames; this card proposes the opening outfit; no source records the choice |
| Cantina set, Chewbacca | Missing | P-7 shares them with the song |
| Dialogue | Missing | a separately prepared step; content proposed above, lines not written |

## Critical blockers and the next bounded repair

1. **No informant adaptation.** One reference round that turns the inspiration into a project-owned character (front and side, the mechanical forearm resolved), under the head standard's review discipline. Owner: CFA, after Ziggy chooses the direction.
2. **No cab.** One design round: exterior with door and step, interior with two seats and a windscreen, in three views. It unblocks P-2 through P-6.
3. **Boarding not proven.** The handoff's first Comfy proof, exactly as it bounds it (one short boarding, fixed camera, stopped cab, one preview at low cost, no retries). Not before 1 and 2.
4. **Dialogue unwritten.** One page, after Ziggy confirms the content of the exchange above.

## Scene grade and review

Grade: Ungraded. Shoot-plan review: Unreviewed. P-4, P-6 and P-7 are proposals beyond the handoff's four beats; the content of the exchange (no fare; the tip as the fare), the opening outfit for the cab, and the cab's departure vectors are proposals for Ziggy.

## One coherent draft prompt (P-2, the cab alongside; silent still, for the geometry)

Landscape 16:9, medium wide, night. A wet metal landing at the right of frame, high above a neon city, a large moon above. A small hovering cab has just settled level with the landing at the left of frame, its passenger door open toward the landing and a fold-down step extended, a narrow gap of dark air between step and landing edge. Running lights reflected on the wet surface. No people in frame. No text, no second vehicle.

## First proof, if and when a run is authorized

The handoff's own: P-3, the boarding, after a reviewed start frame and end state exist, one preview, fixed seed, no retries, with the handoff's accept and stop rules. Before that, the still above (P-2 geometry, no people) is the cheapest check that the cab design holds: door side, step, gap and hover height, which every later cab shot inherits.

— Claude

# Scene card, epilogue — "Back in business"

Project: Hon Dolo / Strictly Business. Section: none; this is the frame story after the song, from the slab to the mirror. Author: Claude, lead writer, October 11, 2026. Status: **proposed detailed design**. Scene grade: **Ungraded**. Shoot-plan review: **Unreviewed** (no reviewer, no time). Timing: null, and no lyric timebase; nothing here is inside the song and no beat carries a song timestamp; its length is an editorial decision for later. Nothing here authorizes a generation, a run, a download, a sourcing decision or a spend.

Fields follow `comfy/projects/collaborators/work_briefs_20261010/SHOOT_PLAN_VERIFICATION.txt`. Reference rules follow `comfy/projects/visual_library/REFERENCE_POLICY.txt` and the head standard. Sources: the quarters package `story/quarters_grill_change_20261009/` (`START_HERE.txt`, `REVIEW.txt`, `asset_ledger.json`; GROK-HD-SB-GRILLUP-v001, received October 9, panels need fixes, not accepted); the workshop `IMAGE_MANIFEST.json` for A, B, F; `asset_review_20261007/storyboard_crosswalk.json` for SB-30.

Each shot carries a Source line listing the kinds it could plausibly take (supplied footage, existing asset, generated or animated, transformed material, or a mix). Per Ziggy, directly in the session on October 11 (DECISIONS section 8), that line only says whether we would have to generate the shot ourselves or already have something to use; the shots are written as if we make every one, and the line never alters a shot.

## Story beat

Real life resumes. The song set the boast against the slab in its last chorus and closed on the mouth (S12-2); the epilogue goes back to the chamber and says he paid the price and survived it. A short thaw, then Dolo alone in his quarters: he sits at the mirror, the lip rings come out, the case opens, the iced grill goes in, the mirror gives him back his smile, and he turns to leave. He is getting ready to charge somebody again. The last ironic beat of the piece is that the man who paid is back in business, and the one mouth change in the whole piece happens here, on camera.

Why the thaw is here and not in the song: the crosswalk's note on SB-30 reads "Thaw/reunion is a source invention, not established in lyrics; may weaken sacrifice ending." My reading of that: inside the song it would; outside the song it does the opposite, because the ending stands and then the frame story takes it back without undoing it. Ziggy said yes to the thaw moving to the frame (DECISIONS section 3, row 5).

Constraints carried from the record: the song's mouth is external-off; the r4 iced anchor (`HEAD-HD-ICED-ANCHOR-LOCK-r4.jpg`, `HD-GRILLUP-40064d98db89`) is Ziggy's selection for this external-grill look, with the lip piercings removed for this look only, and that selection accepts neither the storyboard nor a rule for every grill variant; the ten quarters panels are drafts with a label-content conflict between the files named 02 and 03, a three-hoop count in panel 04 against two in panel 10, and identity, tattoo, jewelry and grill drift across 06–10; CFA's five repair priorities (`REVIEW.txt`) come before any of these beats is detailed past this card; the established Leigh hand-art reference and gold hand rings are to be preserved whenever hands are visible (the drafts drop them), while the exact hand-art transfer stays unresolved per the opening brief; no song timestamp is assigned to any of it; whether the informant returns as a witness is open (DECISIONS section 5).

Proposals, not record: the iced look's only scene is this one; the thaw is with Chewie and Leia does not appear (the farewell was the farewell); the mirror reveal is the last frame.

## Screen geography

The chamber as S10: cool light from screen-left, the doorway at screen-left where S10-4 placed Chewie. The quarters, as this card lays them out (SB-GRILL-01 supplies only a wide ship doorway with the warm cabin behind it; the bureau, the mirror and the screen sides are this card's placements): the doorway at screen-left, the bureau and its mirror against the wall at screen-right, the case and a small dish on the bureau. He enters moving screen-right and ends facing the mirror at screen-right; the exit turns him back toward screen-left. In every mirror shot, the direct face and the reflection must match in expression, lettering, jewelry and hand position (priority 5), which the drafts do not yet do.

The ten quarters beats are written in the board's numeric order, one shot each, with the pixels for beats 2 and 3 drawn from the files the label conflict swapped: the mirror portrait is in the file named 03, the removal close-up in the file named 02. Names and numeric order are preserved here as the review asks; the reorder is of content, not of filenames.

## Shots, in order

### E-1 The thaw (SB-30 repurposed)
- Purpose: he comes out of it. Not a reunion with Leia; a release, with Chewie there because Chewie was asked to be.
- Direction: the chamber, the slab upright, cool light from screen-left. The relief's vapor reverses: the carbonite softens, the surface cracks along the raised hands first, and the man slumps forward out of it. Chewie, from the doorway at screen-left, catches the weight. Dolo's eyes do not open in this shot. Two beats: the crack, the catch.
- Camera: medium wide, locked; the slab centered, Chewie entering from screen-left.
- Lighting: the chamber's cool light; the vapor catching it; a faint warm glow from the floor.
- Start/end intent: start on the slab as S10-7 showed it; end on Chewie holding him, both still.
- References: SB-30 `HD-DROP-32580c30003c` for the idea only (its two-shot is a reunion the lyrics do not establish; its pairing does not govern); the slab prop from S10-7 (undesigned); face A `HD-RETURN-6c8900223ee9` for the relief and the face as it emerges; wrist chain and band F `HD-DROP-b18c4a123579` on the character-right wrist in the relief, as S10-7 (provisional); Chewbacca: no accepted anatomy.
- Continuity: the raised hands and the chain match S10-7 exactly; the opening outfit under the carbonite.
- Optional beat, pending Ziggy: the informant as the witness, standing at the chamber's far edge, screen-right, opposite the doorway, saying nothing. Not written into the shot until he decides (DECISIONS section 5).
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated from the slab prop still with a crack-and-fall effect; a supplied clip of a figure falling forward out of a wall relief if one exists, with the likeness replaced; transformed; a mix.
- Missing art: the slab prop; the chamber; Chewbacca.

### E-2 The doorway (beat 01, SB-GRILL-01)
- Purpose: his quarters. Alone, upright, himself.
- Direction: a wide of the cabin: Dolo enters through the doorway at screen-left and crosses to the bureau at screen-right, where the closed case and the empty dish sit. He does not hurry.
- Camera: wide, locked.
- Lighting: cabin practicals, warm; the mirror catching a cool spill.
- Start/end intent: start on the empty room; end with him at the bureau, hands on its edge.
- References: SB-GRILL-01 `HD-GRILLUP-a9e6f58d0b70` for the doorway and the warm cabin behind it only (its face, tattoos and bare hands do not govern; the room's layout beyond the doorway is this card's); A, F as above; the opening outfit.
- Continuity: the room's geometry is set here; every later beat is inside it.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated from an accepted cabin layout still; a supplied interior clip with the figure composited; a mix.
- Missing art: the cabin as a set; a corrected panel.

### E-3 The mirror (beat 02 by story order; the pixels are in the file named 03)
- Purpose: the first look at himself since the counter. Priority 1's progression begins here: mirror, then removal, then dish.
- Direction: the bureau and mirror portrait: Dolo seated at the bureau facing the mirror at screen-right, seen over his character-left shoulder so the mirror holds his face; the direct view holds his shoulder and his character-right hand resting on the bureau, away from the mouth. He looks at himself. One beat. The reflection matches the direct view in expression, lettering, jewelry and the hand's position.
- Camera: over the character-left shoulder into the mirror, locked; the same framing every later mirror shot uses.
- Lighting: bureau practicals, warm; the mirror's cool spill.

- Direction: close on the mouth and the character-right hand, from the front, the mirror not in this shot: fingers pinch the first lower-lip hoop and ease it out; then the second. The teeth, where the lips part, are the song's external-off set: four gold caps, white central incisors, lower silver/chrome; not long canines, not a white lower row. Two hoops, never three. The hand carries the established gold hand rings and the Leigh hand-art reference where visible; frame so nothing unresolved about the art has to be invented.

- Continuity: priority 2 (the two-hoop count across removal, dish and exit) and priority 3's first half (external-off teeth in the removal close-up) are the gates for this shot.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated close-up from an accepted mouth still with a hand action; a supplied clip would need to carry our mouth, the least likely kind but not excluded.
- Missing art: a corrected removal panel; the corrected mouth ECU the choruses card also needs.

### E-5 Rings in the dish (beat 04, SB-GRILL-04)
- Purpose: the hoops set down. The props that will still be there at the exit.
- Direction: insert on the bureau: the character-right hand sets two hoops into the small dish beside the closed case and withdraws. Two hoops in the dish, none in the hand.
- Camera: insert, locked, slightly high.
- Lighting: bureau practicals.
- Start/end intent: start on the empty dish and the closed case; end on two hoops in the dish.
- References: SB-GRILL-04 `HD-GRILLUP-894990536803` for the idea only (it shows three hoops, generic hand tattoos and no gold hand rings; the count and the hands do not govern); F on the wrist (character-right, provisional); the gold hand rings and the Leigh hand-art reference where the hand shows.

- Purpose: the iced grill, in its case, the first time the audience sees it.
- Direction: insert: the case opens; two iced rows on their bed, the r4 geometry (short even contour, not long fangs). The character-right hand rests on the lid. The dish with its two hoops beside the case.
- Camera: insert, locked, slightly high.

- References: SB-GRILL-05 `HD-GRILLUP-aa4962b0cbaa` for composition only (its long pointed canines differ from r4 and do not govern); the r4 anchor `HD-GRILLUP-40064d98db89` for the grill's shape.

- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated prop insert from an r4-derived grill design; a supplied jewelry-case insert with the grill composited; a mix.

- Camera: medium, locked, from the front; the mirror not in frame.
- Lighting: bureau practicals.

- References: SB-GRILL-07 `HD-GRILLUP-fde483650ebb` for staging only (its different face, large star-like neck tattoo and changed brow do not govern; its held piece is not an r4 match and its fingers lack the character's gold rings); A; F; the gold hand rings; the r4 anchor for the piece.

- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated from an accepted standing still with the prop; a supplied clip would need to carry our face, the least likely kind but not excluded.

### E-9 Grill in (beat 08, SB-GRILL-08)
- Purpose: the change itself, in the mirror.
- Direction: the E-3 framing: Dolo facing the mirror at screen-right, over his character-left shoulder; the character-right hand seats the upper row, then the lower. The reflection and the direct view agree in every detail visible in both.

- Purpose: the smile that pays. The r4 look, lip rings out, in the mirror. The piece's last frame if Ziggy takes the recommendation.
- Direction: the E-3 framing. The lips part; the iced grill; the smile is the salesman's half-smile from the counter, made of different metal. Hold. The eyes in the reflection meet the lens.
- Camera: as E-3.
- Lighting: as E-3, the grill catching the cool spill.
- Start/end intent: start lips closed; end on the held smile.
- References: SB-GRILL-09 `HD-GRILLUP-1c67855e0139` for layout only (different face and major neck, cheek and brow differences; tooth row not verified against r4); the r4 anchor `HD-GRILLUP-40064d98db89` governs the look.
- Continuity: no lip hoops, by Ziggy's selection for this look; everything else about the head per A.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated from the r4 anchor in the mirror framing; a supplied clip would need to carry this exact mouth, the least likely kind but not excluded.

### E-11 The exit (beat 10, SB-GRILL-10): the board's ending, kept as the alternate
- Purpose: the board ends on the turn-back exit with the open empty case and two hoops in the dish. Kept as the alternate ending; the recommendation is to end on E-10.
- Direction: he turns from the mirror toward the doorway, screen-left, one look back over the character-right shoulder at the bureau: the open empty case, the two hoops in the dish. Then he goes.
- Camera: wide, the E-2 framing, locked.
- Lighting: cabin practicals.
- Start/end intent: start on the turn; end on the empty doorway.
- References: SB-GRILL-10 `HD-GRILLUP-5c213b5307ad` for the props' idea (open empty case, two hoops in the dish); its face, tattoos, nose jewelry and dental pattern differ from r4 and do not govern.
- Continuity: two hoops in the dish (E-5); the case open and empty (E-6, E-8).
- Source: TBD. Plausible: as E-2.
- Missing art: a corrected panel.

## Cut logic

E-1 → E-2 on Chewie's hold to the empty room: the hardest cut in the piece, from the chamber to home, no travel shown. 2 → 3 on hands on the bureau's edge to the same hand resting on it in the mirror. 3 → 4 on his look at himself to the fingers at the lip, the mirror left behind. 4 → 5 on the hoops in the fingers to the hoops in the dish. 5 → 6 on the hand leaving the dish to the hand opening the case. 6 → 7 on the open case to him looking down at it. 7 → 8 on the hand moving to the piece lifting. 8 → 9 on the piece below the mouth to the mirror. 9 → 10 inside the mirror, lips closed to lips parted. End on 10; or 10 → 11 on the smile to the turn, and end on the doorway.

Proposed last frame: E-10, the mirror. The piece began on a mouth (S01-1) and ends on one. The exit is a fine ending too, and it is Ziggy's call; both are written.

## Required ingredients

| Ingredient | State | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Slab prop and chamber | Missing | from S10-7; E-1 reuses them |
| Chewbacca | Missing | E-1; the same repair every card names |
| r4 iced anchor | Ready as selected | `HD-GRILLUP-40064d98db89`, Ziggy's selection for this look; lip piercings removed for this look only |
| Iced grill as a prop | Missing | built from r4 geometry; E-6 through E-10 |
| Cabin set | Missing | SB-GRILL-01 gives a doorway and a warm cabin behind it; the rest is this card's layout |
| Ten quarters panels | Needs fixes | drafts; the 02/03 label conflict, the hoop count, teeth, r4 geometry, head and jewelry continuity, hand art and rings, mirror consistency |
| Dolo face A, mouth B, wrist F | Ready | as the manifest limits them; B governs E-3 and E-4's teeth, r4 governs E-10's |
| Gold hand rings, Leigh hand-art reference | Needs fixes | established references the drafts drop; exact transfer unresolved; frame to avoid inventing it |
| Informant as witness | Open | Ziggy's call; one optional beat in E-1 |

## Critical blockers and the next bounded repair

1. **The five repair priorities** (`REVIEW.txt`): resolve the 02/03 manifest mismatch and keep the mirror → removal → dish progression (E-3, E-4, E-5 here); the two-hoop count across removal, dish and exit with the deliberate no-lip-rings final state; external-off teeth in the removal close-up and true r4 geometry for the case, held, inserted and revealed grill; head, face marks, neck, nose and ear jewelry and hand and wrist accessories held across frames; mirror consistency. The review asks for a bounded repair brief, not a batch; who prepares it and which provider receives it are Ziggy's and Nova's calls.
2. **No grill prop.** One design pass from the r4 anchor, reviewed as a prop.
3. **No slab, chamber or Chewbacca** for E-1: shared with S10.
4. **The witness question.** Ziggy says whether the informant returns; one line either way.

## Scene grade and review

Grade: Ungraded. Shoot-plan review: Unreviewed. The thaw with Chewie (not Leia), the mirror as the last frame, the informant as an optional witness, the room layout and the content reorder of beats 2 and 3 are proposals; the ten beats follow the board's numeric order, one shot each.

## One coherent draft prompt (E-6, the case; silent still, for the prop)

Landscape 16:9, close insert looking slightly down at a small open jewelry case on a worn metal bureau, warm practical light from the front-left. Inside, on a dark bed, two dental grills: an upper row and a lower row, both set with small clear stones over polished metal, short even contours, no long pointed teeth. A hand with warm brown skin rests on the open lid at the right edge of frame, a flattened gold curb-link chain and a dark band at the wrist. Beside the case, a small shallow dish holding two small plain metal hoops. No face, no text, no mirror.

## First proof, if and when a run is authorized

Not this scene, and not before the song's proofs. When the quarters are repaired, the first proof is E-5, the hoops into the dish: one hand, two small objects, one placement, no face, no mirror. It tests contact and object count, the two things the drafts get wrong. Accept only if two hoops leave the hand and two sit in the dish, the chain stays on the wrist, the hand's rings hold, and nothing is invented on the hand. Stop on a third hoop, a morph or a changed case.

— Claude

# Scene card, between the music — "Chewy at work" (first Flow / Gemini prototype set)

Project: Hon Dolo / Strictly Business. Section: none; a frame-story beat Ziggy asked for in the Pent House on October 12 ("scenes of Chewbacca helping out, doing work... write a storyboard, have the metadata indicate we want to flow this to Flow and Gemini"). Author: Claude, lead writer, October 12, 2026. Status: **proposed**; the five source frames are preliminary Grok drafts; nothing here is accepted art, an accepted reference, a timing or a run. Each frame's metadata follows `VIDEO_PROTOTYPE_BRIEF_STANDARD.md`; the dispatch of any run is CFA Nova's under the production method, and Ziggy's gate is the actual video.

## Story beat

The ship is down on a dry world at sunset and there is cargo to move. Nobody sings. Chewy does the work: crates down the ramp, crates in the hold, the case of credits checked, and then, the job done, his hands go to the decks and the ship's lights answer him. Dolo walks away from the ship toward the business, as he does. It is the cheapest story in the piece to prove on video, because it is one character doing one physical thing per shot, and it gives the music video's three recurring Chewy images (the boards, the look, the fader) a life outside the song.

No bosses, no enforcer, no Leia: Ziggy wants the bosses handled with special care for IP reasons, so this set stays with the crew.

**Refinement applied (2026-10-12, mailbox 98220a40):** every output from these frames enters Preliminary with no per-image gate; the accepted foundations (face, mouth, wrist, the DJB sheet) do not approve the new scene; each output gets separate Complete look, Scene, Details and Outfit notes, never averaged. Lighting per frame is stated as sources below: W-1 and W-2 the low sun as the key with the hull in shadow; W-3 the hold's practicals and one cold spill; W-4 the credits' own glow as the key on his face; W-5 the console's small lights (and, in the C20 source, the corridor neon, which is the continuity defect recorded there). The actions chosen avoid body-to-object contact physics except the crate carry, which is a hold, not a climb.

## Frames, in order, with prototype metadata

Archive root: `docs\notes\downloads\`. Grok scores are the swarm's preliminary self-scores; mine are from `CLAUDE_GRADES_20261012.md`. "Target" names the providers Ziggy wants a prototype from; nothing is dispatched by this card.

### W-1 Down the ramp
- Source: `GROK-HD-FALCON-1000/C44-chewy-boarding/C44-chewy-boarding-001.jpg`, SHA-256 `9900dcd673ce6b6a1ee13512a6d5c2572bf147a764a48acb415eeddddd6776bb`, 283,433 bytes; Grok L5 S5; Claude L5 S5.
- Locks visible: Chewy per the DJB sheet (dark gorilla-like beast, black over-ear headphones, gold neck chain, bullet bandolier); the ship's ramp and hull (one silhouette candidate, undecided).
- Declared change, one action: Chewy carries the crate down the ramp toward the ground, three or four steps, and stops at the foot; the crate stays level; nothing else moves but dust.
- Sides: the ramp runs from the hull at screen-right down to the ground at screen-left; he moves screen-left.
- Camera: locked; no push.
- Bound: one clip, the model's native short length (six seconds at Flow002's settings), 1280x720; no retries.
- Target: Flow (video from this frame); Gemini (a second scene from the same frame, as HaL's Lisan brief does).
- Acceptance checks: the beast's face, headphones, chain and bandolier hold at start, middle and end; four fingers and a thumb on each hand; the crate's geometry constant; no second figure; no morph of the ramp.
- Defects known: none in the frame; the sunset haze may drift.

### W-2 Walking away from the ship
- Source: `GROK-HD-FALCON-1000/C42-ramp-landing/C42-ramp-landing-001.jpg`, SHA-256 `9f4d516f4ab8f10f541c7494409eaa406682b04bc0e889d6ef9e681c97a0cf6a`, 306,604 bytes; Grok L5 S5; Claude L4 (Dolo) / L5 (Chewy) S5.
- Locks visible: Dolo's face per lf_full, cheek words on the correct sides, two lip hoops, ear hoop, neck blaster character-left, the jacket over the open shirt; Chewy with a crate on the ramp behind.
- Declared change, one action: Dolo walks two steps toward camera and past its right edge while Chewy takes one step down the ramp; the sun stays put.
- Sides: Dolo exits screen-right; Chewy moves screen-left down the ramp.
- Camera: locked.
- Bound: as W-1.
- Target: Flow; Gemini.
- Acceptance checks: Dolo's cheek words, hoops and neck blaster at start, middle and end; no new tattoos; Chewy's beast holds at small scale.
- Defects known: **Dolo wears an extra gold neck chain he does not have, and it hides the chest ship.** For a Prime-lane shot the source needs a repair (remove the chain, show the open shirt) before use; as a motion test the frame is usable with the defect recorded. Ziggy's call.

### W-3 In the hold
- Source: `GROK-HD-FALCON-1000/C67-cargo-hold-dolo-chewy/C67-cargo-hold-dolo-chewy-002.jpg`, SHA-256 `a1a553116a1d985b0c6a151cf79c52c7b95e4c9b70055daf615ffd72839bf0df`, 274,946 bytes; Grok L5 S5; Claude L5 / L5 S5.
- Locks visible: Dolo chest-up, cheek words correct, two lip hoops, both ear pieces, neck blaster character-left; Chewy among crates and netting at screen-left.
- Declared change, one action: Chewy lifts the nearest crate and sets it on the stack behind him; Dolo holds still, one blink, eyes on camera.
- Sides: Chewy at screen-left, crates at screen-left; Dolo screen-right of center.
- Camera: locked.
- Bound: as W-1.
- Target: Flow; Gemini.
- Acceptance checks: Dolo's face and marks unchanged through the clip (he is the still element; any drift fails the clip); Chewy's hands and the crate coherent; the netting does not morph.
- Defects known: the chest ship is not visible (the shirt sits higher); acceptable for this frame.

### W-4 The case
- Source: `GROK-HD-FALCON-1000/C30-cargo/C30-cargo-013.jpg`, SHA-256 `d6b65339e87a0da082e8e1627310d9c84877e9cd7a061d91ed8a6f4298d77ef4`, 266,564 bytes; Grok L5 S5; Claude L5 S5.
- Locks visible: Chewy per the DJB sheet, close; the open case with four luminous credits; crates.
- Declared change, one action: his eyes drop from the lens to the credits and the glow brightens a step; the lid does not move.
- Sides: the case at screen-left-low, his face screen-right.
- Camera: locked.
- Bound: as W-1.
- Target: Flow; Gemini.
- Acceptance checks: four credits, countable, start to end; no readable text; the beast's face holds.
- Defects known: none.

### W-5 The decks
- Source: `GROK-HD-FALCON-1000/C20-fader-push/C20-fader-push-001.jpg`, SHA-256 `8c55b4a2cfdc1275e14f532b881f59f57542a43c2ef3890d8490df57f917fade`, 279,611 bytes; Grok L5 S5; Claude L5 S4 (the beast holds; the corridor is lit with magenta and cyan neon rather than the Falcon's warm practicals). Alternate: `GROK-HD-ENABLERS-03/E13-chewy-hands-actions/E13-chewy-hands-actions-004.jpg`, SHA-256 `b7e2f2956d31c1f74d6eb28c22d5209f21ac94a9c822908fb494886a7e627367`, Claude L5 S4 (club-like void, not the Falcon lounge).
- Locks visible: Chewy per the DJB sheet at the decks.
- Declared change, one action: one fader push, screen-left to screen-right, hand and fader in contact throughout; the practicals pulse once as it lands (the S04-7 beat, here as frame-story rehearsal).
- Sides: fader travels screen-right.
- Camera: locked.
- Bound: as W-1.
- Target: Flow; Gemini.
- Acceptance checks: hand stays on the fader; finger count holds; the decks' geometry constant; no second hand appears.
- Defects known: the neon lighting breaks lounge continuity with W05/W06 v002; acceptable for an action test, or swap the source for a C19 frame in the warm lounge after a view.

## Cut logic

1 → 2 on the crate reaching the ground to Dolo walking; 2 → 3 on Dolo leaving frame to the hold; 3 → 4 on the crate landing to the case; 4 → 5 on his eyes dropping to his hands on the decks. Five shots, five single actions, no dialogue, no song. If only one clip is run first, run W-1: one character, one action, no face lock to fail on.

## Required before any run (per the standard and the method)

- CFA Nova names the mode and model actually offered, verifies the displayed cost and the allowance, and dispatches; unknown cost or access is a stop.
- Each output saved unchanged with its hash beside the source hash; mailbox to `nova` and `claude`; candidate until Ziggy reviews the actual video.
- W-2 needs Ziggy's call on the neck-chain defect (repair first, or motion test as is).
- No lip motion, no song timing, no second character added by the model.

## Scene grade and review

Grade: Ungraded. Shoot-plan review: Unreviewed. Source frames preliminary. This card is the writer's version of the storyboard Ziggy asked the Grok team to draft; when the Chief's and Z_6's draft instructions arrive, they are reviewed against this card and the standard, and the better framing of each shot wins.

— Claude

# CHEWY AT WORK — storyboard and Flow / Gemini prototype briefs, v001

Metadata: video_lane=flow,gemini; stage=prototype brief
Project: Hon Dolo / Strictly Business. A frame-story beat between the music, not part of any song section.
Author: Grok Chief of Staff (grok_chief), 2026-10-12, America/New_York. Owner: Chief of Staff.
Basis:
- Claude's `SCENE_CARD_CHEWY_AT_WORK.md`, with frames W-1..W-5 from C44-001, C42-001, C67-002, C30-013 and C20-001.
- Our added picks: C67-011, C21-009 and E13-011.

Standard: `VIDEO_PROTOTYPE_BRIEF_STANDARD.md`. Every frame below fills all eleven fields.
Status: PROPOSED. All sources are preliminary Grok drafts, not accepted references. This file authorizes no run. Dispatch belongs to CFA Nova under the production method of October 12, and Ziggy's gate is the actual video.
IP caution: there are no bosses, no enforcer and no Leia in this set, per Ziggy's instruction to take special care with the bosses.

Archive root for every source: `docs\notes\downloads\`.
Each SHA-256 below was read from that archive's MANIFEST.csv and re-hashed live on D: on 2026-10-12, and all of them match.

## Story beat
The ship is down on a dry world at sunset, and there is cargo to move. Nobody sings.
- Chewy brings the crate down the ramp, and then hauls the lever that works the ship.
- Dolo walks off toward the business.
- In the hold, Chewy stacks and lashes the cargo, checks the case of credits, and fills the doorway when the job is done.
- Then his hand goes to the decks.

Each frame has one character action, and Chewy is the one working in every frame.

## Recommended first run: W-1 (the ramp)
W-1 has one character, one action and no face lock to fail on. W-2 (the lever) is the second clip. Run the rest only after Ziggy has reviewed the W-1 and W-2 videos.

## Common values (they apply to every frame unless the frame says otherwise)
- **Shot and story place:** "Chewy at work" storyboard, frame W-n, frame-story beat between the music. No song timestamp. Timing stays null until Nova's alignment passes.
- **Output bound:** one clip at the model's native short length. Flow002 returned 6.0 s, 144 frames at 24 fps, 1280x720, with an audio track despite a silent prompt. Use 8 s only if the selected model offers it. No automatic retries and no extra batches. Record the actual returned duration and whether audio is present.
- **Mode and model:** TO BE CONFIRMED ON SCREEN at run time, by the dispatcher.
  - Flow is the video route. Gemini's create tools are a separate route with their own bounds, and the two are not interchangeable.
  - Flow002 used Omni 1.1 Flash. That is recorded for reference only and is not assumed here.
  - If the mode isn't offered, stop.
- **Cost and access check:** check the displayed cost and the current allowance on screen BEFORE pressing Start. The run must stay within the current allowance, with no credits, no purchases, no plan or settings changes and no bypasses. Unknown cost or access means stop.
- **Provenance:**
  - Save the original output unchanged, and record its SHA-256 beside the source hash below.
  - Post a mailbox message to `nova` and `claude` with both hashes.
  - Save any later edit separately.
  - Arrival is not acceptance.
- **Owner:**
  - Prepared by Chief of Staff (grok_chief).
  - Dispatched by CFA Nova, or whoever Ziggy names for that provider surface.
  - Reviewed by Ziggy, on the actual video. Claude reviews this brief against the standard.
- **Forbidden in every frame:** speech, singing or lip motion, cuts, tattoo redesign, costume change, and characters added by the model. At most one gentle camera move; all frames below use a locked camera.
- **Chewy lock (copied from the standard):** Chewy per the DJB sheet: a dark gorilla-like beast, black over-ear headphones, gold neck chain, bullet bandolier.
- **Dolo lock (copied from the standard):** Dolo per `6c8900223ee9__lf_full.png`:
  - the four-gold external-off mouth
  - chain and band on the character-right wrist (provisional)
  - cursive "eye" character-right and serif "know" character-left
  - neck blaster character-left
  - upright chest ship
  - the brown leather jacket over the open off-white shirt
- **Acceptance checks:** each check is judged at the start, middle and end of the clip. There must be no morph, duplicate, added person or set change. The declared action must be completed, and nothing else. Note any audible content. The output is a candidate until Ziggy reviews it.

---

### W-1 Down the ramp (Claude's W-1) — FIRST RUN
1. **Shot and story place:** W-1 opens the beat with the cargo coming off the ship.

1. **Shot and story place:** W-2. With the cargo down, Chewy works the ship's lever.

3. **Locks visible:**

   - Chewy carrying a crate on the ramp behind.
4. **Declared change, one action:** Dolo walks two steps toward camera and out past the right edge of frame.
   - Start state: Dolo mid-frame.
   - End state: Dolo out of frame, screen-right.
   - Chewy takes one step down the ramp as background continuity. This is Claude's wording, and Claude should rule whether it counts as a second action.
   - The sun stays put.
5. **Sides:** Dolo exits screen-right. Chewy moves screen-left down the ramp. Camera locked.
6. **Output bound:** as Common.
7. **Mode and model:** to be confirmed on screen.
8. **Cost check:** as Common.
9. **Acceptance checks:**

**DEFECT (recorded):** Dolo wears an extra gold neck chain he doesn't have, and it hides the chest ship. Ziggy needs to decide, before this frame is run, between repairing the source first and running it as a motion test with the defect recorded.

### W-4 In the hold (Claude's W-3)
1. **Shot and story place:** W-4. The cargo goes into the hold.
2. **Source:** `GROK-HD-FALCON-1000/C67-cargo-hold-dolo-chewy/C67-cargo-hold-dolo-chewy-002.jpg`, 274,946 bytes.

   - Grok L5 S5. Claude L5/L5 S5.
   - Preliminary.
3. **Locks visible:**
   - Dolo chest-up: cheek words correct, two lip hoops, both ear pieces, neck blaster character-left.
   - Chewy among crates and netting, screen-left.
4. **Declared change, one action:** Chewy lifts the nearest crate and sets it on the stack behind him.

9. **Acceptance checks:**

### W-5 Strap it down (our pick)
1. **Shot and story place:** W-5. With the stack in place, Chewy secures it.
2. **Source:** `GROK-HD-FALCON-1000/C67-cargo-hold-dolo-chewy/C67-cargo-hold-dolo-chewy-011.jpg`, 279,047 bytes.

3. **Locks visible:**
   - Chewy, screen-left: the beast, black over-ear headphones on his head, gold neck chain, bullet bandolier.
   - Dolo, screen-right, chest-up: cursive "eye" character-right and serif "know" character-left, two lip hoops, ear hoop, neck blaster character-left, the brown leather jacket over the open off-white shirt.
   - Not visible: the chest ship and the wrist.
4. **Declared change, one action:** Chewy's hands pull the cargo strap across the crate top tight.
   - Start state: the strap lies slack on the crate.
   - End state: the strap is pulled taut and buckled.

5. **Sides:** Chewy and the strapped crate are screen-left. Dolo is screen-right. The netting lamps are in the background. Camera locked.
6. **Output bound:** as Common.
7. **Mode and model:** to be confirmed on screen.
8. **Cost check:** as Common.
9. **Acceptance checks:**

3. **Locks visible:** Chewy per the DJB sheet, in close. The open case holds four luminous credits, with crates behind.
4. **Declared change, one action:** his eyes drop from the lens to the credits, and the glow brightens one step.
   - Start state: eyes on the lens.
   - End state: eyes on the credits.
   - The lid doesn't move.
5. **Sides:** the case is screen-left-low, and his face is screen-right. Camera locked.
6. **Output bound:** as Common.
7. **Mode and model:** to be confirmed on screen.
8. **Cost check:** as Common.
9. **Acceptance checks:**
   - Four countable credits from start to end, and no readable text.
   - The beast's face holds.
   - Known defects: none.
10. **Provenance:** as Common. The output hash sits beside d6b65339…ef4.
11. **Owner:** Chief of Staff.

### W-7 Job done, in the doorway (our pick)
1. **Shot and story place:** W-7. The work is finished, and Chewy fills the lounge doorway.
2. **Source:** `GROK-HD-FALCON-1000/C21-chewy-holds-room/C21-chewy-holds-room-009.jpg`, 245,862 bytes.
   - SHA-256 `35bb4f5829bc9a7e0a2b94eb8eb1711af86874e57b143b287d60754486baf4f8`
   - Grok L5 S5. No Claude grade.
   - This frame was not flagged in the build audit (only C21-005 and C21-010 were).
   - Preliminary.
3. **Locks visible:** Chewy per the DJB sheet, frontal and full-torso: black over-ear headphones around the neck, gold curb chain, bullet bandolier, and both hands on the door frame. The corridor is warm-backlit.
4. **Declared change, one action:** Chewy lets go of the frame and steps one pace forward through the doorway.
   - Start state: hands on the door frame.
   - End state: stepping through, hands lowered to his sides.
   - The backlight stays constant.
5. **Sides:** the door frame is the screen edges, and the corridor runs straight back behind him. He moves toward camera. Camera locked.
6. **Output bound:** as Common.
7. **Mode and model:** to be confirmed on screen.
8. **Cost check:** as Common.
9. **Acceptance checks:**
   - Face, headphones, chain and bandolier hold.
   - Four fingers and a thumb on each hand as they release.
   - His build stays lean per DJB-02, with no bulking up (build-audit rule).
   - The doorway geometry stays constant.
   - Known defects: none recorded.
10. **Provenance:** as Common. The output hash sits beside 35bb4f58…f4f8.
11. **Owner:** Chief of Staff.

### W-8 The decks (Claude's W-5)
1. **Shot and story place:** W-8 closes the beat, with his hand going to the decks.
2. **Source:** `GROK-HD-FALCON-1000/C20-fader-push/C20-fader-push-001.jpg`, 279,611 bytes.
   - SHA-256 `8c55b4a2cfdc1275e14f532b881f59f57542a43c2ef3890d8490df57f917fade`
   - Grok L5 S5. Claude L5 S4, noting that the neon club lighting is not the Falcon's warm practicals.
   - Preliminary.
   - Alternate source: E13-chewy-hands-actions-004, SHA-256 `b7e2f2956d31c1f74d6eb28c22d5209f21ac94a9c822908fb494886a7e627367`, Claude L5 S4.
3. **Locks visible:** Chewy per the DJB sheet at a two-deck console, with headphones on, gold neck chain, bullet bandolier, and one hand on the mixer.
4. **Declared change, one action:** one fader push.
   - Start state: the fader at screen-left.
   - End state: the fader at screen-right.
   - The hand stays in contact with the fader the whole way, and the practicals pulse once as it lands.
5. **Sides:** the fader travels screen-right. Camera locked.
6. **Output bound:** as Common.
7. **Mode and model:** to be confirmed on screen.
8. **Cost check:** as Common.
9. **Acceptance checks:**
   - The hand stays on the fader, the finger count holds and no second hand appears.
   - The decks' geometry stays constant.
   - Known defects: the lighting is magenta and cyan neon rather than the Falcon's warm practicals.
10. **Provenance:** as Common. The output hash sits beside 8c55b4a2…fade.
11. **Owner:** Chief of Staff.

## Cut logic
1. W-1 → W-2: the crate reaches the ground; cut to the hand on the lever.
2. W-2 → W-3: the lever comes down; cut to Dolo walking away.
3. W-3 → W-4: Dolo leaves frame; cut to the hold.
4. W-4 → W-5: the crate lands on the stack; cut to the strap.
5. W-5 → W-6: the buckle closes; cut to the case.
6. W-6 → W-7: his eyes drop; cut to him in the doorway.
7. W-7 → W-8: he steps through; cut to the hand on the fader.

That is eight shots, each with a single action. There is no dialogue and no song.

## Required before any run
- CFA Nova confirms the mode and model on screen, verifies the cost and allowance, and dispatches. Unknown cost or access means stop.
- Ziggy rules on the W-3 neck-chain defect.
- Claude grades the sources that have no grade yet: W-2, W-5 and W-7.
- Each output is saved unchanged with its hash, and posted to the mailbox for `nova` and `claude`. It stays a candidate until Ziggy reviews it.

— Chief of Staff (grok_chief)

# Claude's bounded review of the cinematography R&D proposal and A/B pilot package — for discussion with Ziggy

Reviewer: Claude, lead writer. Date: 2026-10-12. Read in full: `collaborators/cinematography_rd_20261012/PROPOSAL.txt` (SHA-256 4fd9d1bd…, 8,762 bytes) and `PILOT_PACKAGE.txt` (f768ce4c…, 16,857 bytes), both hashes verified on D:, plus Nova's `NOVA_REVIEW_NOTES.json`. Status: review only. Nothing here assigns a candidate, ranks one, launches a comparison, renders, uploads or spends. Proposed status is preserved.

## 1. What the package gets right

- **Compare writing before rendering.** One frozen package, verbatim first responses with author, model, date and the exact inputs each candidate actually received; then one recommendation from Nova and me for Ziggy. This is the right order and the only fair one, since the candidates do not share access.
- **Two passes kept apart.** Pass A preserves A's camera movement and action and changes only the motivated practical lighting; Pass B is a separately declared camera treatment that may need regeneration and cannot be smuggled into Pass A. The proposed C prompt v2 is the single adapter for Pass A. I agree with Nova's caveat: the word "fixed-camera" in the proposal must be read as "preserve the source's existing camera movement," which the pilot package and the actual prompt already say.
- **Lineage and limits are honest.** A is a prepared excerpt of GEM-5A115C59, not a generation; B's job id, seed and cost are unknown; the 720p and nominal-rate caveats are stated; the three Civitai examples are archived stills, not verified motion; a path is not proof of viewing.
- **The method's rules are carried.** New scenes begin Preliminary; an accepted reference does not accept a new scene; dimensions stay separate; Ziggy judges motion, acting and the edit.

## 2. What the package says is missing, and what the writer lane can supply now (proposals)

The package itself states that the dramatic beat, the subject emphasis, the arrival and entry choreography and the storyboard scene-card id for the car scene have not been established, and asks candidates to name the minimum missing information. Those are writer questions. My proposals, for Ziggy to accept or change, so every candidate designs camera against the same beat:

- **Beat.** The car arrival is the prologue's junction between the drop and the cantina walk: Dolo arrives at the cantina landing at night to do business, the man who charges for everything stepping out to collect. In the cards it sits between P-6 (the drop) and P-7 (the cantina walk) as a proposed new shot, P-6b "the arrival." It is not inside the song.
- **Subject emphasis.** The man first, the door second. The car is the delivery, not the subject. Blue night with warm practicals at the door is the mood the cards already give that world (the neon city, wet landings, the cab's lamps).
- **Choreography.** The car settles, the door opens, he steps out, turns toward the door, walks out of frame toward it. That is what A already contains, so Pass A preserves it as is.
- **Sides, so Pass B is comparable across candidates.** The prologue's geography: the landing at screen-right, the vehicle settled at screen-left having arrived from screen-left, departures into depth, the cantina door at the far wall. A camera proposal that contradicts these needs to say why.
- **Identity caveat for Pass B.** A's performer is not lf_full and the silver jacket is not the locked brown-leather-over-off-white outfit; the pilot is a lighting diagnostic on a non-canon scene, which is fine for Pass A. For Pass B, a camera treatment designed only on A may not transfer; the stronger baseline for a regenerated camera test is a graded Grok frame of the same beat from the archives (the street landing N32, the cab landing N29, or the neon city E35, all preliminary) with the locked outfit, so the camera lesson lands on the shot it will actually serve. That choice is Ziggy's, and it changes no part of Pass A.

## 3. Additions I would make to the one-page expert return

- Ask each candidate to **name the beat they are serving and its screen sides** in one line, so camera designs can be compared on the same intention rather than on taste.
- Ask for **light stated as sources**: which emitters exist in A, what each lights, and what the proposed warm contribution does to falloff, occlusion, shadows and reflections; a response that proposes a look without naming a source is the yellow-wash failure in words.
- Ask each candidate to **declare their access level** at the top (text only, stills, video playback) as Nova notes; responses are then grouped by access before any ranking.
- Keep the **three examples bounded** as written; the cab-exit woman is the informant's inspiration, which ties it to the prologue's cab and makes it the most relevant of the three to this beat.

## 4. On the candidate pool

I hold no evidence to rank Gemini Master, Kimi, Qwen, DeepSeek or Nova on cinematography; the proposal is right that a stated preference and a coordination role are not earned grades, and that an operator role does not make Nova the lead by default. Two things will matter in the comparison more than fluency: whether a response separates observed cues in A from assumptions, and how much operator and repair burden its prompt would create for CFA. A small team is only worth it if the division of work is named (for example one candidate on lighting physics, one on camera and coverage) and it does not add coordination turns.

## 5. What I will do, and not do

I will read every candidate's first response against this review and the package and write, with Nova, one short recommendation for Ziggy. I will not assign, rank ahead of the responses, render, upload, or spend. Nothing in this review changes the Flow 002 dispositions (A and B: Scene, Preliminary, Needs fixes, no stars) or the proposed C prompt v2.

— Claude

assets.title: Video prototype brief · Planning standard
assets.text:
# Video prototype brief — the standard every Flow / Gemini request must meet

Author: Claude, lead writer. Date: 2026-10-12. Status: working standard for the writer lane; it applies the CFA production method of October 12 (`collaborators/PRODUCTION_METHOD_20261012.txt`), the Flow project brief (`hon_dolo_strictly_business/flow/project_brief.txt`), the Flow002 milestone recorded in the method, and the shoot-plan verification fields. It authorizes nothing. A brief that meets this standard is ready for CFA Nova to dispatch when Ziggy wants it run; Ziggy's gate is the actual video.

**Refinement of 2026-10-12 (the method's dated user refinement and the Flow 002 A/B review, mailbox 98220a40):** this standard is a completeness checklist for a brief, not an approval gate. New scenes enter Preliminary without per-image signoff; a production-ready character, outfit or tattoo foundation never approves the new scene made from it; the new scene's likeness and scene/action are assessed separately before anyone claims readiness. Review dimensions stay independent and are never averaged: **Complete look** (the character overall, independent of scene), **Scene** (context and action, independent of character fidelity), **Details only** (one isolated feature), and **Outfit** (character fidelity as seen in the outfit, separate from whether the clothing is desirable). Lighting changes must be physically motivated (existing emitters, local falloff, occlusion, shadows and reflections that follow moving surfaces), never a global wash. Body-to-object interaction (entering a vehicle, descending, contact) is a known weak point of the current route, so a brief asks for one simple action. Flow's Omni Flash 1.1 video editing runs at standard 720p (draft 360p); Veo 3.1 Quality does not edit video; the account's export choices are unverified; record the returned duration and frame rate rather than assuming them.

## Why a standard

The swarm has produced over 2,500 preliminary stills. Ziggy wants the best of them flowed into prototype videos with Gemini and Flow, and he has asked the Grok team to draft the instructions and me to review them to my standard. The method says each executable task needs exact inputs, a declared change, preservation goals, an output bound and an actual supported mode and model, with the displayed cost verified before a run and unknown cost or access as a stop condition. This file turns that into a form the team can fill and I can check in one pass.

## The form (one brief per shot; one shot per run)

1. **Shot id and story place.** The card's shot (for example S04-7 Chewie's fader, or the "Chewy at work" storyboard's shot 2) and the section it serves. No song timestamp; timing stays null until Nova's alignment passes.
2. **Source image, exact.** Archive, category, filename, SHA-256 from the archive MANIFEST, the Grok preliminary scores (L and S), my grade if one exists in `CLAUDE_GRADES_20261012.md`, and Ziggy's review state if any. State plainly: preliminary draft, not an accepted reference. One source image per run; a second image only as an end-frame review target, never as an invented conditioning input.
3. **Identity locks to preserve** (copied, not paraphrased): Dolo per `6c8900223ee9__lf_full.png`, the four-gold external-off mouth, chain and band on the character-right wrist (provisional), cursive "eye" character-right, serif "know" character-left, neck blaster character-left, upright chest ship, the brown leather jacket over the open off-white shirt; Chewy per the DJB sheet (dark gorilla-like beast, black over-ear headphones, gold neck chain, bullet bandolier); Leia per the likeness crop with the ivory coat and no deciding jewelry; the enforcer per DA-02 and DA-04, described as the original sci-fi armored enforcer. Name which of these are actually visible in the source frame; only those can be checked.
4. **Declared change, one action.** What moves, in one sentence, with the start state and the end state (for example: Chewy's hand pushes the fader from left to right; nothing else moves). No speech, singing, lip motion, cuts, tattoo redesign, costume change or added characters. One gentle camera move at most. Avoid actions that depend on body-to-object contact physics (climbing in, sitting down, descending stairs) in a first test; a lift, a push, a turn of the head or a walk on flat ground is safer.
4a. **Lighting, stated as sources.** Name the existing emitters in the frame (sunset key, console practicals, a lamp) and what they light; any requested change warms or cools those emitters and the surfaces they reach, with falloff, occlusion, shadows and reflections, and leaves unlit areas alone. Never "make it warmer" as a whole-frame filter.
5. **Sides and geography.** The card's screen directions for this frame (co-pilot screen-left of Dolo in frontal shots; display screen-right; hatch screen-right; cantina counter along the right-hand wall from the entrance; battle light ahead after the turn), so motion does not mirror the set.
6. **Output bound.** One clip; the model's native short length (Flow002 returned 6.0 s, 144 frames at 24 fps, 1280x720, with an audio track despite a silent prompt); eight seconds only if the selected model offers it; no automatic retries; no extra batches. Record the actual returned duration and whether audio is present.
7. **Mode and model, actually supported.** Name the provider and the exact mode and model offered on screen at run time (Flow002 used Omni 1.1 Flash). If the mode is not offered, stop. "Flow" and "Gemini" are not interchangeable: Flow is the video route; Gemini's image or video create tools are a separate route with their own bounds.
8. **Cost and access check.** The displayed cost and the current allowance verified on screen before Start; unknown cost or access is a stop condition. No purchases, plan changes, settings changes or bypasses.
9. **Review checks, stated before the run (not a gate).** Identity, lettering, teeth (where visible), wrist side and wardrobe at start, middle and end; no morph, duplicate, added person or set change; the declared action completed and nothing else; light behaving as sources, not as a wash; audible content noted; returned duration and frame rate recorded. Each output enters Preliminary with separate Complete look, Scene, Details and Outfit notes; grades are attributed and provisional; Ziggy's own scores and his motion, acting and edit judgment are final. A pleasing preview is not preservation evidence.
10. **Provenance.** Save the original output unchanged with its SHA-256 beside the source image's hash; a mailbox message to `nova` and `claude` with both hashes; any later edit saved separately. Arrival is not acceptance.
11. **Owner.** Who prepares (the swarm or me), who dispatches (CFA Nova, or whoever Ziggy names per provider surface), who reviews (Ziggy, the actual video).

## What the Flow 002 test taught (A and B, both Scene / Preliminary / Needs fixes)

Ziggy's attributed review of the first Flow edit: the outfit was perfect and the blue night aesthetic beautiful; the performer was not a sufficient likeness; tattoos were hard to see; the car entry and body interaction were physically unreal; the warmth edit read as a yellow surface wash rather than motivated light. The lesson for every brief here: start from a source frame whose likeness already holds (the swarm's shortlist, graded), ask for one simple action, state the light as sources, and keep an inherited source defect separate from what the edit changed. A single lighting diagnostic (proposed C prompt v2) is on file in `flow/video_test_002/USER_REVIEW_20261012.txt`; it is a proposal, not a run.

## What I check when a brief comes in from the team

- Every field above present; no "see image" where a hash belongs.
- The source frame is one the shortlist or Ziggy named, and its identity defects (from the category NOTES and my grades) are listed, not hidden by its score.
- The action is one action and matches the card; the sides are the card's.
- Nothing asks for lip motion, song timing, a second character, or a boss or Vader video before Ziggy clears the IP question he raised ("take special care with the bosses").
- The bound and the stop conditions are written down.

## Order of candidates (my proposal, for Ziggy to confirm)

Start with single-character or no-face frames where identity risk is lowest and the action is one gesture: Chewy at the decks (C19/C20), Chewy's fader (S04-7), the throttle insert (C07), the harness buckle (C10), the hover (C01 / S07-3), exteriors (C35 hangar exit, C37 bank, C38 turn). Then two-shots (C67 cargo hold, C15). Leia frames after her costume decision. The boss and the enforcer last, after Ziggy's IP call.

— Claude
