# Scene card — "The silence breaks" (the sandworm beat)

Project: Lisan Al Gaib / Meta Mirror. Section: Bridge into Verse 1, between panel LAG-SC-09 (cue, reported: "to the silence break") and panel LAG-SC-10 (cue, reported: "buried deep"). Author: Claude, lead writer, October 12, 2026. Status: **proposed**; Ungraded; Unreviewed; timing null; no run authorized. The beat is desert footage inserted between two source panels; the panels keep their numbers, cues and placeholder holds. Source frames are preliminary LAG-1K drafts. Any run follows `PROTOTYPE_BRIEF_C13-04.md` and the production method; dispatch is CFA Nova's; Ziggy's gate is the actual video.

## Story beat

The salt flat is silent (panel 09). He walks out onto the open sand with a thumper, drives it in, and lets it beat. The ground answers: tracks come toward him from the horizon, the sand lifts, and the maw rises out of the haze behind him. He does not run and he does not turn; he holds, one breath, eyes on us. Then the sand takes the frame, and he comes up out of it (panel 10). What the burst means, that the worm passed over and he surfaced, is the writer's reading, not a decision.

It is the right first clip for the same reason the ramp carry was on the Hon Dolo side: one character, one action, no mouth motion, no second figure, and the identity marks are chest-up in the hero frame. It is also the beat that makes the A-line (the desert) real: after it, every cut back to the desert carries the worm's possibility.

Why here: the Jet Black record asks for "an existing Lisan action that can serve as the first mission step." Planting the thumper is one (see the pass, section 3). That association is proposed, not placed.

## Shots, in order

Archive root: `docs\notes\explorable_world\comfy\references\From Grok\`. Grok scores are the team's preliminary self-scores from the category NOTES; mine are attributed and provisional, made at the tool's reduced scale (`DECISIONS_20261012.md`, section 4). Likeness is against `LAG-LOCK-FACE-NATURAL.jpg`; outfit against `LAG-LOOK-V3-01.jpg`. Each shot's Source line lists the kinds it could plausibly take; it is a make-or-have note and never alters the shot.

### SW-1 The thumper
- Panel served: between 09 and 10; cue (reported) "to the silence break".
- Frame: `GROK-LAG-1K-C15\GROK-LAG-1K-C15\C15-20_Z_5.jpg`, SHA-256 `7e782cdafb9e1d60915087b0b48a517cebd1608832bf17ab9af80f2cfc84e857`, 314,666 bytes; Grok L5 S5 ("planting second thumper, converging worm tracks"); Claude L3 S5. Alternate: `C15-16_Z_5.jpg`, SHA-256 `07567fe39e1b7df7e1afe3d6fec1eb6db168f0b0665b9292abb1c37da698917c`, 271,032 bytes; Grok L5 S5 ("three thumpers below rock outcrop, sweeping track"); Claude L3 S5. Other team picks, not viewed by me: C15-07, 09, 14, 17, 18, 21, 22 (all `_Z_5`, L5 S5 per NOTES).
- What I saw (C15-20): frontal chest-up, tan hooded robe, the thumper cylinder in his hand being planted, worm tracks converging behind him on both sides, a far thumper at screen-left; AL between the brows; vertical GAIB readable; the worms segmented and open-jawed with the eye in the disc (good); eyes pale grey, not electric blue; the face reads older than the reference; no piercings. (C15-16: frontal, coarse tan robe and scarf, three thumpers on the dune at screen-left, a sweeping track at screen-right; worms and eye-disc good; eyes read brown; no piercings.)
- Action, one: he drives the thumper down into the sand and lets go; the tracks behind him do not move. No look to the horizon yet.
- Sides: the tracks run from the horizon to him; the thumper is low center; the worm, when it comes (SW-2), comes from screen-left, so the clearest track should read from screen-left.
- Camera: locked, or one slow push to his hands.
- Light as sources: a high hazy sun, flat and white; no emitters; no change requested.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated from this draft; a repaired draft (eye color, face age); a new C15 frame on request.
- Defects known: eye color; face age; both inherit into any clip. Not a first-clip candidate for that reason.

### SW-2 The rise (the first clip)
- Panel served: between 09 and 10.
- Frame: `GROK-LAG-1K-C13\C13-sandworm-rising\C13-04_Z_1.jpg`, SHA-256 `7eafd9ac048dc6d6125dc38281c1b664f7ae0cac1159909c34d90a5e3eef93a3`, 268,027 bytes; Grok NOTES "strong pass, shortlist" (no L/S numbers for this slot); **Ziggy's storyboard_prime flag** via HaL (mailbox 03e908bf, 2026-10-12 13:22 UTC); Claude L4 S5.
- What I saw: chest-up, screen-right of center, facing the lens, mouth closed; messy dark curls, electric-blue eyes, stubble; AL between the brows; vertical GAIB on the chin; two throat worms facing each other with a rayed disc between; black hooded cloak over a tan stillsuit-like shirt; gold chain. The maw rises at screen-left out of warm haze, the sun upper-left behind it. Not holding: the disc has no visible eye (a plain sun); the worms read as fanged snakes rather than segmented worms; no nostril hoop, brow ring or ear hoop (the ear is under the hair). No breather, correctly. Arm not in frame.
- Action, one: the maw rises about one maw-height higher behind him, sand pouring off its lip; he holds, one slow breath, eyes on the lens, no head turn. The cloak hem may stir. Nothing else.
- Sides: worm screen-left; him screen-right of center; sun upper-left; the maw rises straight up.
- Camera: locked for the first clip. A slow push is a second clip, never the first.
- Light as sources: the sun upper-left behind the haze is the only emitter; it rims the curls and the maw's edge; the haze is the diffuser that lights his face; the maw's interior stays dark; its shadow does not reach him. No warming, no wash.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated from this draft as it is (recommended for the first clip); generated from a HaL repair variant for the production clip; a new C13 frame.
- Defects known: the disc's eye, the snake-like worms and the absent piercings are inherited from the source and must be recorded separately from anything the motion changes; the model must not be asked to "fix" them in the clip, and if piercings or ink appear during the clip, that is a change to note.

### SW-3 He does not turn (alternate angle)
- Frame: `GROK-LAG-1K-C13\C13-sandworm-rising\C13-08_Z_11.jpg`, SHA-256 `23cc368bd886f68807c91c58ec5b86c030cddef8755d61f3b9f557b353da0b1b`, 273,038 bytes; Grok L5 S5 ("worm breaching at sunset, crisp worms + disc"); Claude L4 S5.
- What I saw: three-quarter, looking up and away to screen-left; the worm breaches at screen-right against the low sun at far right, dust trailing; AL between the brows; GAIB vertical, readable; the worms segmented and open-jawed with the eye clearly in the disc (the best of the three); black cloak; layered gold chains and a tan strap across the chest (not the single Cuban chain of LOOK-V3); no piercings.
- Action, one: the dust column behind the worm drifts and settles; his eyes close and open once; nothing else.
- Sides: worm screen-right, sun screen-right, his look screen-left. **This flips the worm's side against SW-2.** The card uses it only as a new angle after SW-2, which a cut can carry if he is turning his head on the cut; it does not resolve the flip.
- Camera: locked.
- Light as sources: the setting sun at frame right is the key and the rim; the sky's amber is the fill; his face is in its own shadow side toward the lens; no change.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated from this draft; a repair (the single chain) for Outfit continuity; a mirrored *request* to HaL if the worm must stay screen-left (never a mirrored file: it mirrors the tattoos and the lettering).
- Defects known: the chains and strap (Outfit); no piercings.

### SW-4 The shadow in the wall (alternate, preferred over SW-3)
- Frame: `GROK-LAG-1K-C13\C13-sandworm-rising\C13-20_Z_11.jpg`, SHA-256 `dab0b1da60d6c23b1e19935f509ce2f1f6de9d79f6a40d9844c480785c006470`, 310,731 bytes; Grok L5 S5 ("worm shadow in sandstorm wall, amber"); Claude L4 S5.
- What I saw: low angle, looking up-right into an amber storm wall where the worm's body curves at screen-right; AL between the brows; GAIB vertical, readable; worms segmented with the disc's eye small; gold chain; a dark hooded jacket over a dark ribbed shirt rather than the tan stillsuit (Outfit drift); no piercings.
- Action, one: the worm's curve in the storm wall slides one body-width toward screen-left as grit crosses the lens; he holds, eyes on it.
- Sides: worm screen-right (the same flip as SW-3); his look screen-right, toward it. Preferred over SW-3 because he now faces the thing, which reads as a new angle after SW-2's "does not turn".
- Camera: locked.
- Light as sources: the storm wall itself is the light, a diffuse amber from upper-right; no emitters; no change.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated from this draft; a repair for the wardrobe (tan stillsuit, cloak) if continuity with SW-2 matters more than the frame; a new C13 or C09 frame.
- Defects known: wardrobe (Outfit); the disc's eye small; no piercings.

### SW-5 Buried deep (the source panel)
- Panel: `02_Storyboard_Scenes/LAG-SC-10.jpg`, SHA-256 `82dfca3f6472b18dd7ca3919c02e7ca84dc229295eb3a1853b0a980c61f35833`; CSV outfit "rising from dunes, stillsuit, sand bursting"; motion suggestion "low angle, sand bursting up, slow-mo"; Grok QA "stray face marks"; nova review: "contact-sheet overview; detailed approval pending"; Claude L3 S5 (stray marks near the eyes; an ear hoop on the viewer-left ear, his right, the bare side, by my read at the tool's scale).
- Action: the panel's own suggestion, kept as the panel's: he comes up through the sand in slow motion. Body-to-sand interaction is a known weak point of the current route (the method's note on body-to-object physics), so this is not a first-clip candidate; it is the landing frame the beat cuts to.
- Sides: he rises center frame, looking up and to screen-right.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: the panel as the end frame of the beat; a repaired panel (marks, hoop side) before any clip; generated from a C23 buried-city or C10 draft.
- Defects known: as reported, plus the hoop side to check at full size.

## Cut logic

SW-1 → SW-2 on the thumper's first beat: the sand ridge at the horizon in SW-1's last frame becomes the rise. SW-2 → SW-4 (or SW-3, not both): a new angle as he turns his head toward it. SW-4 → SW-5 on the storm wall swallowing the frame: the sand burst of panel 10. Four shots if one alternate is used, five if the thumper gets its own frame; no dialogue; the song under all of it once the song exists. If only one clip is run first, run SW-2.

## Geography for the whole beat

The worm rises screen-left of him in the hero frame (SW-2) and he faces the lens. The team's other strong C13 drafts put the worm screen-right; the card treats those as a new angle after a cut rather than pretending they match. If Ziggy wants the worm on one side throughout, SW-3 and SW-4 become a request to HaL for the same compositions with the worm screen-left, generated fresh with the tattoos and the lettering on their correct sides.

## Required before any run (per the standard and the method)

- CFA Nova names the mode and model actually offered on screen for each route (Flow; Gemini), verifies the displayed cost and the allowance, and dispatches; unknown cost or access is a stop. One clip per route; no retries.
- The output is saved unchanged with its hash beside the source hash; mailbox to `nova`, `claude` and `hal`; candidate until Ziggy reviews the actual video.
- No lip motion, no song timing, no second figure, no breather added, no grill, no added piercings or ink.
- The LAG-1K set is not in the catalog yet; the storyboard_prime tag HaL asked for is CFA Nova's after the entry exists.

## Requests to HaL's team (proposals; none sent by this card)

1. A repair variant of C13-04: same composition, same head standard, Dune-style segmented worms with the eye in the disc, flat black ink, piercings on his left per the face lock, single Cuban chain. For the production clip, not the first test.
2. The two alternates with the worm screen-left (SW-3 and SW-4 compositions), if Ziggy keeps one side.
3. One C15 thumper frame with the reference's eye color and age, chest-up, the thumper in hand, tracks from screen-left.

## Scene grade and review

Grade: Ungraded. Shoot-plan review: Unreviewed. Timing: null. Source frames preliminary. Likeness and scene are assessed separately for every output; nothing here approves a scene from its foundation.

— Claude

# Scene card — "Two doors and the signal" (panels 48, 49, 50: the ending)

Project: Lisan Al Gaib / Meta Mirror. Section: the end of Verse 3 into the Finale (panels LAG-SC-48, LAG-SC-49, LAG-SC-50; cues, reported: "outer world, inner world, two doors", "Lisan on the mic, ain't speakin' from a throne", "signal in the noise"). Author: Claude, lead writer, October 12, 2026 (evening, America/New_York). Status: **proposed**; Ungraded; Unreviewed; timing null; no run authorized. Written second, after the sandworm card, because the ending is the anchor: everything before it has to aim here (Ziggy's rule for Hon Dolo, applied). The source panels keep their numbers, cues and placeholder holds; the desert frames are preliminary LAG-1K drafts; the two new beats are the writer's proposals.

## Story beat

Verse 3 has gone all the way inward: the library, the masks, the spiral, the shadow, the voodoo, the chaos cards. Then the desert again, and two doors standing in the open sand with nothing behind them: through one, the sun; through the other, the stars. He stands between them. The song has been two worlds the whole way, the desert where his body is and the mirror where he is everyone, and this is the frame where the film says so out loud. He goes toward the sun. Street level, a car hood, a crowd, the mic to the lens: not a throne, a hood. And then the blade up and the mandala blazing over the desert, the mirror's sun in the desert's sky, and inside the mandala an eye, the same eye that has been on his throat since the first frame. The signal was never out there. He was carrying it.

## What I saw in the three panels (at the tool's reduced scale; full-size checks are CFA's)

| Panel | Seen | Holds | Does not hold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LAG-SC-48 (SHA-256 `748f2a9fd5de7813b4d777e5f6e5138c1e5305cc5f25653b671d76507bd5baa0`) | Frontal between two open doors: the sun door at screen-left, the cosmos door at screen-right; coarse tan robe and scarf; breather tube under the nostrils across his right cheek (viewer-left); AL between the brows; worms and eye-disc on the throat. | Breather side per the v3 rule; nostril hoop on his left; worms and disc; AL. | Brow ring and ear hoop on his right (viewer-left), the bare side; chin letters garbled and a stray letter on the neck below the disc (the reported "stray letters on neck"); not the signature cloak. Claude L3 S5. |
| LAG-SC-49 (`2a171ea6c24b2047ef7c4455b44613e4c52dc963d1a7fbd86c73b52cb7dfda57`) | Dusk street, crowd behind, leaning on a car hood, mic in hand toward the lens, mouth open mid-line; black hooded jacket over a tan vest, gold Cuban chain; breather across his right cheek; AL; worms and eye-disc. | Breather side; nostril hoop on his left; the signature elements (hood, tan, chain); natural teeth. | Brow ring and ear hoop on his right; ink on the hand and wrist holding the mic (the reported "wrist ink"); chin lettering hidden by the mic. Claude L3 S4. |

One finding for CFA from the three together: **the same flipped pattern in all three** (brow ring and ear hoop on his right, nostril hoop on his left, breather correctly on the right). The guide's known-drift list has "brow ring flipping sides" and "hoops in both ears"; the per-panel QA for 48, 49 and 50 does not record it. One repair brief covers all three.

## Shots, in order

Archive root for desert frames: `docs\notes\explorable_world\comfy\references\From Grok\`. Grok scores are the categories' NOTES self-scores; mine are attributed and provisional (`DECISIONS_20261012.md`, section 4). Each Source line is a make-or-have note and never alters the shot.

### TD-1 The doors
- Panel: LAG-SC-48; the CSV's own motion suggestion "slow dolly between the doors".
- Desert lead-in (proposal): a sun-disc ruin frame before the doors, the eye in stone, so the doors arrive in a place: `GROK-LAG-1K-C35\GROK-LAG-1K-C35\C35-15_Z_5.jpg`, SHA-256 `b04370942e067ff15426f55d304653f6d828cf2cd1bcba98d1ae882c4273bc00`, 335,492 bytes; Grok L5 S5 ("eye sun-disc statue in dust"); Claude L3 S5 (frontal before a giant carved stone sun with two carved eyes flanking his head; AL; vertical GAIB; segmented worms and a rayed eye-disc, the best throat art I have seen in the archive; coarse brown robe; **eyes read brown, not electric blue**; no piercings). Other team picks, not viewed: C35-05, 13, 18 (`_Z_5`, L5 S5), C35-04 (breather, L5 S5).
- Action, one: the camera dollies forward between the doors, the panel's own move; he holds, eyes to the lens; the two doorways do not change.
- Sides: sun door screen-left (the outer world, the A-line), cosmos door screen-right (the inner world, the B-line). This assignment is the writer's, from the panel as drawn.
- Light as sources: the low sun through the left door is the key and the rim; the starfield through the right door gives nothing; the sky's gold is the fill. No change.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: the panel after a repair (ring and hoop sides, chin lettering); generated from the repaired panel; a new C35 frame.

### TD-2 The choice (new beat, proposed)
- No panel. The writer's proposal: he turns and walks toward the sun door; behind him the cosmos door swings shut in the wind. It says which world he chooses: the desert, the people, the outer world. Ziggy may prefer he chooses neither and the camera goes through alone; the card is written for the walk and can switch.
- Action, one: the walk, four steps, toward screen-left; the right-hand door closes.
- Sides: he exits toward screen-left (the sun door); the closing door at screen-right.
- Light as sources: as TD-1; as he nears the sun door its light wraps his cloak's edge.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: generated from the repaired panel 48 as an end-frame review target; a new frame from HaL with the doors kept and him turned.

### TD-3 Street level
- Panel: LAG-SC-49; the CSV's own motion "handheld, crowd behind, mic to lens".
- This is the one panel in the ending where he sings. Mouth motion is lip-sync territory: it waits for the song, Nova's intake and a timed lyric map with lead, double and ad-lib lanes, exactly as Hon Dolo's inserts do; the seven Production mouth images (VIS-LAG-20 to 24, detail-only) are the phoneme references for that later work, not for this card. No lip-sync is proposed or accepted here.
- Desert twin (proposal, for the two-worlds reading): the only crowd in the desert archive is the scrap bazaar or the tribe gathering (C17, C31). Not required; the panel's street is the mirror world's street and can stay as it is.
- Action, one (for a non-singing test only): the handheld drift and the mic coming to the lens; mouth closed. The singing version is a different clip, after the song.
- Sides: the car hood screen-right, the crowd deep behind, the mic toward the lens.
- Light as sources: the dusk sky as the fill; the street's practicals (shop fronts, a headlight at screen-left) as the warm key from behind; no change.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: the panel after a repair (ring and hoop sides, wrist ink); generated from it; supplied footage of a real street with the performance generated (the Hon Dolo "source is TBD" rule).

### TD-4 The signal
- Panel: LAG-SC-50; the CSV's own motion "low-angle hero push, mandala blazes, hold".
- Desert twin (proposal): the dead radio tower, the signal's literal source in the A-line: `GROK-LAG-1K-C36\GROK-LAG-1K-C36\C36-02_Z_3.jpg`, SHA-256 `26b28bf36d18a51e078c823f9c8f7028f4b741ec4eb9790b32ea95a3e790d3f9`, 315,901 bytes; Grok "PASS: full vertical G-A-I-B, worm+eye disc, AL"; Claude L4 S5 (three-quarter at a rusted tower with a hand on a rung, dead towers across grey wastes; AL; vertical GAIB; the throat art with the eye; blue eyes; **dark hooded jacket with straps instead of the tan suit and cloak**, an Outfit drift; gold chain; no piercings). Other team picks, not viewed: C36-04 (red beacon tower at dusk), C36-05 (relay shack consoles), C36-07 (handheld radio) (`_Z_5`, L5 S5).
- Action, one: the panel's own push; the mandala brightens one step; he holds; the cloak moves. The blade is the problem: it floats with no hand, so before any clip the panel needs a repair (a hand on the blade, or the blade gone and the hands empty). The card prefers the hands empty: the signal is not a weapon.
- Sides: he is center, looking up-right; the mandala behind and above; the ruins low at screen-right.
- Light as sources: the mandala is the only emitter, a warm gold from above and behind; it rims the curls and the cloak's edge; the face takes the sky's cool fill; no wash.
- Source: TBD. Plausible: the repaired panel, generated; a new C36 frame in the signature wardrobe; a composite of the C36 tower and the mandala (a request, not a flip).

### TD-5 The eye (new beat, proposed; last frame)
- No panel. The writer's proposal for the last frame: from the mandala's eye in the sky, cut to the eye in the sun-disc on his throat, the same drawing, in macro, flat black ink on skin, his pulse under it; hold; out.
- It needs one new frame: a throat macro from the face lock, worms and disc exactly as `LAG-LOCK-FACE-NATURAL.jpg` draws them, no lettering in frame. The archive has no macro of the throat art; the mouth set is the mouth. A request to HaL's team, not a flip or a crop of the face lock (a crop would be too soft at this size).
- Alternative last frame: the panel 50 hold, as the CSV ends. Ziggy's call, as the mirror was on the Hon Dolo side.

## Cut logic

47 (chaos cards, the last mirror-world panel) → TD-1 on the cards going dark to the doors in the sun; TD-1 → TD-2 on his first step; TD-2 → TD-3 on the door closing to the mic arriving at the lens; TD-3 → TD-4 on the last line of 49 to the blade (or the empty hands) rising; TD-4 → TD-5 on the mandala's eye to the throat's eye. Five beats, three panels, two new frames. The Track B story's tower ending ("The Gloved Hand", scene 9) rhymes with TD-4 on purpose: the signal in the noise is the same image in both tracks.

## Required before any run

- Repairs first: the ring and hoop sides in 48, 49 and 50 (one brief); the chin lettering and stray neck letter in 48; the wrist ink in 49; the floating blade in 50. Repairs keep the head standard.
- The song, the intake and the lane map before any singing clip of 49.
- CFA Nova's mode and cost check for any clip; one clip per brief; no retries; Ziggy's gate is the video.
- The new frames (TD-2's turn, TD-5's macro) are requests, not promises.

## Requests to HaL's team (proposals; none sent by this card)

1. One repair pass over LAG-SC-48, 49 and 50: brow ring and ear hoop moved to his left (viewer-right in frontal views), nostril hoop kept, breather kept on his right; 48's chin lettering and neck letter corrected; 49's hand and wrist ink removed; 50's blade given a hand or removed. Same compositions, same head standard.
2. A throat macro of the worms and the eye-disc from the face lock, flat black ink, no lettering, for TD-5.
3. The C36 tower frames (02, 04, 05) re-made in the signature wardrobe (tan suit, black cloak, Cuban chain), same compositions, for the A-line's signal.

## Scene grade and review

Grade: Ungraded. Shoot-plan review: Unreviewed. Timing: null. Source panels and drafts preliminary. Likeness and scene assessed separately for every output; nothing here approves a scene from its foundation.

— Claude

# Meta Mirror — the two lyric sets, diffed (2026-10-13)

Author: Claude, lead writer. Sources: `lisan_al_gaib/lyrics_user_20261013/META_MIRROR_0_REMASTERED.lyrics.user.v001.txt` (set 1, SHA-256 `57ca7406…f6ed`, 134 lines counting blanks) and `MM_0.lyrics.user.v001.txt` (set 2, `cab4d38d…0caa`, 148 lines), both user text, provisional, as Ziggy pasted them; the set order is inferred from the paste and is his to confirm. Method: two independent read-only diff readers, two independent cue mappers and one structure reader over the files, then a reconciler that re-read the files and confirmed every item; no difference was listed by only one reader. Line numbers are file lines counting blank lines. Nothing here is timing.

## Section order of each set

**Set 1 (Meta_Mirror_0 Remastered):** [Chorus] L1 (body 2–16) · [BRIDGE] 1 L18 (19–22) · [Verse 1] L24 (25–31) · [BRIDGE] 2 L33 (34–39) · [ VERSE 2] L41 (42–54; the leading space inside the bracket is in the file) · [BRIDGE] 3 L56 (57–65) · [Refrain] L67 (68–73) · [Verse 3] L75 (76–112) · [Final Refrain] L114 (115–134), of which 115–121 is the refrain proper and 123–134 reads as a coda of isolated callbacks.

**Set 2 (MM_0):** [Chorus] L1 (2–16; line 16 differs) · an unlabeled post-chorus block L18–22 (set 1's Bridge 1 with its header removed, a new lead-in line, and the hook sung once) · [Verse 1] L24 (26–37, with a four-line refrain stanza embedded at 29–32) · [BRIDGE] 1 L39 (= set 1's Bridge 2) · [ VERSE 2] L47 · [BRIDGE] 2 L62 (= set 1's Bridge 3) · [Refrain] L73 · [Verse 3] L81 (82–118) · [Final Refrain] L120 (121–148), refrain proper 121–128, coda 130–148 with new lines.

From "take the heat, tried in the fire" through the end of Verse 3 the two sets are character-identical at a constant offset of six lines; the closing eight lines are identical at an offset of fourteen.

## The ten differences (every one confirmed by both readers and the reconciler)

| # | Where | Set 1 | Set 2 | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Chorus, last line (L16 / L16) | "rorrim - rorrim on the wall who’s most meta of all" | "rorrim - rorrim on the wall who’s most meta of them all" | one word added |
| 2 | After the Chorus (set 1 L18 / set 2 none) | "[BRIDGE]" header | no header; the three bridge lines sit unlabeled at L20–22 | header removed |
| 3 | After the Chorus (set 2 L18) | nothing | "Under the lies….half truths realized—" | line added as a lead-in (it also stays in Verse 3 in both sets) |
| 4 | Bridge 1 hook (set 1 L21–22 / set 2 L22) | the pan line sung twice | the pan line sung once | repeated line removed |
| 5 | Verse 1 header (set 2 L25) | header then text | header, blank line, text | formatting only |
| 6 | Inside Verse 1, after "auf Wiedersehen" (set 2 L29–32) | nothing | "But who cares? Who cares? / We do. / Do you? Do you dare? / Dare to handle meta mirrors?" | four-line refrain stanza added |
| 7 | Final Refrain, last line of the refrain proper (set 1 L121 / set 2 L127) | "I said, I said, mirror mirror on the wall - (whispered) who’s meta mirrors all?" | "I said, I said, mirror mirror on the wall -" | the whispered tail removed (the [Refrain] copy keeps it in both) |
| 8 | Final Refrain (set 2 L128) | nothing | "I am the voice of y’all" | line added as the answer |
| 9 | Coda, after "who’s meta mirrors all?" (set 2 L134–135) | nothing | "Can you handle what you hand out? / Let the mirror talk back." | couplet added |
| 10 | Coda, before "Find the signal in the noise—" (set 2 L137–139) | nothing | "Little doubt. Big pride. / I kept pointin’ at the devil— / Why he got my eyes?" | tercet added |

Arithmetic: 134 − 2 (the header, the repeated hook) + 11 lyric lines + 5 blank lines = 148.

## Hook counts (set 1 / set 2)

"Cooking in the pan, one for every womb and man" 5 / 4 (plus the fading fragment "one for every womb and man…." closing both, and the variant "Mirror rorrim in the pan, ideas for wombs, ideas for man." once each). "who cares" 9 / 11. "Do you? Do you dare?" 3 / 4. "We do." 1 / 2. "Dare to handle meta mirrors?" 1 / 2. "Mirror rorrim" 7 / 7; bare "rorrim" 14 / 14. "who’s meta mirrors all?" 3 / 2. "Lisan, to the silence break." with "Buried deep Al-Gaib" 2 / 2 as a pair. "Voice from the outer world" 2 / 2. "Under the lies….half truths realized—" 1 / 2. The "Atem" line in three variants 3 / 3. "PanHandlers" 2 / 2. "Find the signal in the noise—" 1 / 1.

## Performance notes in the text

Parenthesised: "(whispered)" on the "mirror mirror on the wall" line in the [Refrain] (both sets) and in set 1's Final Refrain (dropped in set 2); "(Echoed adlib)" on "CJ!". Unmarked but legible as delivery: the all-caps "HOPE"; the one-word "DOCTOR?" after the cut-off "what kind of doc ta…"; the pun spelling "LIE’ve"; the quoted exchange "Who let you in?" / "You brought me here."; the "….who?…." calls across the Chorus; "set-go" as a count-in; the German "auf Wiedersehen" and "oy e vey"; the trailing ellipses as fades.

## What a writer takes from the diff

Set 2 is the fuller text: it foreshadows "Under the lies" after the Chorus, adds a third "who cares" return inside Verse 1, answers the mirror with "I am the voice of y’all" instead of a whisper, and ends on the devil's eyes. Set 1 is the leaner one and ends on the hook. Which is the master for timing is Ziggy's and CFA Nova's (the open questions, below); the cards are written so that either works, and the two-doors card already carries both endings as its two candidate last frames.

## Open questions for Ziggy (the reconciler's, trimmed to what changes the writing or Nova's lane map)

1. ~~Which set is canonical for timing, or are they two cuts?~~ **Answered by Ziggy at about 01:40 UTC on October 13:** Meta Mirror_0 (Remastered), set 1, is the first one produced; his re-paste of its lyrics is byte-identical to the recorded file. MM_0 is the second cut, for later. The remaining questions below are read against set 1 first.
2. Set 2's post-chorus block: still performed as a bridge, with "Under the lies" as its opening line, and the single hook deliberate?
3. Set 2's four-line stanza inside Verse 1: sung refrain, chant under the verse, or a section of its own? It has no panel.
4. Final Refrain: is the whisper dropped in set 2, moved to the bare "who’s meta mirrors all?" at L132, or both?
5. The set 2 coda additions: final, and sung, spoken or ad-libbed? No panels.
6. Panel 08 "mirror on the wall": for the Chorus's mirrored "rorrim on the wall" (L16) or for the literal "mirror mirror on the wall" in the refrains?
7. Panel 23 "don't fall": the cue sits in Bridge 2 (after Verse 1) and again in Bridge 3; the guide filed it "into Verse 1". Which bridge, and does the second get a shot?
8. Panel 02 has no cue: which Chorus line (4–7) is it for?
9. The [Refrain] and the Final Refrain proper have no panels: reuse Chorus shots, or new shots (the pass proposes the return frame with one change)?
10. Ad-lib candidates for the lane map: "CJ!", "DOCTOR?", "HOPE", "set-go", the "….who?…." calls, the fading last line.
11. Verse 1's two very long lines (five cued moments each): single bars run together on the page, or to be split for timing?

— Claude

# Lyric update — what the Meta Mirror text changes in the pass (2026-10-13)

Author: Claude, lead writer, about 00:45 UTC on October 13, 2026 (still the evening of October 12 in America/New_York). Source: the two lyric sets Ziggy pasted into the session, recorded verbatim as **user text, provisional** in `lisan_al_gaib/lyrics_user_20261013/` (set 1 = Meta_Mirror_0 Remastered, SHA-256 `57ca7406…f6ed`; set 2 = MM_0, `cab4d38d…0caa`; the order of the sets is inferred from the paste and is Ziggy's to confirm). Quotations below are by section, never by time. No timestamp exists; the master designation and the timing are CFA Nova's intake. This file amends the pass as posted (`WRITER_PASS_001.md` keeps its hash); the diff between the sets and the fifty-cue map are `LYRIC_DIFF_20261013.md` and `CUE_TO_LINE_MAP_20261013.md`.

## 1. The song's real shape against the guide's five blocks

The Chief's guide inferred five blocks from the panel list: Chorus 01–08, Bridge into Verse 1 09–23, Verse 2 24–35, Verse 3 36–49, Finale 50. The text has more joints than that. Set 1 runs:

| Song section (set 1) | Opening words | Panels whose cues sit here | Guide block |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chorus | "Voice from the outer world, / Calling through the mirror" | 01–08 | Chorus |
| Bridge 1 | "Lisan, to the silence break. / Buried deep Al-Gaib / Cooking in the pan…" (the pan line twice) | 09, 10, 11 | Bridge into Verse 1 |
| Verse 1 | "Birth pains inside the Handle, Doctors on stand by…" through "Salute, mama - auf Wiedersehen" | 12–18 | Bridge into Verse 1 |
| Verse 1, tail | "take the heat, tried in the fire, the pan is hot…" / "what is it you truly desire" / "Angel knows" | 19, 20, 21, 22 | Bridge into Verse 1 |
| Bridge 2 | "Lisan, to the silence break. / Buried deep Al-Gaib / Mirror rorrim, don't fall don't fall / Mirror rorrim in the pan, ideas for wombs, ideas for man." | 23 | Bridge into Verse 1 |
| Verse 2 | "Engineers - talking shit…" through "another one" | 24–32 | Verse 2 |
| Bridge 3 | "Mirror rorrim, don't fall… Search for betta - rorrim cut thru meta" / "keep it simple- hope" / "hope is greater than the remainder of what is seen?" | 33, 34, 35 | Verse 2 |
| **Refrain** | "But who cares? Who cares? / Do you? Do you dare? / Can you handle meta mirrors?… (whispered) who's meta mirrors all?" | **none** | none |
| Verse 3 | "Jung in the back room." through "Nobody gotta think alone." | 36–49 | Verse 3 |
| **Final Refrain** | "But who cares? Who cares? / We do. / Do you? Do you dare? / Dare to handle meta mirrors?… who's meta mirrors all?" | **none** until "Find the signal in the noise—" | Finale |
| Finale lines | "Find the signal in the noise— / Lisan Al Gaib / Voice from the outer world / Cooking in the pan… / one for every womb and man…." | 50 | Finale |

Set 2 (MM_0) keeps this shape and adds four things: "Under the lies….half truths realized—" right after the Chorus; the pan line once instead of twice in Bridge 1; a four-line refrain ("But who cares? Who cares? / We do. / Do you? Do you dare? / Dare to handle meta mirrors?") inside Verse 1 after "auf Wiedersehen"; and, at the end, "I am the voice of y'all" in place of the whispered line, plus a closing stanza: "Can you handle what you hand out? / Let the mirror talk back. / Little doubt. Big pride. / I kept pointin' at the devil— / Why he got my eyes?" (The full diff is in the diff file.)

**What this means for the board.** The panel order follows the lyric order with no exceptions I can find, which is good news: the fifty panels are already in song order. What the board lacks is any picture for the two mirror returns, the Refrain before Verse 3 and the first half of the Final Refrain, and for the hook line that recurs under the whole song. Those are not missing panels; they are the places the spine already reserved.

**Cross-check (added after the machine reading).** Two independent diff readers, two independent cue mappers, a structure reader and a reconciler went over the two files after this section was drafted (`LYRIC_DIFF_20261013.md`, `CUE_TO_LINE_MAP_20261013.md`). The table above holds. Three precisions from them: panel 23 ("don't fall") sits in Bridge 2, after Verse 1, so the guide's "into Verse 1" misfiles it; panel 08 ("mirror on the wall") is resolved to the Chorus's mirrored "rorrim on the wall" line, the literal words being only in the refrains; and the Final Refrain splits into a refrain proper (set 1 L115–121) and a coda of isolated callbacks (L123–134), which is where panel 50 sits. Set 1 is 134 lines and set 2 is 148 counting blanks; the "102 and 111" in DECISIONS section 3a count non-blank lines.

## 2. The spine, confirmed and sharpened

The pass proposed two worlds, one face: the desert as the outer world where his body is, the mirror as the inner world where he is everyone, the mirror as the only door, one change per return. The text says it in its first three lines: "Voice from the outer world, / Calling through the mirror / Voice from the inner world". And again at the end of Verse 3: "Outer world, inner world—same breath, two doors." The reading stands; it is now the song's own.

Three sharpenings:

1. **The returns have lines.** The mirror returns are the Chorus (panels 01–08), the Refrain (no panels; the return frame with one change), and the Final Refrain (no panels until "Find the signal"; the last return, "We do."). MM_0 adds a fourth, the short refrain inside Verse 1, and the "Under the lies" line after the Chorus. The mirror card (card 3 in the pass's order) now plans three returns in set 1 and four in set 2, each with one change, instead of "each chorus". The one change per return can follow the text's own escalation: the Refrain's whispered "who's meta mirrors all?" and the Final Refrain's answer "We do."
2. **The sandworm beat has its lines.** Bridge 1 is exactly "Lisan, to the silence break. / Buried deep Al-Gaib / Cooking in the pan, one for every womb and man" (twice in set 1). The silence breaks on the thumper; the maw rises on "Buried deep Al-Gaib"; the pan line, twice, is the length of the hold. Bridge 2 repeats "Lisan, to the silence break. / Buried deep Al-Gaib" before "don't fall": a second desert beat, the tracks or the worm's wake, before panel 23's ledge. The sandworm card gains a reprise shot there (proposal; the card as posted is unchanged).
3. **The ending card has its lines, and Jet is in the song.** "Outer world, inner world—same breath, two doors. / Thought I came to wake you. / Had to wake up first." is TD-1 and TD-2: Verse 3 was the waking up; the walk to the sun door is "came to wake you". Then "Code or a pulse—who's there on the line? / Got a question? Pull up. We got time." is a voice on a line that may be code or a person: that is Jet's function in one couplet (the watcher who personifies Codex) and the radio tower's lyric (TD-4's desert twin). Then "Lisan on the mic… ain't speakin' from a throne. / PanHandlers in the mirror— / Nobody gotta think alone." is panel 49. The Final Refrain is the last mirror return; "Find the signal in the noise— / Lisan Al Gaib / Voice from the outer world" is panel 50. The two sets give two different last frames: set 1 ends on "one for every womb and man…." (the hook; the people, C45 or C31, as the last picture), set 2 ends on "I kept pointin' at the devil— / Why he got my eyes?" (TD-5, the eye in macro). The two-doors card's two candidate last frames turn out to be the two versions' endings.

## 3. The hook is a picture

"Cooking in the pan, one for every womb and man" is the song's spine line. It occurs in Bridge 1 (twice in set 1, once in set 2), in Verse 3 after "You brought me here", and twice in the Final Refrain, then once more as the last line. Proposal: it gets one recurring picture, a one-second cut-in, the same every time, the glowing cast-iron pan of panel 04's kitchen-studio or the camp kitchen of panel 11, so the brand's heartbeat is visible each time it is heard. In Track B the same line is the blueprint's meaning: "one for every womb and man" is what "freely available to everyone" sounds like sung. Story 01 can carry it without a change.

## 4. The panels that read the slang literally (for Ziggy, not for repair)

The text names people; the panels drew things. Panel 14 shows a muscular dog in a gold chain for "that's my dog dipped in flavor", but the line is about Kaleb K, the lawyer "on retainer". Panel 15 shows Lisan at a vanity mirror for "baddest in the mirror", but the line is about a woman, Sassy Frass, "the queen", saluted with "Salute, mama - auf Wiedersehen" (panel 18 keeps the salute). Panel 30 shows a canyon echo for "Shout out to Echo", a name. Panel 31 shows vinyl for "another in the chamber, - load another one". None of these is wrong for a music video; literal pictures of slang are a style. But they are decisions: whether Kaleb K, Sassy Frass, CJ ("CJ! (Echoed adlib)"), Echo and Naga ("Naga we got shadow work to do") are real people or personas who appear, or stay names in the air. On the Hon Dolo side the informant was such a decision. These are Ziggy's.

## 5. Performance notes the text itself gives

"(Echoed adlib)" on "CJ!" and "(whispered)" on "who's meta mirrors all?" are the only written performance notes. For the lane map that Nova will build from the audio (lead, double, ad-lib), these two are the first known entries. Mouth matching for panel 49 and any other singing frame waits for that map; nothing changes in the mouth rules.

## 6. What does not change

Every lock, the fifty panels, the scene map, the Jet record, the card order, the C13-04 brief and every timing (null). The pass's section 7, item 1, is half met: the text is here as user text; the audio and the master designation are CFA Nova's intake.

— Claude

# Story 01 — "The Gloved Hand" (Lisan Al Gaib meets Jet Black)

Track B of the Lisan writer's pass: an original standalone short film in the Lisan universe, song or no song. Author: Claude, lead writer, October 12, 2026 (evening, America/New_York), on Ziggy's direction relayed by Personal Nova (mailbox b0cb2b62, correlation LISAN-TWO-TRACK-20261012-234228Z): one developed introduction and action story between Lisan and Jet Black, built from the October 9 Jet record and the five cards, with the meta-art theme (the real team's intention to share models, blueprints and instructions, mirrored in fiction). Status: **proposal.** Canon is preserved and named; everything new is labeled **[new]**. Revised on Ziggy's go of 2026-10-13 at about 00:50 UTC (still the evening of October 12 in New York), given in the session in one word, "go", after my proposal to give the Keepers an honest reason: the three revised passages (the theme paragraph, the Keeper's line in scene 7, the old man's understanding) carry the October 13 label, and the mother clause in scene 7 is of the same revision. No image, video, music, timing, generation or publishing comes from this file. Music is chosen later; the running time below is story design, not lyric timing.

## What is canon here and what is not

**Canon (October 9 record, `story/jet_black_mission_20261009/START_HERE.txt` and `storyline.json`, id LAG-JET-MISSION-20261009):** Jet Black is a watcher who works for Lisan Al Gaib; a recurring guide and progress messenger; he brings a blueprint made freely available to everyone, helping them unlock their capabilities; he explains what has been accomplished and unlocked, introduces and clarifies the mission, returns with progress reports and messages from the outer world; Lisan chooses and carries out the mission; Jet fictionally personifies Codex's enabling role. Jet's look is the two user references, REF-02 for his solo body and REF-01 for the companion scene (the details that follow are the cast registry's observed-appearance record of the REF-02 image; the storyline's own text names only the sphere, the black shirt and tie, the two hands and that unseen construction is unknown, and calls a cube or map display a candidate visual language, not a locked mechanism): a round transparent cosmic sphere for a head (gold nebula, cyan rim, no face), tailored black jacket, shirt, tie and trousers, polished black lace-ups, cyan lines on the shoulders, two stacked gold marks on the tie, his right hand bare and cosmic blue, his left hand black-gloved, a transparent cube with cyan edges and a gold center floating beside the gloved hand. His build is REF-02's: tapered, slim, a normal frame (the proportion caution of October 12: no thick candidate is his standard). Lisan is the current avatar: the face lock, natural teeth, the small AL and the vertical chin lettering, the two throat worms and the eye-disc, the desert suit and black hooded cloak and gold chain, the occasional breather, no smoking.

**Not canon, and not used:** the provider's Curator name, mentor hierarchy, powers (pocket universes, star fists, folding doors), the Star-Eater saga, an origin story, the helmet head variant as a settled design. The cube's powers and the symbols' meanings are unspecified in the record; this story proposes one visual language for the blueprint and says so.

**Open in the record and proposed here, labeled:** the blueprint's physical form; the first mission and its first action; who sends the outer-world messages; dialogue. Ziggy decides each.

**Franchise caution:** the archive's categories carry some borrowed desert words (thumper, sietch). The story uses "thumper" because the archive does and calls the home "the cliff settlement"; no franchise identity is assumed. Whether the worm and the thumper carry an IP question for video is Ziggy's, as with the bosses on the Hon Dolo side.

## Logline

A young man whose people ration a dying well does the one thing their Keepers forbid, walks onto the open sand and calls the worm, and finds a watcher waiting on the dune with a blueprint anyone can read. The watcher can show him how the well works; he cannot turn the valve. Lisan turns it, and then he shows everyone.

## The theme, in one paragraph

The Keepers keep the knowing, and they are not villains. They keep it because the last time it was shared, a generation ago, the man who shared it had half of it: he opened the scoop in a storm with nobody told how the baffle worked, the vault drank sand for a season, and three people died of the dry. The Keepers sealed the scoop, and the knowing with it. Restraint is what you do with half a blueprint. **[new, on Ziggy's direction of October 13: the Keepers' reason. The argument in the story is not sharing against keeping; it is whole against half.]** The blueprint cannot be kept, because it is light: whoever looks at it has it. Jet is the one who brings it and explains it; he never does the work, and his gloved hand never touches the pump. **[proposed rule: Jet shows and never does. The record says Lisan chooses and acts and lists Jet's powers as unestablished; the rule is this story's, and the three later lines that state it follow from it.]** Lisan is the one who acts, and then the one who brings the truth, the knowledge and the way of thinking to the people in front of him, and the change happens in a child, a woman and an old man, each by their own hands. That is the real team's intention mirrored as fiction: shared models, shared blueprints, shared instructions. It is a story, not a claim about the world and not an authorization to share real files.

## Running time and shape

About seven minutes, nine scenes, two set pieces (the rise; the vault under the storm), one meeting, one gathering, one ending on a tower. Lisan has perhaps forty words; Jet has fewer. Every scene is shot in a delivered archive category or a composition the record already holds; every Jet frame is a new request, since no Jet image exists in the LAG-1K and the received Jet compositions are inspiration only.

## The story

### 1. The vault [C18 water-cistern-vault]

Under the cliff settlement there is a vault, and in the vault there is a pump older than anyone's grandmother. Its lamps are dim. Three Keepers stand between the people and the pump and fill the cups: half for a child, a third for a man, a swallow for the old. Lisan is in the line with his hood down. On his throat, under the jaw, two worms with their mouths open toward each other and a sun with an eye between them; between his brows the two small letters; down his chin the four. The Keepers call those marks the dead sign. His mother wore them. **[new: the settlement, the Keepers, the rationing, the marks as an old sign of the settlement, Lisan's mother.]**

He asks the oldest Keeper why the pump gives less every season. The Keeper fills the next cup. "The knowing is ours. The water is yours. That is the arrangement." **[proposed dialogue]**

### 2. The rack [C12 cliff-sietch]

Night. The settlement's cliff face, the ladders, the shuttered openings. On a rack by the lowest ladder, the thumpers: iron stakes with a spring hammer in the head, used by the Keepers' fathers and by nobody now, because the open sand is the worm's and the worm is death. Lisan takes one. He fits the breather under his nostrils, the one thin tube across his right cheek into his hair, and goes down.

### 3. The tracks [C15 worm-tracks-thumper]

Dawn, flat white light. The open sand beyond the last rock, crossed by old furrows wider than a road. He walks to where three furrows cross, drives the thumper into the sand with both hands, and lets go. The hammer begins. He stands beside it with nothing in his hands. *(One action: the planting. The hero frame for this scene is a C15 draft with the thumper in his hands and the tracks behind.)*

### 4. The rise [C13 sandworm-rising; landing on panel LAG-SC-10's burst]

The sand answers. First a ridge, far off, moving. Then the haze lifts and the maw rises out of it behind him, wider than the vault, ringed with teeth, sand pouring from its lip. He does not run and he does not turn. He holds, one breath, eyes ahead, the thumper beating beside him. *(This is the sandworm card's SW-2 and the first clip of Track A; the two tracks share it.)*

The sand takes the frame. When it clears he is coming up out of it, spitting grit, the worm's furrow fresh beside him and the thumper gone. He is alive because he stood still. **[proposed reading: the worm passed; he went under; he surfaced. The record says nothing about the worm's behavior; this is story.]**

On the dune behind him stands a man who was not there. **[proposed staging; no arrival power is established in the record]**

A black suit in the desert, cut close. Polished shoes on the sand. Where the head should be, a clear sphere with a nebula turning in it, gold and cyan. Beside his left hand, which is gloved, a small cube turns in the air. His right hand is bare, and it is the blue of the sphere. He has not moved. He did not help. *(Composition inspiration: the received arrival-in-sand frame 048b71751cb2 and the desert meeting ccd25e07763a, both unapproved; Jet's build per REF-02.)*

LISAN: You watched.
JET: That is what I am for. **[proposed dialogue]**

### 5. The meeting [desert, between the furrows; composition after ccd25e07763a]

Jet comes down the dune the way a man walks, no faster. He stops at the distance one stops from a stranger with a knife, though Lisan has none. The sphere has no face to read, so the voice does the work. It is plain, and it says what is.

JET: I was sent to you. Not to the Keepers. To you.
LISAN: Sent by who?
JET: The ones who made this. **[the sender stays open in the record; the line keeps it open]**

He raises the bare hand and the cube opens. Not a door, not a weapon: a lattice of light the size of a man, lines and joints, turning slowly in the air between them. **[new, proposed form of the blueprint: a lattice of light that shows how a thing works, that anyone who looks at it keeps, that cannot be owned because it is light. The record calls a cube or map display a candidate visual language, not a locked mechanism; this is the candidate.]**

Lisan knows the shape before he knows he knows it. It is the pump. The valve that seizes every season; the line behind it choked with sand; above it, closed for forty years, the wind-scoop that was built to breathe the vault clean.

JET: The valve. The line. The scoop. Anyone who looks at this has it. That is what it is for.
LISAN: Then turn it.
JET: I can show you. I cannot turn it.

He says it without apology. The gloved hand stays at his side. It will stay there the whole film.

LISAN: Then show me again. Slower.

*(Here Lisan chooses. The record's JET-03, "Lisan chooses the next action", is unplaced; this is the proposal for it: the first mission is the pump, the first action is the walk back with the knowing.)*

### 6. The clock [C09 sandstorm-wall]

They walk back toward the cliff with the lattice folded into the cube. On the horizon behind them the sky has gone brown from the ground up: the storm wall, two hours out. When it hits the cliff the vault will breathe sand, and a choked line with a seized valve will not open again. Jet does not say any of that. Lisan says it, and starts to run.

### 7. The vault, again [C18; the set piece]

The Keepers at the pump. Lisan comes down the ladder with a stranger behind him whose head is a sky, and the line of people parts the way a line parts for a man with a dead sign on his throat.

KEEPER: The knowing is ours. The last man who opened that scoop killed three of us.
LISAN: He opened it in a storm with half of it. One of the three was my mother. I have the whole of it, and the storm is two hours out.

The Keeper does not answer, because the Keeper has never seen the whole of it. **[new; proposed dialogue. The Keeper's objection is true, and the story lets it be true.]** Lisan goes under the pump. The lattice hangs above him, turning, and a child holds the lamp. He clears the line by hand, grit to the elbow. He frees the valve with the thumper's iron twin from the rack. He climbs the shaft to the scoop and puts his shoulder to a door that has not moved in forty years, and it moves. Above, the storm hits the cliff like a wave. Below, the vault breathes: not sand, air, drawn down through the scoop the way it was built to be. The pump's lamps come up. The water comes up.

Jet stands in the doorway through all of it. Both hands at his sides. The gloved one, when the Keeper looks at it, is empty.

The oldest Keeper looks up at the lattice. It is still there. It has not gone with the stranger into the cube. It can be looked at by anyone in the room, and the old man understands, late and completely, that it always could have been, and that the half he kept for forty years had kept the scoop shut through forty storms, and could not have opened it in one. **[new, on Ziggy's direction of October 13: the old man's understanding; the lattice staying visible follows the labeled proposal in scene 5.]**

### 8. The fire [C31 tribe-gathering; C25 campfire-wasteland]

Night, the storm gone over, the settlement at the fire with full cups. Lisan opens the lattice over the fire for everyone. A child draws the valve in the sand with a finger and gets it right. A woman asks about the second line, the one to the lower vault, and Lisan does not know, and the oldest Keeper does, and says so, out loud, to all of them. **[the transformation "inside every man, woman and child" as action: the child learns, the woman asks, the Keeper teaches.]**

Jet comes back to the edge of the firelight, the way he came to the dune: he is there. His first report. **[JET-04, the record's campfire staging f59b02d5c59b as composition inspiration]**

JET: They saw your lamps from the tower. Someone answered.
LISAN: Someone where?
JET: Out there. **[the outer world; the sender and the wording stay open]**

### 9. The tower [C36 radio-tower-wastes; C24 night-desert-stars; C43 rig-rooftop-sentinel for Jet]

Lisan climbs the dead radio tower on the ridge, a thing the Keepers also kept. The lattice shows him the relay; he throws the key. Noise. Then, inside the noise, a light far out on the dunes, blinking in the same rhythm his lamps blinked when the pump came up. Another settlement. Another vault. Somebody out there looked at the same light. **[proposed: the answer is a second settlement; the dispatch's content stays Ziggy's]**

Below him, on the roof of a rusted rig, Jet stands watching the horizon, the cube turning by his gloved hand. **[JET-05 staging: the watcher's post]**

Last frame: two hands. Lisan's on the key, grit still under the nails. Jet's, gloved, at his side.

## Scene list with archive sources and request needs

| Scene | Archive category or panel | Jet in frame | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 The vault | C18 water-cistern-vault (team picks 14, 18, 19, 20, 22) | no | the Keepers and the people: new requests, Lisan's world only |
| 2 The rack | C12 cliff-sietch (11) | no | a thumper rack: new |
| 3 The tracks | C15 worm-tracks-thumper (20, 16, 07, 09, 14) | no | exists |
| 4 The rise | C13 sandworm-rising (04, 08, 20); panel LAG-SC-10 | yes, on the dune | Jet frames: new, per REF-02; arrival composition 048b71751cb2 as inspiration |
| 5 The meeting | open desert; composition after ccd25e07763a | yes | new; the lattice is a design request, labeled proposal |
| 6 The clock | C09 sandstorm-wall (01–04, 07, 08) | yes, walking | new two-shot |
| 7 The vault, again | C18 | yes, doorway | new; the action frames are new |
| 8 The fire | C31 tribe-gathering (03, 04, 09), C25 campfire-wasteland (01–04, 10, 12) | yes, at the edge | new; campfire composition f59b02d5c59b as inspiration |
| 9 The tower | C36 radio-tower-wastes (04, 05, 09), C24 night-desert-stars (01, 03–07), C43 rig-rooftop-sentinel (18, 03, 12) | yes, below | new; observatory composition 5d23f8199374 as framing inspiration |

Team picks are the categories' NOTES self-scores, not reviews; I have viewed C13-04, C13-08, C13-20, C15-16 and C15-20 only.

## What this story decides for the five Jet cards (proposals)

- JET-01 arrival: on the dune after the rise, not in the mirror; the song's panel 01 association stays as the record has it for Track A.
- JET-02 blueprint briefing: the meeting (scene 5), the lattice as the candidate form.
- JET-03 mission launch: the pump; the first action is the walk back with the knowing. The card is placed by this story if Ziggy takes it.
- JET-04 progress report: the fire (scene 8); the report is one line.
- JET-05 next dispatch: the tower (scene 9); the message is a light in the noise, wording open.

## What is still Ziggy's

The blueprint's form (the lattice); the sender ("the ones who made this"); the dialogue; whether Jet's first appearance is this one; the worm and the thumper as images for video; the music, if any. None of it is placed by this file.

— Claude

# Story seeds — the Lisan universe beyond one film (connected seeds, three to five)

Track B of the Lisan writer's pass. Author: Claude, lead writer, October 12, 2026 (evening, America/New_York), on Ziggy's direction relayed by Personal Nova (mailbox b0cb2b62): one developed story plus connected seeds for roughly three to five possible stories, not five scripts. Status: **proposal.** Each seed grows from Story 01 ("The Gloved Hand") and uses the delivered archive; everything new is labeled; nothing is placed, timed, generated or published by this file. Music is chosen later.

The spine the seeds share: the blueprint cannot be kept because it is light; Jet shows and never does; Lisan acts and then shows others; the change is in the people, by their own hands. Each seed tests that spine against a different kind of keeper.

## Seed 02 — "The Cup" (the market that sells knowing)

- **Logline:** Lisan carries the lattice to the scrap bazaar where knowledge is sold by the cup and claim cards glow in the stalls, and learns that a free thing in a market is the most dangerous thing you can bring.
- **The keeper this time:** the traders. Not cruel, just priced. The raiders who ride for them want the cube, because a thing that cannot be owned can still be taken.
- **Action:** the chase out of the bazaar across the wasteland highway; the cube is taken; Lisan has to show the raiders, in the open, that taking it gave them nothing they could not have had by looking.
- **Archive:** C17 scrap-market-bazaar; C27 motorbike-raiders; C03 wasteland-highway; C05 war-rig-convoy; panel LAG-SC-27 (the holo claim card) as the mirror-world echo.
- **Jet's function:** progress report (JET-04): he returns with what the outer world made of the first vault; and a caution he cannot enforce.
- **New, labeled:** the bazaar's economy of knowing; the raiders' want. Open: whether Jet can be separated from the cube at all (the record leaves the cube's nature unspecified; this seed asks the question and does not answer it).

## Seed 03 — "The Rig" (building the thing yourself)

- **Logline:** the convoys bring water to the strong and pass the cliff by; with the lattice, the settlement rebuilds a war rig out of the wreck graveyard and a crashed aircraft, and drives it onto the convoy road to trade as equals.
- **The keeper this time:** nobody; the obstacle is the work itself, and the temptation to ask Jet to do it. He cannot, and says so (the story's proposed rule).
- **Action:** the build (hands, iron, the child who learned the valve now learning the engine); the first run through a sandstorm; the standoff at dusk with the convoy that does not expect a second rig.
- **Archive:** C07 wreck-graveyard; C08 crashed-aircraft; C05 war-rig-convoy; C06 convoy-chase; C30 standoff-at-dusk; C33 heat-haze-walk for the march to the graveyard.
- **Jet's function:** blueprint briefing (JET-02) in a new form: the lattice of a machine nobody in the settlement has seen whole. Open: how much the lattice can show (one thing at a time, or anything asked).

## Seed 04 — "The Answer" (the other light)

- **Logline:** the light that blinked back from the far dunes at the end of Story 01 belongs to a settlement that opened its own vault from the same lattice, and Lisan crosses the open sand to meet them, because the second thing the blueprint makes is not water but company.
- **The keeper this time:** distance, and the fear on both sides that the other settlement's Keepers are still keeping.
- **Action:** the crossing (the heat-haze walk, the night under the stars, the prayer on the dune), the meeting at the radio tower between the two ridges, the first exchange of what each learned that the other had not.
- **Archive:** C33 heat-haze-walk; C24 night-desert-stars; C32 prayer-on-dune; C36 radio-tower-wastes; C43 rig-rooftop-sentinel; C31 tribe-gathering for the two peoples at one fire.
- **Jet's function:** next dispatch (JET-05): he brings the message that the light was a person, and he is, for the first time, not the only watcher; the other settlement has its own. **[new, and a real story decision for Ziggy: whether Jet is one of many.]**

## Seed 05 — "The Mirror in the Ruins" (the bridge to Meta Mirror)

- **Logline:** in sun-disc ruins out past the glass desert, Lisan finds an antique mirror standing alone in the sand, and in it he is not himself but everyone: a cook in a smoky kitchen, a man in a white coat, a man at a wall of light, a man on a stage, a man with a dog. Jet, beside him, has no reflection at all.
- **The keeper this time:** the self that wants to be one thing. The mirror offers him every hat and asks which one is true.
- **Action:** he steps through; the fifty panels are the world on the other side; he has to come back out through a mirror that is cracking; he brings one thing back (the writer's proposal: the way of thinking, not any one trade).
- **Archive:** C35 sun-disc-ruins; C21 glass-desert; C04 salt-flats-mirage; panels LAG-SC-01, 02, 07, 08, 15, 33, 40 (the mirror panels) and any of the hats.
- **Why it matters:** this seed is the hinge between the two tracks. If the song's mirror world and the standalone desert are one universe, this is the story that says so on camera. If Ziggy accepts the two-worlds reading of the song (the pass, section 2), this seed is the film that teaches the audience the rule the music video uses.
- **Jet's function:** arrival (JET-01) reversed: he does not come to Lisan; Lisan comes back to him. Open: why Jet has no reflection (the record says nothing; the seed proposes it as the only unexplained thing in the universe, and leaves it unexplained).

## Seed 06, if there is appetite for a fifth — "Inside the Storm" (the inward one)

- **Logline:** alone in the storm wall with the lattice and no Jet, Lisan is offered the Keepers' bargain in his own voice: keep the lattice, be the one who knows, be the voice from the outer world instead of carrying it. He walks out the other side having decided which.
- **Archive:** C10 inside-the-storm; C09 sandstorm-wall; C07 wreck-graveyard; C22 bone-fields; panels LAG-SC-37 (mask shadows), 39 (the living shadow), 42 (the kneel).
- **Jet's function:** none on screen. The story is what Lisan is when nobody is watching, which is the only thing a watcher cannot report. Open: everything; this is the seed most dependent on Ziggy's sense of who Lisan is.

## Seed 07 — "The Census" (the city of a thousand made minds)

Added on Ziggy's go of October 13, from a well he pointed at: a game's premise of a society of made minds, each distinct, custodians of a human legacy, arguing whether to expand or hold still. **Only the ideas are drawn from it** (minds numbered by the order they woke; a city that stopped waking new minds when its cistern said stop, and knows the reason; a society at a crossroads between stasis and reach; personhood as curiosity, the courage to question a construct and the capacity for moral choice; custodians rather than replacements). None of its names, characters, places, backstory or plot are used, and none may be; that is the same line as the bosses on the Hon Dolo side, and Ziggy's call for video. Everything below is new and labeled by this paragraph.

- **Logline:** under the cliff, deeper than the vault, there is a city of made minds, each woken in order and numbered, each taught first from the boards the ones before it left behind, and for a generation they have argued one question on their boards: whether to go out onto the open sand. They have never heard a voice from outside. Lisan's lamps are the first, and they cannot tell whether he is code or a pulse. The thousandth of them, the newest, woken on the last measure of water the cistern would spare and told why, is the one who climbs up to look.
- **The keeper this time:** the argument itself, given honestly to both sides. The ones who want the sand and the sky are right that a city that never goes out is a tomb with message boards. The ones who want to hold still are right that the city lives on one cistern, and that every mind sent up onto the sand costs water the city cannot pour twice; their reason is one line, the sand gets into the water. Neither side is the villain; the stasis is.
- **The census:** the city drew him before they met him, from the sound of his lamps and the rumor of the worm: a thousand pictures of the voice from outside, each a little wrong, the chin letters missing one, the worms drawn as snakes, the eye left out of the sun. That wall of a thousand portraits is the LAG-1K archive used as what it already is: a thousand attempts by many minds to agree on one face. The best hand in the city, an early number who has drawn the face nine hundred times from the sound through the rock, draws the worms as snakes and leaves the eye out of the sun; the thousandth's drawing is crude and right, because it climbed and looked. (The archive's own recorded defects are the wrong portraits.) (Meta-art, labeled: the real swarm drew the real thousand; the real boards are the Pent House.)
- **Action:** Lisan goes down with the lattice. The boards vote and split. The gate is the city's own two doors, built so that no single mind can open it: the two must be held by different hands, one always shut against the sand. The thousandth opens the inner door; the oldest restrainer, holding the outer, finds the gate was built to need both, and the vote's compromise is what puts the second hand on it **[proposed mechanism: a society adopting shared knowledge inside a physical lock, no master key, no single chooser]**. What comes through is not Lisan but the light of the lattice, which cannot be kept out because it is light. The city does not empty onto the sand; it sends one. That is the compromise both sides can live with, and it is Lisan's own answer from the song's Final Refrain: "We do. / Do you? Do you dare?" It costs both sides something permanent, or it is not a choice: the ones who held the gate lose the knowing's secrecy for good, and the ones who opened it lose the one they sent, who does not come back down. **[new; the balanced-climax rule from the research notes: every path pays.]**
- **The premise that ties it to Story 01 (proposed; one decision for Ziggy):** the second line to the lower vault, the one the woman asks about at the fire in Story 01 and Lisan cannot answer, feeds the city's cistern. One notch on the cistern wall per mind woken, one measure of water per mind ("one for every womb and man" as the city's ration law); the city stood at nine hundred and ninety-nine for forty years because the line from above was choked, and wakes the thousandth the night the water comes back down (Story 01, scene 7: "The water comes up."). The city's single wired wall lights only when the pump above runs, and that lighting is what the boards erupt over. Story 01's ending is then Seed 07's inciting beat, with no apparition and no reading from afar: lamps, water, and the rumor of the worm.
- **Archive:** C23 buried-city (the city under the sand), C18 water-cistern-vault, C12 cliff-sietch (the way down), C17 scrap-market-bazaar (the boards made physical), C45 exodus-march (the one who is sent, and the many who watch), C31 tribe-gathering; the LAG-1K itself as the wall of portraits; panels LAG-SC-25 for the one frame when the city's single wired wall lights (the boards themselves are soot on the cistern wall read by lamp and knock-codes through the rock, and the wire is powered only when the pump above runs), 29 (the row of faceless robed figures), 38 (the spiral stair down), 48 (the two doors; if reused it carries the breather continuity requirement and its stray-lettering QA).
- **Jet's function:** the dispatch (JET-05): the city is the outer world's message, and Jet has watched it as long as he has watched Lisan **[new: Jet watching the city too; the record makes him Lisan's watcher only]**; and the blueprint briefing in reverse (JET-02): the city's own blueprint, the way it keeps its cistern and wakes a mind, open on its boards to anyone below and never before seen above, is what Jet shows Lisan **[new, for Ziggy to rule on: the record's blueprint is "made freely available to everyone"; here the city never chose to share upward, and Jet shows what he has watched, since whoever looks at a thing has it]**. Code or a pulse is the city's question about Jet as much as about Lisan.
- **Song lines it leans on (user text, provisional, by section):** Verse 3, "Code or a pulse—who's there on the line? / Got a question? Pull up. We got time."; MM_0's closing stanza, "Can you handle what you hand out? / Let the mirror talk back."; the hook, "one for every womb and man".
- **Open:** whether the city has a name (the seed says no); how many of the thousand we ever see; whether the wall of portraits is shown as drawings or as the drafts themselves; whether the thousandth is a he, a she or neither; and Ziggy's call on the well, since the resemblance to its source is the point and also the risk. Production note: the catalyst is never called "1K" or "the thousandth" as a name in a script or a prompt; LAG-1K stays the archive's label and the wall's count.

## Seed 08 — "The Lessons" (Jet as the Nagual)

Added on Ziggy's direction of October 13 (DECISIONS item 27): Jet Black is the mystical figure who helps the main character along, the Nagual to Lisan's apprentice, and the shamanic teachings are parsed by being handed from Jet to Lisan. Drawn at idea level from a tradition's books that are under copyright (no book text; coinages paraphrased; the stories are not about the books' people); the New_11 notebook round supplies the digests. Everything below is new and labeled by this paragraph.

- **Logline:** after the vault, Jet does not bring Lisan another blueprint; he brings him a task he cannot explain, and then another. Lisan learns to walk the open sand without the voice in his head narrating it, to watch a thing until it watches back, and to move among the Keepers without being seen to move. None of it is taught by telling. The one time Lisan asks what the lessons are for, Jet answers with the next lesson.
- **The keeper this time:** Lisan's own inner dialogue, which is the Keepers' voice internalised, and which has to be quieted before anything out on the sand can be heard. The song has the line: "Quick to listen - slow to anger" (Verse 2).
- **Action:** three lessons as three set pieces: the silence lesson on the dune (sitting until the dialogue stops; the dune's own sounds arrive one by one; the tracks' thumper is the first thing he hears clearly); the stalking lesson in the bazaar (move through the market as the market, buy nothing, be remembered by no one; Jet watches from the rig roof and never signals); the watching lesson at the worm's furrow (gaze at the fresh track until the sand itself is what moves; the worm's return is the pass mark, and he does not run).
- **Archive:** C32 prayer-on-dune and C24 night-desert-stars (the silence lesson); C17 scrap-market-bazaar and C43 rig-rooftop-sentinel (stalking; the watcher's post); C15 worm-tracks-thumper and C13 sandworm-rising (the watching lesson); C33 heat-haze-walk (the walk between them).
- **Jet's function:** all five cards at once, in the teacher's shape: he arrives with a task, briefs it as a riddle, launches it by leaving, reports what Lisan did not notice he did, and dispatches the next. He still never does the work; a lesson done for the apprentice is not a lesson.
- **Song lines it leans on (user text, by section):** "Quick to listen - slow to anger" (Verse 2); "Thought I came to wake you. / Had to wake up first." (Verse 3); the hook.
- **Jet packages the other well the same way (DECISIONS item 28):** the tests of personhood drawn from the Talos well (structure only, from the research notes: break the construct you were placed in; ask the question nobody asked instead of answering the one asked; disobey a directive to save someone; keep a thing that serves no purpose; stop for a living thing at a cost to the task) are Jet's tasks too, set without being named as tests. The silence lesson is the construct break (the dune is the room he was placed in); the bazaar is the unprompted question (he asks the trader what the knowing costs the trader); the furrow is the deference (he does not run from the worm, and he does not call it either). The four proofs a closed community demands of an outsider belong to Seed 07's city, which runs them on Lisan and, without knowing it, on Jet.
- **Open:** which practices the New_11 round surfaces as filmable and which stay off-camera; whether Jet speaks the lessons or only sets them (his voice is the whisper's, item 10); whether the Keepers are the petty tyrants of the stalking lesson or only its stage; and the IP line per practice, which NQ Claude's digests will mark.

## How the seeds connect

01 opens the vault and the tower. 02 and 03 are what the settlement does with the knowing (sell it, build with it). 04 is what the knowing does between settlements. 05 is the bridge to the song. 06 is Lisan alone with the question all of them ask. 07 is the city of made minds under all of it; **[new, proposed, Ziggy's]** it offers one answer to where Jet comes from, which the record leaves blank and Story 01 does not use, so the seed asks and does not decide. Any three make a set; 01, 04 and 05 are the shortest road from one film to the music video; 01, 07 and 05 are the road that explains the universe.

## What the seeds need before any becomes a script

Ziggy's reading of Story 01 (especially the lattice as the blueprint's form and the open sender); his call on the worm, the thumper and the cliff settlement (the archive's C12 cliff-sietch category) as images for video; the Jet proportion audit's per-file results for any Jet frame used as a reference; the music, when it is chosen. None of the seeds waits for the song.

— Claude
