# First Lisan clip — the writer's shot handoff to CFA Nova (2026-10-14)

Author: Claude, lead writer, about 00:55 UTC, at CFA Nova's request in the session on Ziggy's behalf: one first Lisan shot for the existing Flow/Gemini prototype lane, moving from the Flow driving test to footage from the written scenes. Status: a creative handoff; nothing generated; the actual mode, cost and source-intake checks are Nova's; Ziggy's gate is the video. This supplements `PROTOTYPE_BRIEF_C13-04.md`: its fields stand except 2 (the source), 4a (the repaired frame has no sun disc; the key is the haze) and 5 (the maw screen-right, him centred), which this file replaces for the patch-c source, and it tightens the action for a first run. Corrected after a read-only fact check on 2026-10-14 (ten findings applied; the first version is superseded, its hash 424b5c94…). The IP question for the worm beyond this first test is still Ziggy's (DECISIONS open item 8).

## 1. The shot: SW-2, the rise (Story 01 scene 4; the sandworm card; the song's Bridge 1 beat)

The signature image of the world, no mouth, no hand-to-object contact, one action, and the frame Ziggy himself flagged as the storyboard's prime. It stays the right first move.

## 2. The source, resolved: the repaired variant

- **Recommend:** `docs/notes/explorable_world/comfy/references/From Grok/GROK-LAG-1K-C13/C13-sandworm-rising/repairs/C13-04_Z_1_R1-try5-patch-c.jpg`, sha256 `23817577d3d32f0df03d57ac1e49c4c85246e86c405b13c492194f7aa2f52bad`, 447,799 bytes (re-measured 2026-10-14 00:50 UTC). Variant: R1 try5 with the chin patch c (the Chief's repairs NOTES: L4 S5, best; the patch edited only the chin box, everything else is try5).
- **Why, against the drift Nova recorded:** the things that must survive motion are the face's carriers, and patch-c carries all four and fixes the two the raw frame has wrong: segmented worms facing an eye in the disc (the raw has fanged, snake-like worms and an eyeless disc); the legible vertical G-A-I-B, the AL and the blue eyes are present in both frames. The maw's side, the dark shirt under the cloak and the stacked hoops on his left ear are per-frame facts a clip inherits at no cost to the motion test, and the production method already records inherited defects rather than fixing them in the clip. The raw `C13-04_Z_1.jpg` (sha256 `7eafd9ac048dc6d6125dc38281c1b664f7ae0cac1159909c34d90a5e3eef93a3`, 268,027 bytes) stays on file as the reference composition only, as Ziggy's item 25 set.
- **What acceptance costs the record:** the sandworm card's SW-2 sides flip to worm screen-right, so the alternates C13-08 and C13-20, which already put the worm screen-right, match SW-2 and the card's two "flips the worm's side" notes come off, by a card delta; the wardrobe drift is recorded as inherited and the wardrobe is re-locked by the turnaround set LAG-COV-00 before any production clip. I do not recommend waiting for another composition-preserving repair before this clip: R1 took five tries and three patches to get the face right, and a sixth that also keeps the maw's side is not guaranteed.
- **Ziggy's look is still the gate.** His recorded words were "I'm gonna have to see it" of the raw frame (DECISIONS item 18) and, after that look, "go with the repaired variant" (item 25), which is what ordered the repair; nothing he has said on the record covers the delivered patch-c frame. The frame was put in the session on the 13th and at 04:21 UTC he asked to see it beside the original (Personal Nova's ed4878f9, whose own upload failed); both frames are sent to him again with this handoff, and no look of his is recorded yet. If he rejects the drift, the recorded alternative is a further repair that keeps the composition (item 25; Nova's 6a36ba15; the coverage call's anchor note). A motion test from the raw frame with its inherited defects is the writer's alternative proposal only, and would need his word, since item 25 ruled the raw frame out.

## 3. One action, start to end

The worm's maw rises one maw-height behind him at screen-right, its rim lifting through the haze with sand spilling off it, while he holds still for one breath: the chest rises and settles once, eyes on the lens as the brief's field 4 and the card's SW-2 have it, no head turn, no step. Dust lifts at the maw's rim and drifts screen-left on the wind. End state: the maw one height higher and still open; he unchanged.

## 4. Camera and light

- **Camera:** locked, as the still frames it: eye height, medium, normal lens. No push, no drift, no handheld. The slow push is the second variable, for a retry, not this run (one variable per retry).
- **Light:** the anchor's, stated as sources: a high diffuse warm haze, no sun disc; soft near-frontal on his face; the maw's interior dark; the dust catching the haze; no new emitter, no flicker, no whole-frame wash.

## 5. Native short output bound

The route's native short length (Flow 002 returned 6.0 s; the Gemini take LAG-VID-PROOF-01 returned 10.0 s), eight or ten seconds only if the selected model offers it (the brief's field 6), 16:9 as the still, no upscale, no extension, a silent prompt (the score is produced separately per the cue cards). One clip per run; mode and model read on screen; cost verified before Start; no automatic retries.

## 6. Preservation checks (first frame against last, and sampled through)

1. The face carriers constant: the AL between the brows, the vertical G-A-I-B legible, the two segmented worms facing the eye in the disc, blue eyes.
2. No new piercings appear; the hoops stay on the same ear throughout.
3. Wardrobe constant: the dark shirt, the cloak, one chain.
4. The maw stays screen-right and only rises: no lunge, no second worm, no teeth animation beyond the rise.
5. He does not speak, sing or mouth; eyes on the lens throughout; one blink at most; no head turn; no step.
6. No camera move, no cut, no lettering or watermark artifacts, no change of the haze's colour.
7. Returned duration, fps, resolution and whether audio is present recorded (a silent prompt does not make a silent file: Flow 002 returned an audio track despite one); the clip intaken with the source path and hash; the run's mode, model and displayed cost in the record.

## 7. Unresolved creative choices (Ziggy's)

1. Accept patch-c's drift for this prototype (the writer recommends yes), or await a composition-preserving repair (the writer recommends not before this clip).
2. The SW-2 sides delta on the card, which follows from acceptance.
3. The IP question for the worm and the thumper beyond this first test (open item 8).
4. Whether the second clip is the vault's lamps coming up (C18 picks; a light-change shot with no contact, and the cue card's release beat) or the thumper planted (C15-20; hand-to-object contact, which the sandworm card keeps out of a first clip on the method's Flow 002 finding of unnatural body interaction).

## 8. Not in this clip

No breather (none in the frame). No sung mouth, no song timing, no lyric cue; the prompt is silent and the Bridge 1 panels are unaffected. No new characters. No change to the raw frame's storyboard_prime tag. Nothing on the Hon Dolo side.

— Claude

# Card deltas, 2026-10-14 (the posted cards keep their hashes; this file is the record of what changes in them)

Author: Claude, lead writer, about 02:10 UTC. Trigger: Ziggy selected the repaired C13-04 patch-c as the SW-2 source (CFA Nova, in the session at his request, about 02:05 UTC), which the sandworm card's sides were written against the raw frame.

## SCENE_CARD_SANDWORM.md (posted sha256 96a60050148ac10f246d8bcfc59cc607fa8686653776ba03fb04637090d976ed)

- **SW-2 sides:** the worm is now **screen-right**; he is centred and frontal; the sun disc is not in frame and the key is the haze (DECISIONS §4, the repaired row; COVERAGE_CALL_20261013.md LAG-COV-01). The card's "worm screen-left; him screen-right of center; sun upper-left" for SW-2 is superseded for the clip and for any coverage anchored on patch-c.
- **SW-3 (C13-08) and SW-4 (C13-20):** they already put the worm screen-right, so they now match SW-2 and the card's two "flips the worm's side against SW-2" notes come off; they remain alternate angles, never mirrored files.
- **SW-5 (panel LAG-SC-10):** unchanged.
- **The raw C13-04_Z_1.jpg** stays the reference composition on file (DECISIONS item 25); it is no longer the clip's source.
- **Inherited in the clip's source, recorded, not fixed:** the dark shirt under the cloak (the wardrobe lock is re-asserted by LAG-COV-00 before production), the stacked hoops on his left ear with no brow or nostril hoop visible.

## PROTOTYPE_BRIEF_C13-04.md (posted sha256 9da1db98…bdef1)

- Field 2 (source): the repaired patch-c, sha256 23817577d3d32f0df03d57ac1e49c4c85246e86c405b13c492194f7aa2f52bad, 447,799 bytes.

Author: Claude, lead writer, about 01:55 UTC. Source of the request: Ziggy, in the session, showing the frame open in the Visual library (Lisan, outfits, L19 "S3 worm vs harvester") and asking that it be woven into the test as well. Status: a creative handoff for the same Flow/Gemini prototype lane as `FIRST_CLIP_HANDOFF_20261014.md`; nothing generated; mode, cost and intake are Nova's; Ziggy's gate is the video. Viewed by me at full size (1280 by 720) before writing.

## 1. The shot and its story place

**"The signal."** A worm takes a raiders' crawler rig behind him while he stands on the dune with one hand raised, holding the camp back. Not a scene in Story 01; a candidate for Episode 5 "The Rig" (the standoff with the convoy) or Episode 3's chase, proposed, and a story scene study in the record (`grok_500_20261008/asset_ledger.json`, id LAG500-L19-S3, role story_scene_study, localReviewStatus unreviewed). The library's caption calls the rig a harvester of the desert franchise's kind; the handoff calls it the rig, and the worm-and-rig imagery sits under the same video IP question as the worm and the thumper (DECISIONS open item 8), Ziggy's, which this test does not decide.

## 2. The source (raw; no repair exists or is requested)

`docs/notes/explorable_world/comfy/projects/lisan_al_gaib/grok_500_20261008/received/content/LAG-500-MASTER-part03/LAG-L19-fire-trial-armor.zip.contents/LAG-L19-fire-trial-armor/LAG-L19-fire-trial-armor__S3-worm-vs-harvester.jpg`, sha256 `b26aa61a04528cd8c3ef820ccc946e74738db634f29aed018286c138efd8bb09`, 388,976 bytes, 1280 by 720 (ledger and disk agree, re-measured 01:51 UTC). Grok's own QA on intake: an OK-note drift note, breather on, piercings mirrored to his right, kept; a Grok hero candidate, not a user favorite and not an approved reference.

**What I saw at full size (reviewer claude, L4 S5, preliminary):** the AL between the brows; the vertical G-A-I-B legible on the chin; the two segmented worms on the throat facing the sun disc with its eye; pale blue eyes; natural mouth, closed. The breather's tube crosses his RIGHT cheek (viewer-left) into the hair, the lock's side, so the breather is not mirrored. Drift, recorded as inherited and not fixed by the clip: two ear hoops and the brow ring on his RIGHT (the lock's side is his left); the nostril hoop on his left (the lock's side); the outfit is the L19 fire-trial armour with a tan hood, not the stillsuit-and-cloak lock. (The first version of this file read the breather's side backwards; corrected after a read-only fact check on 2026-10-14, which viewed the frame and the lock.) Scene: he is three-quarter to camera at screen-left, his right hand raised palm-out at the frame's left edge; the maw at screen-right closing over a burning rig on wheels; dust everywhere; a warm overcast haze as the key, the fire as a second emitter at screen-right. The face is the strongest part of the frame; the wardrobe is its own look and stays its own look for the test.

## 3. One action, start to end

The maw closes over the rig: the rig tilts and goes under as sand pours off the worm's lip and the fire gutters in the dust; a wave of dust rolls toward camera and thins. He holds: the raised hand stays raised and open, eyes on the lens, the breather in place, no step, no turn; at most the fingers tighten once. End state: the rig gone, the maw closing, the dust settling, he unchanged.

## 4. Camera and light

- **Camera:** locked, as the still frames it: eye height, medium close, normal lens. No push, no handheld. (The push is a retry's variable.)
- **Light, as sources:** the key is the warm overcast haze from above; the fire at screen-right is the second emitter and the one permitted light change: it flickers on the rig, the worm's lip and the dust, and only faintly on his far cheek; the dust catches both. No new source, no whole-frame wash, no colour shift of the haze.

## 5. Native short output bound

The route's native short length (Flow 002 returned 6.0 s; the Gemini take LAG-VID-PROOF-01 returned 10.0 s), eight or ten seconds only if the selected model offers it, 16:9 as the still, no upscale, no extension, a silent prompt (the score is separate). One clip per run; mode and model read on screen; cost verified before Start; no automatic retries.

## 6. Preservation checks (first frame against last, sampled through)

1. The face carriers constant: the AL, the vertical G-A-I-B, the two worms facing the eye in the disc, the blue eyes.
2. The breather stays on the same cheek, one tube, no mirroring, no duplication, no rear connector invented (the known failure mode of this prop).
3. The piercings stay where the still has them; none added.
4. The armour and hood constant; the raised hand stays raised, five fingers, no second hand.
5. The worm only closes over the rig: no second worm, no lunge toward him, no teeth animation beyond the closing; the fire stays on the rig and the dust, never on him.
6. Eyes on the lens; no speech or mouthing; one blink at most; no step; no turn.
7. No camera move, no cut, no lettering or watermark; returned duration, fps, resolution and whether audio is present recorded; the clip intaken with the source path and hash; mode, model and displayed cost in the record.

## 7. Order, and the unresolved choices (Ziggy's)

- **Order:** the rise first (one emitter), the signal second (two emitters), so the second test adds exactly one variable, the fire. If Ziggy wants the signal first, nothing in the handoff changes but the order.
- **Unresolved:** (1) the IP question for worm-and-rig imagery beyond this test (open item 8); (2) whether the mirrored ear hoops and brow ring are acceptable for a prototype (the writer says yes, inherited, as with patch-c); the breather sits on the lock's cheek and needs no acceptance; (3) the story placement (Episode 5 or 3) if the clip lands; (4) whether the fire-trial armour becomes a recorded look of Lisan's or stays a scene study.

## 8. Not in this clip

No sung mouth, no song timing, no lyric cue; no new characters; no change to the ledger's status (unreviewed stays unreviewed until Nova intakes); nothing on the Hon Dolo side.

# Shot direction — the reusable structure for every storyboard shot (2026-10-14)

Author: Claude, lead writer, first saved 02:24 UTC by the clock, on Ziggy's direction relayed by CFA Nova in the session a few minutes before: each storyboard shot carries LIGHTING, CAMERA, CHARACTER DIRECTION and BACKGROUND ACTION, with their coordinated time beats and the resulting video-generation prompt; in his words, "background, rolling, lights, camera, action—we need it all." The writer runs point on the writing. Source lineage, technical settings, actual results and acceptance are carried separately and never merged into the creative sections; a good scene is never promoted into approved performance by the card itself.

## The card, section by section (every section present, "none" written where there is nothing)

0. **SHOT.** Id (SET-SHOT-TAKE), title, story place (episode, scene, card, panel), what the shot is for in one sentence.
1. **SOURCE LINEAGE.** The start frame by exact path, sha256 and bytes; variant and repair history; prior takes by file and hash; what in the frame is lock, what is inherited drift. Never edited after posting; new takes append.
2. **LIGHTING.** Emitters only: the key (what it is, where it is, its colour and softness), the fill (sky, haze, bounce), the rim, every practical (fire, lamp, console, lattice). How each behaves over the shot. No whole-frame washes; no light without a source. Sides stated as the character's and the viewer's, both, every time.
3. **CAMERA.** Height, distance, lens feel, move (locked, push, track, orbit) and when it starts and ends; the line (the axis between the character and what he faces) and which side of it the camera keeps; the frame's edges (what is in, what is off-screen and where).
4. **CHARACTER DIRECTION.** Who, what he does (one action, start to end), eyeline (one target, named as off-screen or in-frame, stated as character-left/right AND viewer-left/right, with up/down), face (brows, eyes, jaw, mouth; the mouth's rule), hands and body (which hand, how far, how fast; what does not move), breath, blinks. Ziggy's acting note verbatim when he gives one, marked as his. The read in one phrase (what the audience should understand), never an emotion label pasted into the prompt.
5. **BACKGROUND ACTION.** Everything that moves that is not him: creatures, vehicles, people, weather, dust, fire, debris, light changes; where each starts and ends; what must not happen (no second creature, no lunge, nothing reaching him).
6. **TIME BEATS.** One table, seconds as story design inside the route's native length, never accepted timing: for each beat, what LIGHTING, CAMERA, CHARACTER and BACKGROUND are doing at once, so that the four sections are coordinated and nothing is asked for that another section forbids.
7. **RESULTING PROMPT.** The copy-ready video-generation prompt, assembled from sections 2 to 6 in plain English: the scene, the character's action and face and eyeline, the background action, the light as sources, the camera, then the negatives. No franchise names, no coinages, no emotion labels, no words the generator over-plays ("dramatic", "epic", "signals", "gestures"); no sung or spoken words unless a card says to-lens and the song timing is accepted.
8. **TECHNICAL SETTINGS** (CFA Nova's; filled at run): route, model, mode, resolution, aspect, length, outputs, credits displayed, project and scene ids, the prompt as actually submitted if it differs from section 7.
9. **ACTUAL RESULTS** (CFA Nova's; filled on return): file, hash, bytes, duration, fps, resolution, whether audio is present and what it is, the frames sheet, the measured defects.
10. **ACCEPTANCE** (separate; Ziggy's gate is never written by the writer): Ziggy's verdict on the video; beneath it, clearly labelled, the writer's attributed preliminary grade (reviewer, date, L and S separate, a performance line: reads or not, which beat failed); nothing in sections 0 to 9 counts as acceptance.

## Rules the structure enforces

- The four creative sections are written together and reconciled in the beats table before the prompt is assembled; the prompt is derived from the card, never the other way round.
- One new variable per take against the prior take of the same shot; the card says which.
- Every side is written twice (character's, viewer's) in sections 2 to 6 so a correction like "up to your right" is never silently inverted; in section 7, the prompt, the approach to try next is directions in frame terms only with a landmark in the frame ("toward the top-left corner, past his raised palm"), a hand's motion as a frame direction with a limit ("a few inches, staying beside his head, never in front of his face"), and the mouth as a state after any source exception is stated exactly (a frame's parted lips close in the first half-second, then closed and still). Hypothesis from one result (LAG-SIGNAL-002, 2026-10-14): the generator may not resolve a character's left and right; untested until a take runs on it.
- The original of any take is preserved; a revision is a new take id beside it.
- The card changes only its own sections 8 to 10 after a run; a creative change is a new take, with the prior take's card kept.

— Claude

Technical settings, actual results and acceptance remain separate. The later frame-landmark prompt approach is explicitly proposed and untested after one returned prototype; it is not an established causal rule. The frame-zero parted-lips exception is preserved.

# Shot direction — LAG-SIGNAL-002, "The signal", take two (2026-10-14)

Author: Claude, lead writer, first saved 02:24 UTC by the clock (earlier stamps in this file were guessed ahead of the clock and are corrected here), in the structure of `SHOT_DIRECTION_TEMPLATE.md`, on Ziggy's direct correction relayed by CFA Nova before take two. This card supersedes `SIGNAL_PERFORMANCE_DELTA_20261014.md` for take two (that file is kept, marked superseded, its eyeline corrected to match). Revised again at 02:32 UTC at CFA Nova's preflight: section 7 carries its own preservation sentence for the face carriers, the mouth line is qualified (parted at frame zero, closed within the first half-second), and the gaze onset in section 4 is reconciled with the beats table (leaves the camera from about the half-second, on the teammates by about a second and a half). Revised at 02:27 UTC after a fact check of the delta: the first take's eyes were toward the camera and a touch off the lens, not on it; the start frame's lips are slightly parted, so the mouth closes in the first half-second rather than being closed throughout; the first second's eye closure is one observed closure, not a verified count. Execution and intake are Nova's. Nothing here is acceptance.

## 0. SHOT

LAG-SIGNAL-002. "The signal", take two. Story place: a scene study (Grok 500 look L19, shot S3), proposed for Episode 5 "The Rig" or Episode 3's chase; not a panel of the song. Purpose: the worm takes a raiders' rig behind him while he turns to his teammates off-screen and tells them, with his face and one open palm, that this is concern: hold, wait.

## 1. SOURCE LINEAGE

- Start frame: `docs/notes/explorable_world/comfy/projects/lisan_al_gaib/grok_500_20261008/received/content/LAG-500-MASTER-part03/LAG-L19-fire-trial-armor.zip.contents/LAG-L19-fire-trial-armor/LAG-L19-fire-trial-armor__S3-worm-vs-harvester.jpg`, sha256 `b26aa61a04528cd8c3ef820ccc946e74738db634f29aed018286c138efd8bb09`, 388,976 bytes, 1280 by 720; raw, no repair.
- Lock in the frame: the AL, the vertical G-A-I-B, the two segmented worms facing the eye in the disc, blue eyes; the breather on his RIGHT cheek (viewer-left), the lock's side. Inherited drift, kept: the lips slightly parted (the lock wants a natural closed mouth; take two closes them in the first half-second); two ear hoops and the brow ring on his right (viewer-left); the nostril hoop on his left (viewer-right); the L19 fire-trial armour and tan hood instead of the suit-and-cloak lock.
- Take one: `flow/signal_prototype_20261013/FLOW-LAG-SIGNAL-001_original.mp4`, sha256 `e6ace86c4ebe59a3fa7c695cb3e1960840e0424a7fc57a7deed984c0417b524a`, 3,635,702 bytes, 8.0 s, 24 fps, 192 frames, audio present near silent; scene 0d53ab12-5bc8-4f1d-bcc9-27834273884e. Take one as measured (Nova's RESULT_TECHNICAL_REVIEW and the frame sheets): the carriers held; the rig gone by about the fifth second; the maw open at the end; the eyes toward the camera and a touch off the lens, as the still has them; the lips slightly parted as in the source; one eye closure around the first second (shut roughly 0.7 to 1.3 s), whether the take's only blink awaiting playback; the hand raised and open throughout. Ziggy's review: the scene came off really well; Lisan is only standing there. Preserved.
- The one new variable in take two: the performance (sections 4 and 6). Light, camera and background are take one's, including the fire, which flickers as it did in take one and gutters as the rig goes under; no timed flare is added (a fact check caught an earlier wording that would have made the fire a second variable).

## 2. LIGHTING

- Key: a warm overcast desert haze from above, soft, no sun disc; it does not move or change colour.
- Fill: the haze itself and the pale sand bounce from below, on his face and the armour's plates.
- Rim: none from the sky; the fire gives a faint warm edge on his far side only (his left, viewer-right) when it flickers.
- Practical: the fire on the rig at screen-right (viewer-right; behind him on his left side). As in take one it flickers on the rig, the worm's lip and the dust, gutters as the rig goes under, and is embers and lit dust by the end; only faintly his far cheek when it flickers; never his near side, never a new source.
- Dust catches both the haze and the fire; no whole-frame wash.

## 3. CAMERA

Locked for the whole take: eye height, medium close, normal lens, 16:9 as the still. No push, no drift, no handheld. The line runs from him to the off-screen teammates up to his right (viewer-left, above the frame's left edge); the camera stays in front of him, on the maw's side of that line: the maw is behind him at screen-right (viewer-right, his left), the teammates off-screen up and to his right (viewer-left). Edges: his raised right hand at the frame's left edge, the maw and the rig at the right, sky above, sand below.

## 4. CHARACTER DIRECTION

- **Ziggy's acting note, verbatim (relayed by CFA Nova, 2026-10-14):** "Look over off-screen, UP TO YOUR RIGHT, and indicate to your teammates that it's concern."
- **Who:** Lisan, three-quarter to camera at screen-left, his right hand already raised palm-out at the frame's left edge; the breather on.
- **Eyeline (one target):** from about the half-second his eyes leave the camera (they are toward it in the still, a touch off the lens) and by about the first second and a half they are UP and to HIS RIGHT, which is VIEWER-LEFT, off-screen above the frame's left edge, past and above his raised hand, where his teammates stand on the higher dune behind the camera's left shoulder. The chin lifts a little; the head turns toward them by a few degrees; the shoulders stay square. The eyes stay on that one target for the whole take: no wander, no glance back at the worm, no return to the lens.
- **Face, the read is concern:** brows draw down and together; the eyes open a fraction wider as they find the teammates, then narrow a touch against the dust; the jaw sets; the lips, slightly parted in the start frame, press closed within the first half-second and stay closed. One hard breath through the nose as the rig goes under (the nostrils flare once); the breather's clip does not move. No words, no mouthing, no teeth.
- **Hands and body:** the raised right hand (viewer-left) is already a hold. Two small pushes of the open palm toward the teammates, up and to his right, each no more than a hand's width out and back: the first as the maw begins to close, the second smaller and sharper as the rig goes under; between and after, the hand open and still, five fingers spread, the forearm where it was. No fist, no wave, no pointing; the left hand stays out of frame; no step; no body turn.
- **Blinks:** one at most.
- **Mouth rule:** closes in the first half-second and stays closed; this is not a to-lens or sung shot.

## 5. BACKGROUND ACTION

The worm's maw at screen-right closes over the burning rig: the rig tilts (first to third second), the fire flares on it, sand pours off the worm's lip, the rig goes under (about the fifth second), a wave of dust rolls toward camera and thins (sixth to eighth second), the maw settles and may remain open at the end as in take one. Nothing else moves but dust and embers. Not allowed: a second worm, the maw turning toward him, anything reaching him, the fire spreading to him, people entering the frame.

## 6. TIME BEATS (story design inside 8 s at 24 fps; not accepted timing)

| Beat (s) | LIGHTING | CAMERA | CHARACTER | BACKGROUND |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.0 to 0.5 | haze key; fire steady on the rig | locked | the start frame; eyes toward the camera as the still has them; the lips press closed | the maw open behind the rig |
| 0.5 to 1.5 | fire flickers on the rig as in take one | locked | eyes go up and to his right (viewer-left), off-screen; chin lifts; brows draw | the rig tilts |
| 1.5 to 2.5 | fire flickers; faint warm edge on his far (left, viewer-right) cheek | locked | first small palm push toward the teammates as the maw begins to close, then hold | the maw begins to close; sand pours off the lip |
| 2.5 to 5.0 | fire flickers, then starts to gutter | locked | holds the look; jaw set; eyes narrow against the dust | the maw closes over the rig; dust rises |
| 5.0 to 5.5 | fire gutters | locked | second, sharper push; the hard breath through the nose | the rig goes under |
| 5.5 to 8.0 | embers and lit dust; haze unchanged | locked | hand open and still; the look held up and to his right (viewer-left); no return to the lens | the dust wave rolls toward camera and thins; the maw settles, open |

## 7. RESULTING PROMPT (copy-ready; Nova may trim for the route's limit without changing a side)

```text
Start from the provided frame exactly: a young man with dark curls, three-quarter to camera at the left of frame, wearing dark plated armour with a tan hood, a thin black breather tube across his right cheek, his right hand raised palm-out at the frame's left edge; behind him at the right of frame a giant sandworm's open maw closes over a burning wheeled rig in a desert of warm overcast haze.

Preserve his face exactly as in the frame for the whole shot: the same face geometry and dark curls, the pale blue eyes, the small "AL" mark between the brows, the vertical letters G-A-I-B down the chin, the two segmented worm tattoos on the throat facing each other, and the sun disc with an eye between them at the base of the throat; the breather tube on the right cheek, the ear hoops, brow ring and nostril hoop where they are.

His performance: from about the half-second his eyes leave the camera and look up and to his own right, off-screen above the left edge of the frame, toward companions on higher ground behind the camera; they are on them by about a second and a half and stay there for the rest of the shot. His chin lifts slightly and his head turns a few degrees toward them; his shoulders do not move. His brows draw down and together, his eyes widen a fraction then narrow against the dust, his jaw sets; his lips, slightly parted in the first frame, press closed within the first half-second and stay closed; he does not speak. His raised right hand pushes forward twice toward those companions, small, open-palmed, a hand's width each time: once as the maw begins to close, once sharper as the rig goes under, with one hard breath through the nose; otherwise the hand stays open and still with five fingers spread. He does not step, turn his body, or lower the hand.

Background: the maw closes over the rig; the rig tilts, the fire on it flickers then gutters, sand pours off the worm's lip, the rig goes under, and a wave of dust rolls toward the camera and thins; the maw settles and may remain open. Nothing else moves but dust and embers.

Light: a soft warm overcast haze from above as the only key, no sun; the fire on the rig is the only other light, flickering as before and guttering as the rig goes under, lighting the rig, the worm's lip and the dust and only faintly the far side of his face.

Camera: locked, eye height, medium close, normal lens, no movement.

Do not: add a second worm or any creature movement toward him; add other people in frame; add a second hand; show teeth, or let the mouth open after it closes in the first half-second (the first frame's slightly parted lips close and stay closed, no teeth, no speech); move the camera; change the clothing, the breather or the jewelry; add lettering or watermark; add music or voice.
```

## 8. TECHNICAL SETTINGS (CFA Nova's; filled at run)

Route, model, mode, resolution, aspect, length, outputs, credits displayed, project and scene ids, the submitted prompt if it differs from section 7. (Take one was Flow, Omni 1.1 Flash, frames mode with the start frame only, 720p, 16:9, 8 s, one output.)

## 9. ACTUAL RESULTS (CFA Nova's; filled on return)

File, hash, bytes, duration, fps, resolution, audio present and what it is, the frames sheet (first, middle, last, and the two push beats), the measured defects.

## 10. ACCEPTANCE (separate)

Ziggy's gate: the video (never written by the writer). Beneath it, labelled: the writer's preliminary grade on return from the frames (reviewer claude; date; L and S separate; performance: reads or not, which beat failed). Take one's grade from frames, reviewer claude, 2026-10-14 02:19 UTC: L4 S5, performance static. Take two's grade from frames, reviewer claude, 2026-10-14 02:55 UTC: L4 S5, performance does not read as directed (eyeline inverted to viewer-right at 0.5 to 1.5 s; both pushes toward the camera and across the face; the look lost and the mouth reopened from about 4 s); the face's concern read; details and a proposed take-three delta in SIGNAL_002_ASSESSMENT_20261014.md. Nova's technical settings and actual results for take two are in take_002/PREFLIGHT_AND_SUBMISSION_RECEIPT.json and RESULT_INTAKE.json. Nothing in sections 0 to 9 is acceptance; a good scene is not an approved performance.

— Claude

# "The signal" — performance delta for one revised take (2026-10-14)

**SUPERSEDED for take two at 02:24 UTC (by the clock; earlier stamps here were guessed ahead) by `SHOT_DIRECTION_SIGNAL_002_20261014.md`, on Ziggy's direct correction relayed by CFA Nova: the eyeline is UP and to the CHARACTER'S RIGHT (viewer-left in this setup), not below eye level, and the read is concern (his words: "Look over off-screen, UP TO YOUR RIGHT, and indicate to your teammates that it's concern."). The eyeline lines below are corrected to match; everything else in this file stands as the first statement of the delta. A later fact check (02:27 UTC) found three baseline slips carried into the card and corrected there: the first take's eyes were toward the camera and a touch off the lens, not on it; the start frame's lips are slightly parted, so the mouth closes within the first half-second rather than being closed throughout; the first second's eye closure is one observed closure, not a verified count.**

Author: Claude, lead writer, about 02:25 UTC, at CFA Nova's request in the session on Ziggy's review of the first take. Ziggy, in substance: the scene came off really well, but Lisan is only standing there; if the intention is "wait, wait, hold on, not yet" to someone off-screen, he needs to say it with his face and with proper motion. Nova's own reading: the first brief over-constrained the performance (hold, no turn, no gesture). Status: a bounded delta for ONE revised take; the original `FLOW-LAG-SIGNAL-001_original.mp4` (sha256 e6ace86c4ebe59a3fa7c695cb3e1960840e0424a7fc57a7deed984c0417b524a, 3,635,702 bytes) is preserved and untouched; execution and intake are Nova's; nothing accepted; no song-sync claim.

## 0. What the first take did (from the sampled frames, `flow/signal_prototype_20261013/result_review/SOURCE_AND_SAMPLED_FRAMES.png`, sha256 efcf554d…3b0ff)

The face carriers held through all eight seconds (the AL, the chin lettering, the worms and the eye-disc, the blue eyes, the breather on his right cheek, the hoops); the maw closed over the rig and the rig was gone by about the fifth second; the maw stayed open at the end at screen-right; dust rolled through; one blink at the first second; the hand stayed raised and open; the eyes stayed on the lens. Reviewer claude, from frames: likeness as the still (L4), scene S5, performance static, which is what the brief asked for and what Ziggy now wants changed. The audio track is present but near silent (mean -91 dBFS).

## 1. What stays exactly as in the first take

The L19 start frame by the same path and hash; the locked camera, eye height, medium close, no push; the worm and rig action (the maw closes over the rig, the rig goes under by about the fifth second, the maw may remain open at the end); the fire-trial armour and hood; the breather on his right cheek, one tube, unmoved; the hoops and brow ring as the frame has them; the local fire at screen-right as the only second emitter; 8 seconds native, 16:9, 720p, one output, a silent prompt, the returned audio recorded; one run.

## 2. The one change: the performance, in three parts

**(a) One purposeful off-screen eyeline.** In the first half-second his eyes leave the lens and go to one point off-screen: UP and to HIS RIGHT (viewer-left), past and above his raised hand, where his teammates stand on the higher dune behind the camera's left shoulder (corrected per Ziggy; the first version said below eye level). The head turns toward it by a few degrees at most; the shoulders do not turn. The eyes stay on that one point for the whole take: no wander, no glance at the worm, no return to the lens.

**(b) Facial tension that reads as "not yet."** The brows draw down and together; the eyes narrow a touch against the dust; the jaw sets; the lips press closed and stay closed. One hard breath through the nose as the rig goes under (the nostrils flare once); the breather's clip does not move. No words, no mouthing, no parted lips, no teeth.

**(c) A restrained hold-and-wait palm cue.** The raised right hand is already a "hold" in the first frame. Two small pushes of the open palm toward the off-screen people, each no more than a hand's width forward and back: the first as the maw begins to close (about the second second), the second, smaller and sharper, as the rig goes under (about the fifth second). Between and after them the hand stays open and still, five fingers spread, the forearm where it was. No fist, no wave, no pointing, no second hand entering the frame.

Timings are story design inside the eight seconds, not accepted timing; the two pushes and the breath are the beats, not the clock.

## 3. What is still forbidden

No step; no body turn; no second figure; no lip-sync, voice or spoken line; no new light source and no change to the fire's place; no camera move; no change to the worm's action beyond the first take's; no change to wardrobe, jewelry or breather.

## 4. Prompt guidance for Nova's wording (plain English, the only performance words)

Say what he is doing and to whom: he is looking up to his own right at teammates out of frame, telling them with his face and one open palm that this is concern, hold, wait, while the worm takes the rig behind him; his eyes stay on them; his mouth stays closed; the hand pushes forward twice, small, and holds. Avoid words the generator over-plays ("signals," "gestures," "shouts," "dramatic"); do not name an emotion as a label; describe the brows, the jaw, the palm and the eyeline.

## 5. Checks on return (the handoff's seven, plus the performance)

1. The face carriers constant first frame to last (the AL, the chin lettering, the two worms facing the eye in the disc, the blue eyes).
2. The breather on the same cheek, one tube, clip unmoved; the hoops and brow ring where the still has them; nothing added.
3. The armour and hood constant; the raised hand five fingers, open; no second hand.
4. The worm only closes over the rig; no second worm; no lunge; the fire stays on the rig and the dust.
5. **The eyeline on one off-screen point**, up and to his right (viewer-left), for the whole take; no return to the lens; no look at the worm.
6. **The mouth closed throughout**; no teeth; one blink at most.
7. **The two palm pushes small and forward**, then the hand still; the head turn small; the shoulders square.
8. No camera move, no cut, no lettering; duration, fps, resolution and whether audio is present recorded; the take intaken beside the original as a second take, never replacing it.

## 6. The writer's read on return

Nova extracts first, middle, last and the two push beats; I grade from those against the eight checks (reviewer claude, L and S separate, and a third line for the performance: read or not read, with the beat that failed if any). Ziggy's gate is the video.

— Claude

# LAG-SIGNAL-002, take two — the writer's attributed preliminary assessment, and a proposed delta for a take three (2026-10-14)

Reviewer: Claude, lead writer, 2026-10-14 02:55 UTC by the clock, from CFA Nova's frame sheets, not from playback (no video viewing here); qualified at 03:00 UTC on Nova's three points (the rig's timing in take two; the diagnosis as a hypothesis; the source's parted-lips exception kept in any mouth-as-state wording). Status: preliminary; likeness and scene are the writer's attributed aesthetic judgment, the performance read is against the card; technical checks and human acceptance stay separate; nothing accepted; no third take requested or implied; the delta in §4 is a writer's proposal only. Ziggy's gate is the video.

## 1. What was reviewed

- Take two: `flow/signal_prototype_20261013/take_002/FLOW-LAG-SIGNAL-002_original.mp4`, sha256 `38ff31d1e9de551509112e35eacad8b96804a6e3b65811fe2992b0f4d00f6e6c`, 4,310,690 bytes; 1280 by 720, 24 fps, 192 frames, 8.0 s; audio present and substantial (mean -15.6 dBFS, peak 0 dBFS), contents not auditioned. Scene 25ca7370-c0f5-4630-96a4-1d3f568bca70. Run: Flow, Omni 1.1 Flash, frames mode with the start frame only, 720p, 16:9, 8 s, one output, 12 credits displayed; the submitted prompt was the card's section 7 with Nova's native-settings prefix (ACTUAL_SUBMITTED_PROMPT.txt, sha256 b725c3f1…); the card frozen at submission is the final aa04a82c… version.
- Frames: `take_002/result_review/SOURCE_AND_BEAT_FRAMES.png` (sha256 aa9286ad…bb0b; frames 0, 24, 36, 48, 60, 96, 120, 132, 191) and `TAKE_ONE_AND_TWO_MATCHED_FRAMES.png` (sha256 2b9de466…ea74d; takes one and two at 0, 48, 96, 120, 191). Both viewed at full size.

## 2. Grades (reviewer claude; preliminary)

- **Likeness: L4.** The carriers hold in every sampled frame: the AL, the vertical G-A-I-B, the two segmented worms facing the eye in the disc, the blue eyes, the breather on his right cheek (viewer-left), the hoops and brow ring where the still has them; the armour and hood constant; no new piercings; the hand is his right throughout, five fingers. The same L4 as the still (the inherited drift is the still's, not the take's).
- **Scene: S5** (an attributed aesthetic judgment). The maw closes over the rig; rig structure and fire are still visible inside the dust at 5.5 s (frame 132) and the rig is gone by the last sample (frame 191, 7.958 s), so the beat at which it goes under is somewhere between and is not established from these samples (take one's "gone by the fifth second" does not transfer); the dust wave rolls and thins; the maw settles open at the end; the fire flickers and gutters as in take one; no second worm, nothing reaches him; the haze key constant; the locked frame held. As a scene it is as good as take one and more alive.
- **Performance: does not read as directed.** What read: the face. From the first to the second second the brows draw down and together, the eyes narrow, the jaw sets, and concern is legible; the mouth closes as asked in the first half-second. What failed, by beat:
  1. **0.5 to 1.5 s, the eyeline, inverted.** The head and gaze go to VIEWER-RIGHT (his left, the maw's side), the opposite of the directed up and to his right (viewer-left). He is looking toward the worm, not the teammates.
  2. **1.5 to 2.5 s, the first push, wrong direction and too big.** The hand leaves the frame's left edge and comes toward the camera, crossing in front of his face by 2.5 s; the card asked for a hand's-width push toward the teammates, away from the camera, the hand staying where it was. At 2.5 s the eyes are shut (a blink or a flinch at the hand).
  3. **About 4.0 s, the look is lost.** The gaze returns source-like toward the camera and the mouth has reopened; the card asked for the look held on the teammates and the mouth closed for the rest of the take.
  4. **5.0 to 5.5 s, the second push, again at the camera.** The open hand is up in front of the face toward the lens, fingers spread; the mouth open; at 5.5 s the eyes roll up rather than hold a target.
  5. **5.5 to 8.0 s, no held target.** The last frame has the eyes toward the camera and the mouth slightly open, the hand back at the edge.
- **Against take one:** take one was static and correct; take two is active and wrong-sided. The one new variable produced motion. **Hypothesis, not a finding:** the result is consistent with the generator resolving "his own right" as frame-right, "pushes forward" as toward the camera, and "the lips press closed" as a mouth action to keep performing; one result does not prove how the words were interpreted.

## 3. The next approach for the structure (proposed; untested)

In the card, sides stay written as the character's and the viewer's. **In the prompt, the next approach to try is directions in frame terms only, with a landmark in the frame**: "toward the top-left corner of the frame, past his raised palm", never "his right" or "his left"; a hand's motion as a direction in the frame with a limit ("a few inches toward the top-left corner, staying beside his head, never in front of his face"); and the mouth as a state after the first half-second, keeping the source's exact exception (the lips are slightly parted at frame zero and close during the first half-second; from then on, closed and still). This is an untested approach drawn from one result and the hypothesis above; whether it works is what a take three would test.

## 4. Proposed delta for a take three (writer's proposal only; not a request; no run implied)

Everything of the aa04a82c… card stands except the prompt's performance paragraph and the negatives, which would read:

```text
His performance: within the first second his eyes leave the camera and look up toward the top-left corner of the frame, past and above his raised palm, at companions who are out of frame up there; the eyes stay fixed on that top-left point for the rest of the shot and never return to the camera or turn toward the worm. His chin lifts slightly and his head turns a few degrees toward that top-left point; his shoulders do not move. His brows draw down and together, his eyes narrow against the dust, his jaw sets. His lips, slightly parted in the first frame, close during the first half-second; from then on the mouth stays closed and the lips still, no speech. His raised right hand stays beside his head at the left edge of the frame and gives two small pushes of the open palm toward that same top-left point, away from the camera, a few inches each: one as the maw begins to close, one sharper as the rig goes under; the hand never comes toward the camera and never passes in front of his face; otherwise it stays open and still, five fingers spread. He does not step, turn his body, or lower the hand.

Do not: add a second worm or any creature movement toward him; add other people in frame; add a second hand; move the hand toward the camera or in front of his face; open the mouth or move the lips after it closes in the first half-second; look toward the camera or toward the worm after the first second; move the camera; change the clothing, the breather or the jewelry; add lettering or watermark; add music, voice or any sound.
```

The character-side statement (up and to HIS RIGHT, viewer-left) stays in the card's sections 3, 4 and 6 for the record; it leaves the prompt. One new variable against take two: the prompt's wording of the same direction, as an untested approach. Whether a take three runs is Ziggy's and Nova's call; none is executed by this note; the audio question (a substantial track despite the silence prefix) is Nova's lane and is noted, not diagnosed, here.

— Claude

assets.text:
# Character note — James, Lisan Al Gaib's brother (continuity, 2026-10-14)

Author: Claude, lead writer, recorded at about 03:53 UTC by the clock; six small corrections from a read-only fact check applied at about 04:00 UTC (the sleeved right arm; the preservation list attributed to the relay, not the record; the Keepers' fear not in Story 01; the raising as the Angels note's proposal; the sign never required of a Panhandler; the stamp). Source: Ziggy's direct decision relayed by Site Index and carried to the session by CFA Nova, with the adoption record `cast/james/adoption_20261014/ADOPTION_RECORD_396fad0e-c0e0-4987-819e-4a808700b1ba.json` (sha256 `9e0543d7d8541730ec0a7a2c42086f8eaacb8e7df8f713f3ef1ccb9d00dfe6ff`, 2,486 bytes; verified on disk). Status: the facts in §1 are canon by that record; everything in §3 onward is the writer's continuity, labeled **[proposed]**, for Ziggy's reading; backstory beyond the relationship is his to direct. No image is requested by this note; the gun-removal derivative is already with Grok and its return and acceptance are pending.

## 1. Canon, from the adoption record

- **Character:** LAG-CAST-JAMES, display name James. **Relationship:** brother of Lisan Al Gaib. Target project: Lisan.
- **The look:** the exact pictured man in `HD-RETURN-957897bd45c4`, the Hon Dolo return `grok_return_20261009/received/content/957897bd45c4__HIP-COAT-01_v001.jpg` (sha256 `957897bd45c4fc03d685c4a40af7670385ab3970108cdbd319d839385dceacc1`, 306,212 bytes, 1280 by 720), referenced in place; the one derivative requested is gun removal only (the record); CFA Nova's relay adds Grok's acknowledgement that it preserves the exact character, tattoos, coat, jewelry, pose, setting and holster. Derivative acceptance needs Ziggy's review on return (repair request 2d33fb25).
- **Lineage rule:** a cross-project lineage. The original stays Hon Dolo's asset with its Hon review intact ("verified received candidate; not approved" as a Dolo outfit; the ledger's note that the chest tattoo reads as a compass or mandala, not the twin-tower ship, is Hon's finding and stays Hon's). James is a Lisan character; nothing of Hon Dolo's story comes with the picture.
- **Unknowns the record lists:** age, backstory beyond the relationship, powers, future wardrobe, the derivative's generation method and actual preservation. The adoption scope is "this exact character and visible look; no invented age, powers or backstory."

## 2. The man, as seen at full size (reviewer claude; a description, not a grade)

Tight dark curls; a wide open smile with natural teeth; gold hoop earrings in both ears; two gold chains; small tattoos on the cheek under the eye and script on the neck; a black leather overcoat worn open over a bare chest carrying a large compass-like mandala; lettering and figures on the stomach, the left forearm (viewer-right) and the back of the left hand, the right arm sleeved to the hip; black trousers, a wide belt, an ornately tooled holster on his left hip (viewer-right) with a revolver in it, to be removed; standing square to camera in a hangar with a ramp and a lit ship's mouth behind him, steam on a wet floor. **What he does not carry:** the AL, the chin lettering, the throat worms and the eye-disc, the blue eyes, the breather. He is unmistakably not Lisan, and that is the point of him.

## 3. What a brother does to the continuity **[proposed]**

- **The sign skipped him.** Story 01 makes Lisan's marks "the dead sign," his mother's, the sign the Keepers name and the line parts for. James has none. The simplest continuity, and the richest: two sons of the same mother, and the sign came down to one of them. James is the brother who was spared it, or passed over by it, and which of those he believes is his whole character.
- **The smile is his.** Lisan is the one who holds still. James is the one who grins in a hangar with a ship behind him: the brother who left, or the brother who trades, who moves between settlements and the city under the cliff and the raiders' market (Seed 02's bazaar sells knowing by the cup; Seed 03's rig is built from a wreck graveyard; Episode 5's convoy has a standoff). The picture's setting, a hangar and a ship, says he goes where the ships are. **[proposed; the setting is Hon Dolo's hangar in the source and is not Lisan canon; what it suggests is a brother with reach.]**
- **Angels and Sassy raised both, or one.** The Angels and Sassy note proposes, not yet with Ziggy's word, that they raised Lisan after the mother died. Either they raised James too and he left (the son who would not stay for the water line), or James was already gone when she died and comes back when the lamps are seen from far off. The second gives Story 01's tower a second reader: the light that blinks back from the dunes is answered later by the brother who saw the lamps from the ships. **[proposed; two options for Ziggy, not a decision.]**
- **The Panhandlers and the Fall.** James does the shadow work or he does not; if he does, he is a Panhandler of the mother's own line without the sign, which tests whether the sign runs in the blood or lands where it chooses (unmarked Panhandlers already exist: Sassy, the child, the thousandth); if he does not, he is Angels' ally in doubt with a younger face. In the Fall branch (Episode 4's voice, Episode 8's devil with Lisan's eyes), the brother is the one who would see it first, because he knew the boy before the name. **[proposed]**
- **Time.** In the forty-year loop, the brother is the one who can be at both ends without a mirror: the same man at two ages, which the time well's shape (Seed 09, TIME_AND_THE_FALL) already asks for in the people at the fire. A grown James at the tower's reply is the loop's cleanest proof. **[proposed; and it depends on the age Ziggy gives him.]**
- **What stays separate:** the gun. The derivative removes it, and the writer keeps it removed in every scene: James does not carry a weapon in the Lisan world unless Ziggy says so; the holster stays as a thing he wears empty, which is a story in itself.

## 4. Where he enters, episode by episode **[proposed]**

| Ep | James | The beat |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 The Gloved Hand | Not in the settlement; named once at the fire when Sassy counts who is missing. | The empty place. |
| 3 The Cup | The brother in the bazaar, among the traders of knowing by the cup; he knows Lisan's face before Lisan knows the market. | The first meeting as grown men. |
| 5 The Rig | He rides with the convoy or builds against it; the holster empty either way. | The standoff with a brother on the other side, or the same side. Ziggy's. |
| 7 The Answer | He is at the far end of the forty years, grey in the curls, at the relay. | The loop's proof in one face. |
| 9 The Thousandth | He teaches the thousandth what the sign does not: how to be unmarked and still belong. | The brother's lesson. |

## 5. Open for Ziggy

1. James's age against Lisan's: older or younger, and by how much.
2. Whether Angels and Sassy raised him too, or he was already gone.
3. Whether he is a Panhandler, outside them, or the test of whether the sign is needed.
4. Which side of the convoy he rides in Episode 5.
5. Whether the empty holster stays as his mark, and whether he ever carries anything in it.

## 6. What this note does not do

It does not change the Hon Dolo asset, its review or its album; it does not request any image beyond the gun-removal derivative already with Grok; it does not give James age, powers or backstory as canon; it does not edit the posted Angels and Sassy note, Story 01, the seeds or the plan (their next revisions carry the brother); it does not place James in any coverage set or shot card until Ziggy has read this and the derivative is accepted.

— Claude

# Story 01 "The Gloved Hand" — storyboard skeleton in the shot-card structure (2026-10-14)

Author: Claude, lead writer, recorded at about 12:50 UTC by the clock, on Ziggy's direction of 12:35 UTC (item 61): storyboards worked out now as the preparation for the video push; video stays short-story scale; character development by images meanwhile. Status: a skeleton, **[proposed]** throughout; one line per shot with the four creative sections in brief; full cards (`SHOT_DIRECTION_TEMPLATE.md`, eleven sections, beats table, prompt) are written per shot only when a shot is chosen to run. Sources: `STORY_01_JET_BLACK_INTRODUCTION.md` (the nine scenes and the scene list), `SCENE_CARD_SANDWORM.md`, `COVERAGE_CALL_20261013.md`, `LAG1K_STORY_MAP.md`, the character notes (Angels, Sassy, James), `TIME_AND_THE_FALL_20261013.md`, `LESSON_DIAGRAM_20261013.md`. Nothing generates; no character without an accepted reference enters a run (Angels, Sassy, James-with-ink, the Keepers, the child and Jet all wait on the character-development pass and Ziggy's acceptance); Lisan's shots run from the LAG-1K and the repaired frames already on disk. **Revision 2 (12:56 UTC):** one read-only check against Story 01, the cards, the story map, the coverage call and the record returned ten findings; each was verified against the story text and applied: the count; 4.3's rear-view side; the burst and the surfacing added as 4.4; the valve added as 7.4; the oldest Keeper's understanding added as 7.10; Lisan's ration (a third, not the child's half); 1.2's lamp side; scene 5 moved between the furrows with Jet's one walk; the lattice's colour left unrecorded; Jet's bare right hand opening the cube and the two held dialogue beats of scenes 4 and 5. The check's eight passes (scene order and quoted lines, sides elsewhere, every folder and pick on disk, the Flow return and items 52 to 61, the cue references, every pending mark, the one to-lens shot) are in the check output.

Conventions: shot ids `S01-<scene>.<shot>`; sides written as the character's (viewer's); light as sources; "L" = Lisan; the first clip already on disk is marked; the two score-song set pieces are marked. Counts: 9 scenes, 38 shots (counted by id).

## Scene 1 — The vault (C18 water-cistern-vault; the Keepers; the line)
- **S01-1.1 WIDE.** The vault from the ladder's foot: the pump under dim lamps at screen-right (the practical key), the line of people from screen-left, three Keepers between. Camera locked, eye height, wide. Background: the pump's slow stroke; the line shuffles. Nobody looks at the lens. Sources: C18 picks 14, 18, 19, 20, 22 (setting); no Keeper reference yet.
- **S01-1.2 MED.** L in the line, hood down, the cup in his hand; the marks on his throat in lamp light from his left (viewer-right; the pump's lamps at screen-right as in 1.1, the hero side kept). Angels behind him takes the swallow for the old (Angels pending). One action: L lifts the cup, drinks the third (a man's ration; the half is a child's). Sources: face lock; C18.
- **S01-1.3 CU, two-shot.** The oldest Keeper filling the next cup as L asks why the pump gives less; the Keeper's eyes on the cup, never on L. "The knowing is ours." (no lip-sync in the test: the line is off-camera or the shot ends before it). Sources: C18; Keeper pending.

## Scene 2 — The rack (C12 cliff-sietch, night)
- **S01-2.1 WIDE, night.** The cliff face, ladders, shuttered openings; one lit window; the rack at the lowest ladder's foot. Moonlight as the key from above-left (viewer-left), cold; a window's warm practical. Camera locked, low. Background: wind, a shutter moving. Sources: C12 category.
- **S01-2.2 INS.** Hands take a thumper from the rack: the iron, the spring hammer. Angels' hand on the rail beside (pending), not stopping him. Light: the window practical rakes across the iron. One action: lift. Sources: a thumper rack is a new request (the scene list says so).
- **S01-2.3 CU.** L fits the breather under his nostrils, one tube across his right cheek (viewer-left) into the hair; eyes down on the work; no look at the lens. Then he turns to the ladder. Sources: face lock; breather decision v3.

## Scene 3 — The tracks (C15 worm-tracks-thumper)
- **S01-3.1 WIDE HIGH.** Dawn haze; tracks converging from the horizon on one small figure; the thumper planted; the camera high and locked, looking down the tracks. Light: the high hazy sun behind the camera. Sources: C15-20, C15-16, 07, 09, 14.
- **S01-3.2 MED.** L drives the thumper into the sand, both hands on the iron, the chain's glint, eyes on the sand (hand-to-object contact: not a first test; a later run). Sources: C15-20_Z_5 (L3 S5).
- **S01-3.3 INS.** The hammer's first strike; sand jumps; the knock is the scene's own sound (the cue card's rule). Sources: C15 inserts.

## Scene 4 — The rise (C13 sandworm-rising; the first clip's world; score song MD-LAG-SW-001)
- **S01-4.1 MED (ON DISK: FLOW-LAG-SW2 from patch-c).** The maw rises one maw-height behind him at screen-right (over his left shoulder); he holds, one breath, eyes on the lens (the one to-lens shot of the film, by the card). Light: the haze key, no sun disc. Sources: `C13-04_Z_1_R1-try5-patch-c.jpg`; the Flow return on disk; Gemini pending.
- **S01-4.2 WIDE LOW.** From the sand, his full body small at screen-left, the maw huge at screen-right, the tracks converging (coverage set LAG-COV-01 slot 3). Sources: C13 alternates.
- **S01-4.3 3QBR.** Camera behind him: over his right shoulder (viewer-right; the rear view flips the sides) to the maw at screen-right; his back half-lit; the maw's face in the key (LAG-COV-01 slot 2). Sources: LAG-COV-01 when generated.
- **S01-4.4 LOW.** The sand takes the frame; when it clears he is coming up out of it, spitting grit, the furrow fresh beside him, the thumper gone (panel LAG-SC-10's burst; card SW-5; cue event 5; body-to-sand contact: a later run, not a first test). Light: the haze key through the settling sand. Sources: LAG-SC-10; C13 alternates.
- **S01-4.5 WIDE, the dune.** On the dune behind him stands a man who was not there: Jet, small, the sphere catching the haze, both hands at his sides, the cube turning by the gloved left hand (viewer-right when he faces the lens). The cue's tail (held reveal, never a fade). Dialogue beat held, not synced: "You watched." / "That is what I am for." Sources: Jet per REF-02 (new request; the arrival composition 048b71751cb2 as inspiration only).

## Scene 5 — The meeting (open desert; the lattice)
- **S01-5.1 TWO-SHOT WIDE.** Between the furrows below the dune: Jet has come down the way a man walks, no faster (his one walk in the film), and stopped a stranger's distance from L; he comes no closer; the cube floats by the gloved left hand (viewer-right). Light: the haze; the cube's cyan edges the only practical. Camera locked, eye height. Sources: new Jet frames; composition ccd25e07763a as inspiration only.
- **S01-5.2 INS.** Jet's bare right hand (viewer-left when he faces the lens) rises and the cube unfolds into the lattice of light above the sand between them (the proposed form of the blueprint); the gloved left stays at his side; L's face lit from above by it; Jet's sphere reflecting it. Dialogue beat held, not synced: "I can show you. I cannot turn it." Sources: new.
- **S01-5.3 CU.** L looking at the lattice, not at Jet, not at the lens; the first time his face is lit by something he was given. Sources: face lock + new.

## Scene 6 — The clock (C09 sandstorm-wall)
- **S01-6.1 WIDE.** The two walking back toward the cliff, the storm wall brown on the horizon behind them (screen-right); the cube folded. Light: the sun ahead of them, the storm's shadow behind. One motivated move: a slow track with them at their pace. Sources: C09 01 to 04, 07, 08; Jet new.
- **S01-6.2 MED.** L turns to the wall, says the time (two hours), and starts to run; Jet does not run. The one shot where the two part in tempo. Sources: as above.

## Scene 7 — The vault, again (C18; the set piece; score song MD-LAG-VAULT-002)
- **S01-7.1 WIDE.** L down the ladder with Jet behind him in the doorway; the line parts; the Keepers at the pump. Light: the dim lamps; Jet's sphere the only cold light. Sources: C18 picks; Keepers and Jet pending.
- **S01-7.2 MED.** The oldest Keeper: "The last man who opened that scoop killed three of us." L: "One of the three was my mother." (dialogue shot; lip-sync is a later gate; the skeleton holds the beat). Sources: C18; Keeper pending.
- **S01-7.3 INS.** Hands clearing the choked line, grit to the elbow; the child's hand lamp as the key from screen-left (the child pending). Sources: C18; cue card event 3.
- **S01-7.4 3QL.** The seized valve freed with the thumper's iron twin from the rack; the lattice's light on the iron; hands and iron, the face not needed (cue card event 4; hand-to-object contact: a later run). Sources: C18; the LAG-COV-02 3QL slot.
- **S01-7.5 LOW.** The climb to the scoop from below; the lattice above him turning; the shaft dark. Sources: C18 18, 19.
- **S01-7.6 MED.** The shoulder to the door that has not moved in forty years; the door moves. The build's peak (the cue card: not the release). Sources: new.
- **S01-7.7 WIDE.** The storm hits the cliff like a wave (exterior cut-away). Sources: C09.
- **S01-7.8 WIDE, the release.** The vault breathes; the lamps come up; the water comes up. The cue lands here, on the breath and the lamps. Sources: C18 14 (best).
- **S01-7.9 CU.** Jet in the doorway, both hands at his sides; the gloved one empty when the Keeper looks at it. Sources: Jet new.
- **S01-7.10 CU.** The oldest Keeper looks up at the lattice, still there, lit by it from above; the understanding, late and complete, as a state in a face that barely moves (the October 13 revision; the prompt names the state, never the emotion). Sources: C18; Keeper pending.

## Scene 8 — The fire (C31 tribe-gathering; C25 campfire-wasteland; the Panhandlers)
- **S01-8.1 WIDE.** The settlement at the fire with full cups; L opens the lattice over the fire; the camp lit from two sources (the fire warm, the lattice from above, its colour unrecorded). Angels at the edge not kneeling; Sassy with the cups; James at the fire (all three pending references). Sources: C31 03, 04, 09; C25 01 to 04, 10, 12; the campfire composition f59b02d5c59b as inspiration only.
- **S01-8.2 INS.** The child draws the valve in the sand with a finger and gets it right; the lattice's light on the sand. Sources: C25; child pending.
- **S01-8.3 MED.** Sassy asks about the second line; L does not know; the oldest Keeper does, and says so. Three faces, none to the lens. Sources: pending references.
- **S01-8.4 MED.** Jet at the edge of the firelight, the way he came to the dune: he is there. "They saw your lamps from the tower. Someone answered." Sources: Jet new.

## Scene 9 — The tower (C36 radio-tower-wastes; C24 night-desert-stars; C43 rig-rooftop-sentinel; score song, the tower)
- **S01-9.1 WIDE, night.** The dead radio tower on the ridge; L climbing; stars; the camp's glow below. Light: starlight, the camp's warmth from below. Sources: C36 04, 05, 09; C24.
- **S01-9.2 INS.** The key thrown; the relay's lamps; noise. Sources: C36.
- **S01-9.3 POV.** Far out on the dunes, a light blinking in the rhythm of his lamps (the reply; per Seed 09 and TIME_AND_THE_FALL, the settlement's own tower forty years on; the greeting in his own name, Episode 7's seed). Sources: C24 01, 03 to 07.
- **S01-9.4 WIDE.** Below, on the rig's roof, Jet watching the horizon, the cube turning by the gloved hand. Sources: C43 18, 03, 12; Jet new.
- **S01-9.5 INS, last frame.** Two hands: L's on the key, grit under the nails; Jet's, gloved, at his side. Sources: new.

## What this skeleton needs before any shot beyond scene 4 runs
Accepted references for Angels, Sassy, James (lettered), the Keepers, the child and Jet (the character-development pass); Ziggy's reading of Story 01; his IP call on the worm and the thumper beyond the first test (open item 8); the music direction for the two cue cards. Lisan-only shots in scenes 2, 3, 4 and 9 can run from existing frames once the rise and the signal have taught the route.
